# What changed

Newest first. One version number covers the desktop app, the phone app and
the backend files (the `VERSION` file). Builds made by GitHub add a build
number as the last part - `0.2.57` is a build of 0.2.

## Not in a numbered version yet

- **The Updates card's proof sentence is compact, and the 22:22 rulings are in the record (2026-11-21).** Gemini's rulings 5.1-5.6 of 2026-11-21 22:22 PT are applied. The one change a person sees is the Updates card: its `ROUTE:` sentence - the line the card renders verbatim - now reads `and the bounded checks above passed (9 of 9, 4 skipped - a subset, not the full suite)` instead of carrying the long trailing clause, and the full explanation stays in the transcript as the same run's `ALL DONE` line ("a subset, not the full suite") and skip note ("NOT counted as proven"). Ruling 5.1 fixes PM5's last open design question in the record: the executor's scheduler and step state lives in the existing `jarvis_tasks` SQLite store plus one `scheduler_tick` control row, never a second store and never a Rust-owned state file, and `docs/PM5-HUD-SCHEDULER-TICK.md` §7 now records that answer instead of asking for one (ruling 5.2's legacy-manifest fallback and corrupt-manifest refusal already ship in the update path, so nothing changed there; 5.5's "has not been tried on a real voice" stays because it is a measured limit of the shipped spotter; 5.6's fixed `2s`/`120s` phone poll stays a fixed contract, not a setting). Ruling 5.4's guide guard is recorded honestly as owed: there is no new-user-guide source in this repository to scan - the guide is built outside it and only the PDF exists - so the wake-copy guard's own docstring names the gap and what to add when the source lands, instead of claiming coverage it cannot have. The first live manifest closed the one open doubt an audit of its coverage claim had raised: measured on the owner's install (2026-11-21, deploy of `b611efd1a`) it holds **352 leaves**, `manifest_sha256 60c1082d3790`, and **all five** patched base files are listed - `jarvis_hud.py`, `jarvis_gate.py`, `jarvis_extract.py`, `jarvis_models.py`, `jarvis_skills.py` - each recorded sha256 matching the live file. So `docs/ONE-UPDATE-FOR-BOTH.md`'s "including the five patched base files" is true on a real deploy; a hermetic fixture without that delta lists four, so the docs now say "when this deploy manages them" and quote the measured install. The same audit found two claims that needed telling straighter: the manifest is written after the files are re-read and re-hashed (and after the route probes WHEN THIS RUN RUNS THEM - the in-app backend half is stopped and skips them for a stated reason, printed as "This is NOT a route pass"), not unconditionally "after the probes passed", and `read_deploy_manifest`'s "never raise" is now true for bytes that are not UTF-8 too (a `UnicodeDecodeError` is named as a corrupt marker instead of escaping to the caller), with both proved by `backend/test_reconcile_live_backend.py` (a skip-probes deploy writes and validates the manifest; a non-UTF-8 manifest is present-but-invalid with a reason). Tests: `backend/test_update_backend.py` (549 checks, 0 failed) pins the compact sentence, the long clause no longer being on the card, and the unchanged no-skip sentence; `backend/test_reconcile_live_backend.py` (all 888 checks passed) proves the manifest write path, including that a skip-probes deploy still writes and validates the manifest and that a non-UTF-8 manifest is present-but-invalid with a reason; `backend/test_api_doc.py` (173 checks, 0 skipped, 0 failed) proves the frozen section and the code agree; `node jarvis-desktop/tests/wake-copy.mjs` passes over 231 copy files with ruling 5.4's gap stated in its own docstring; and the updated docs quote the shipped sentence exactly.

- **The deploy route's proof sentence names checks skipped inside the suites (2026-11-21).** The 0.2.495 acceptance run's `ROUTE:` line said "the bounded checks above passed (9 of 9)" while 4 checks inside `test_reconcile_live_backend` were skipped for this PC (a skipped check is never counted as proven, and the PROOF lines and result already said so). The one sentence that names the proof now carries the count - "passed (9 of 9), with 4 check(s) inside those suites skipped for this PC and not counted as proven" - built by one pure `bounded_proof_phrase()` used by the deploy route, with both shapes pinned (test_update_backend 519 checks).
- **The preset contract reports the lane a preset was applied to, not the default lane (2026-11-21).** Measured on the owner's phone at ~20:24 PT: Brain → Focus said "General - Chosen - not running now" while General WAS running (`presets-choice.json` = `general`, `presets-active-lane.json` = 11450 with the General model resident), because `GET /api/work` answered `active_lane.key = "main"` / 11436. `jarvis_presets._active_lane_key()`, the `lane` block and `active_lane.base_url` were reading `_active_url()` - the DEFAULT lane (`jarvis_models.ollama_url_on_this_pc()`), never the applied one. They now read the persisted applied lane first (`_persisted_lane_url()`, loopback-only, the same file `jarvis_hud.active_ollama_url()` points a chat turn by) through a new `_chat_lane_url()` helper, and fall back to the default only when no applied lane exists; an applied lane on no preset port reports `key: null`, `ready: false` and the honest `why`, never a guessed key. `_active_url()` itself is unchanged for `reconcile_after_restart`'s "point chat back at the default" path. Read-only: no switching, no writes, no lane start. Five checks in `backend/test_presets.py` (three of them fail on the pre-fix tree), with `backend/jarvis_presets.py` and `jarvis-backend/jarvis_presets.py` kept byte-identical.
- **A preset keeps loading when the phone leaves the screen (2026-11-21).** Tapping a focus preset used to send the apply on the screen's own coroutine scope, so going to another menu or another part of the map cancelled the phone's half of the request while the PC kept loading the model: the row came back pressable, and the list could say "Chosen - not running now" over a model that was in fact being prepared. The press now runs in the app itself, the pressed row says "Being prepared" for as long as it lasts, and the phone re-reads `/api/work` every two seconds (for up to two minutes) until your PC reports the preset's own lane active - then it stops and the row says Current. If the PC is slower than that, the notice says it could not confirm and the row keeps the PC's own words; the apply is never posted a second time.
- **The Updates card is first where you look for it, says which half still needs finishing, shows the bounded proof's own step line, and Devices gets a dry-run-first clean-up (2026-11-21).** Four measured complaints and rulings from 2026-11-21 (the owner ~10:12 PT; Gemini's rulings 5.2, 5.4 and 5.6). (1) **Search.** Searching the update words in Settings put the Updates card last or hid it: "update"/"updates" already ranked first, but "upgrade" matched no card at all and "version" ranked About above it. A query made only of UPDATE_WORDS (`update`, `updates`, `upgrade`, `upgrades`, `upgraded`, `upgrading`, `updater`, `updaters`, `version`, `versions`, plus **`sync`** and **`mismatch`** - the two words the version handshake prints when the halves differ) - or the update phrases (`check now`, the card's own button name, and `check for update`/`check for updates`) - now pins the Updates card first in all three places the owner may have searched: the Settings page's filtered results (`settings-search.js`), the app-wide Find list built from the compiled menu catalogue (`palette.js`, which imports the same `asksForUpdates` rule so the boxes cannot disagree), and a one-row quick entry at the top of Settings that opens the card (`settings.html`/`settings.css`). The pin shows the card even when no words on it match ("upgrade"), and a query with any other word in it is left to the ordinary ranking, so no unrelated search is reordered. (2) **A banner at the top of Settings (ruling 5.4).** While the backend half is BEHIND, or a backend half is being finished right now, a banner above every card says so - naming both versions and linking "Go to Updates" - and it clears in place when a version read-back says IN SYNC: no reload, no restart. It re-reads the pair when the window comes back, when a run starts or ends, and on a slow beat while it is on screen; the card keeps its own handshake line underneath. It is deliberately not shown for a backend that is NEWER, two schemes that cannot be compared, or a backend that cannot be reached - "Update everything" is not what fixes any of those. (3) **The Updates card's own line is the release check AND the two versions.** Equal halves with a finished check read "Up to date." followed by the check's own line; a backend behind the desktop reads "Jarvis Desktop 0.2.492 is installed; the backend is 0.2.491 - press Update everything to finish the backend half." with the check's line appended, so a no-newer-release answer can never hide a behind backend; and a backend half that is running now reads "Finishing the backend half now. ... - the card updates when it ends." (the shell marks a live backend half in `update.rs`, and `backend_self.rs` carries it out as `VersionSync.running`). (4) **The bounded proof's own progress line (ruling 5.2).** While the app-path proof runs, the Updates card shows a clean phase-and-count line - `Step 3/4: Live invariants - 8 of 12…` - drawn from the runner's own `PROOF: Step N/M - <phase> - x of y` lines (`module imports` / `instant API answers` / `live invariants` / `look spec & config`). `update_progress.rs` carries only that exact shape (the proof stage's five-minute `PROOF: still running - ...` heartbeat and the older full sweep's suite lines are deliberately NOT steps), so the newest step always wins and a legacy full sweep keeps the card's current words instead of inventing a count. The 5-minute heartbeat and the 15-minute silence bound underneath are untouched: they still end a real hang, and the step line never replaces them. A run whose FILE half has already written VERSION while its own checks are unfinished never reads "Up to date." - it says the two halves are not claimed to match yet and that a restart's handshake will read IN SYNC (the 0.2.492 proof run, ended by the 3-hour ceiling at 20:32:11Z, is the measured case). (5) **Settings -> Devices: "Clean up duplicate/inactive devices" (ruling 5.6).** A new section offers one button; pressing it asks the PC what WOULD be removed and shows the names and how many days ago each was last seen. Anything active in the last 30 days is kept by the PC itself and is never offered, nothing is removed until the owner confirms, and the confirm ends in the PC's own `devices_cleanup` approval card (`POST /api/devices/cleanup`: dry run -> the would-remove list; confirm -> 202 while the card waits, 200 `{removed, kept}` after approval). The page never prunes on load, on a timer, or device by device; a stale link blocks the confirm (it ends in a card) but never the dry run (it only reads). The desktop door (`devices_cleanup` in `devices.rs`, its permission and the settings-surface entry) calls that route and passes 202 through as "waiting", not as a failure. "Both or neither" is untouched: no card, gate, route or approval changed, and the desktop half's install rules are exactly as they were.
- **The bounded proof runs its invariant suites staged, so a healthy update stops reporting 7 of 9 (2026-11-21).** The first real bounded run against the owner's installed build ended honestly but wrongly: "the deploy route carried the files, but the checks did not prove the update" - because `test_gate_egress` ("the row stores what is being asked about") and two `test_projects` taint checks compare the code they run with the words the repository's copy should carry, and the live folder is a PATCHED DEPLOYMENT. The three invariant suites now run staged from the update's own copy, exactly as CI runs them; the live folder is still proven by the deploy route's own bytes-and-markers check and by the checks that read it directly (compile + import every shipped module from it, its HUD answering three routes, its look spec, its config). Re-measured on the live install: **9 of 9**. `backend/test_update_backend.py` pins the staged shape with the measured reason (510 checks). An audit then hardened the same path: a suite that exits 0 having printed "N passed, M skipped" now carries its skip count and the ending says those checks are NOT counted as proven; an empty, non-JSON or non-commit `SOURCE-COMMIT` no longer selects the deploy route (the deploy tool never deletes its backup folders, so a stale one on its own is corroboration only, never evidence); a repository with no copies to compare now fails verification instead of passing it green; and a fallback `ROUTE:` line says "on this install" instead of the untrue "on a deployed install".
- **The phone's Done tap asks once when a linked PR is still open or its linked job is still running (2026-11-21).** Ruling 5.7 of the external review: instead of silently marking a work item Done or hard-blocking the owner, the tap on the phone's **Next 3 ready tasks** reads the plan answer it already has and, when that item's `linked_pr_state` is still open or the store's own job-to-status projection still shows the linked durable job running/waiting, shows ONE confirmation naming what is still live - "Linked PR #42 is still open - mark done anyway?", "The linked job is still running - mark done anyway?", or both in one sentence - with **Mark done anyway** and **Cancel** as its two buttons. Mark done anyway sends exactly the ONE status request the immediate tap would have sent (`POST /api/projects/<id>/work_items/<wid>/status`, `{"status":"done"}`, one event and one receipt as today); Cancel sends nothing and changes nothing; an unlinked item, a merged or closed PR, or a link whose state the PC has not read yet taps through immediately, so a missing link state never asks and nothing is invented. No route, card class, gate row or state is added: the warning is words over the plan read's own fields, the job's state is PM3's `TASK_STATE_TO_WORK` projection onto the item's status, and the words join the contract's `plan_words` (`tools/gen_projects_cases.py`). The phone's JVM `ProjectDoneWarningTest` (seven tests: the open-PR confirmation with nothing sent, the one confirming POST on the one route, Cancel sending nothing, the tap-through cases, the running/waiting job words, the contract's own words, and a source pin on the dialog) proves it, and `ProjectPlanTest` keeps the old 4,002-test suite green. Android half only, as the ruling names the PM4 phone surface; the desktop board's own card-detail move is unchanged. **One honest limit:** a linked job's state reaches the phone only as PM3's job-to-status projection, and a projected running/waiting item is never on the PC's ready list, so today the PR half is the one the phone's Done tap can show; the job words and their test stay for the non-ready row (or richer plan read) the ruling's sentence covers later.
- **The four PM4 project routes are frozen into the API contract and the parity classification (2026-11-21).** Gemini's ruling 5.3: `GET /api/projects/<id>/plan`, `POST /api/projects/<id>/work_items`, `POST /api/projects/<id>/work_items/<wid>/status` and `POST /api/projects/<id>/export` are implemented and live-verified on `main`, and both apps now depend on them, so they become contract rather than build notes. `docs/JARVIS-API.md` gains the stable frozen section §88.12 - the four routes in one at-a-glance table, every request and response key read from the real answer, the 200/400/404/405 status table, the export's 202/200 answers and the read-only/cardless/owner-direct statements - while §88.10 and §88.11 keep the build record and point at it. `tools/check_parity.py` keeps the shared three routes `ported` and the desktop-only export `deliberate`, with every reason naming §88.12 and the freeze. No route, schema or behaviour changed. The freeze exposed one sentence that contradicted the code and it is corrected: §88.10 said a work item had five states, which was the pre-PM3 count and never the store's seven. `backend/test_api_doc.py` now pins the frozen section's four routes, each key list, each status list and the two parity classifications against the real handler and the real classifier; every new check failed on the provisional tree first.
- **The device list can clean up duplicate or inactive devices - dry run first, one card, never automatic (2026-11-21).** Settings, Devices gets a "Clean up duplicate or inactive devices" action (Gemini's ruling 5.6): `POST /api/devices/cleanup {"dry_run": true}` answers 200 with the plan and writes nothing; `{"dry_run": false}` raises ONE `devices_cleanup` card at tier ask and answers 202 while it waits, and the first call after the owner's answer collects 200 with the counts. A device used in the last 30 days, the newest device on the list and the device making the request are never removed, a copy of the device list is written beside it before anything changes, and a removed device pairs again with the QR code. This pull request is the backend and card half; the Settings button is a separate lane, so `POST /api/devices/cleanup` ships classified `planned` in `tools/check_parity.py` and documented in JARVIS-API section 231.
- **The app's update proof is bounded, and a deploy-managed install is recognised before it starts (2026-11-21).** The in-app "Update everything" press and the automatic finish both run `tools/update_backend.py`, and both used to run the full ~48-65-minute CI suite list as their proof (measured 2026-11-21: the desktop's bound ended a healthy run at 48m 10s). The default proof is now a bounded post-update subset of 9 checks in 4 phases - `py_compile` + imports for every shipped module from the live folder, the live HUD's answers to `/api/version`, `/api/status` and `/api/presets`, the egress census, the gate/egress/reconcile/projects smoke suites, and look-spec + config agreement - reported as `PROOF: Step N/4 - <phase> - x of y` with the five-minute heartbeat kept for quiet stretches. The full sweep is a developer run only (`--full-proof`), and a bounded pass ends "proven by the bounded checks (9 of 9): a subset, not the full suite", never claiming the full check. The backend half's route is also detected up front: a deploy-managed install (evidence: `SOURCE-COMMIT` beside `VERSION`, and/or `_jarvis-deploy-backup-tool-*` backup folders) goes straight to `tools/reconcile_live_backend.py --apply`, skipping the measured 51-hunk patch-stack refusal, while a legacy patch-only install still starts with `scripts/apply-patches.ps1`; a deploy refusal is reported verbatim and "both or neither" is untouched.
- **The proof stage says it is alive, so the update's silence bound only ends a real hang (2026-11-21).** Measured on the owner's PC: the automatic finish for desktop 0.2.491 started at 07:07 PT, the deploy route carried the file half (`VERSION 0.2.491` at 07:11), delivered the look spec and recorded the everyday lane's model, and the run was ended at 07:55 PT - 48m 10s in - with *"The patch run was ended by the silence bound after 48m 10s (no new output arrived for 15m)"*. The backend half had genuinely succeeded (the restart logged *"Jarvis Desktop 0.2.491 and the backend 0.2.491 - IN SYNC"*) and the lane restore line worked (*"LANE: ... warmed the recorded qwen3.5:9b at 196608"*); the only fault was that one proof suite (`test_live_settings_parity.py` was one; the previous full run took ~48-57 minutes) prints nothing between suite boundaries, so "no output" was read as a stall. While the suites child is quiet, `tools/update_backend.py` now prints its own line at least every five minutes - *"PROOF: still running - 24m 05s elapsed, checking the backend against the live folder"* - and every real child line still flows through unchanged and restarts that clock. The app's 15-minute silence bound and 3-hour ceiling are unchanged: the silence stretch now means the heartbeat AND the child's output both stopped, a real hang, so a healthy proof stage can never be pre-empted by it. The honest ending is unchanged (marker == installed desktop -> the files and version are updated and a restart will read IN SYNC, never a claim of a match now; unchanged/unreadable -> exactly what the marker says), no card or gate changed, and "both or neither" is untouched. Tests on both sides drive injected clocks and scripted output: the heartbeat while a suite is silent, the bound firing only when the heartbeats stop too, the ceiling still firing, a slow-but-continuous run not ended, every ending's words, and `--restore-lane` still running on a heartbeat-era bound ending; a Rust test reads the tool's own `PROOF_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS` and pins it at least three times inside the Rust silence bound.
- **The phone's Projects screen shows the next 3 ready tasks, marks one Done, and takes a quick add (2026-11-21).** The Android companion gets the concise Projects surface the owner approved instead of a shrunken Kanban: the Projects list, the **Next 3 ready tasks** across projects (each naming its project), a Done tap for each, and a Quick Add box that saves the owner's typed words only - no date is invented, and nothing is a card. It reads one new additive route, `GET /api/projects/<id>/plan` (objective, milestones with progress, work items, the store's own ready order, newest events), and its two taps use the plan store's existing doors through two thin routes: the status change goes through `set_work_item_status` (one event, one `jarvis_undo` receipt), and Quick Add through `add_work_item`. The readout and the spoken summary are capped at 3 - the same cap the deterministic "what should I work on next?" answer and the morning brief keep - so the screen and the voice can never disagree about how long the list is; the desktop's PM4 page reads the same plan route. `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 88.10 documents all three routes, `backend/test_projects.py` proves them against a real store, and the phone's JVM `ProjectPlanTest` proves the cap, the project name on each row, one request per tap, the exact-words Quick Add, the honest empty/error states and the spoken cap against the generated contract answers.
- **A release's new tools reach the owner's own config, additively (2026-11-21).** PM2 shipped its eight project tools **ON in the published config** and deploy #5 carried every module - but the owner's live `jarvis-framework.toml` still listed 29 tools and none of the eight, so `enabled_tools_for_turn()` was 29 and the model was never offered a single project tool (measured: all eight `enabled=False offered=False`). The deploy never touches that file **on purpose** - it holds the owner's vault path, bind address and every switch they chose - so what was missing was the explicit step between the two. `tools/enable_new_tools.py` is that step: it adds only the names it is given (`--add`), refuses a name that is not a real tool, is a dry run unless `--apply`, backs the file up first, writes only the `[tools] enabled` array and proves every other line is unchanged; a second run is a no-op. **Measured on the owner's PC after the first apply:** enabled 29 -> **37**, all eight `enabled=True offered=True`.
- **The update's bound now measures progress, every ending re-reads the two versions, and the release's look spec goes with the file half (2026-11-21).** Measured on the owner's PC, 2026-11-21: the automatic backend finish started at **11:08:54Z** because Desktop 0.2.488 was ahead of backend 0.2.487; the deploy route carried the backend half and wrote `VERSION 0.2.488` and `SOURCE-COMMIT d7003442e`, so the halves were genuinely equal; the proof stage (`backend/run_suites.py` against the live folder, Balanced/14 workers) then legitimately took **~57+ minutes**; and at **12:08:54Z, exactly 60 minutes after the start**, a single one-hour wall clock killed the healthy run and said "The backend half is the one that did not finish. The backend is still 0.2.487" - both false by then, the backend read 0.2.488, and a restart logged "Jarvis Desktop 0.2.488 and the backend 0.2.488 – IN SYNC." The look spec was never delivered by the run either. The bound now measures progress: new output resets the clock, a 15-minute silence stretch ends it honestly, and a three-hour hard ceiling sits well above the measured worst case; the words name which bound ended it and after how long, for both the automatic finish and an "Update everything" press, which run the same runner. On every ending the two versions are re-read: when `<backend>/VERSION` equals the installed desktop's version the line says the backend's files and version ARE updated, that the full check did not finish, and that restarting Jarvis will read IN SYNC (the marker is not claimed as IN SYNC itself - only a restart's own handshake may say that); a run that wrote nothing says what its marker still reads, and an unreadable marker is never guessed. `tools/update_backend.py` now delivers the release's look spec as soon as the deploy's bytes+markers proof has passed, before the proof suites, so a suite phase that runs long cannot leave the owner with the old spec and a "the look spec DISAGREES" warning; the `BESIDE:` line is part of the run report (read from the whole output, not the last-60-lines tail), and the release's new tool defaults still wait for the full proof. "Both or neither" is unchanged: a deploy that did not prove its bytes or markers claims nothing and delivers no spec.
 The same run left the owner's everyday model lane switched: the proof suites load a different model on lane 11436 without putting the owner's back (jarvis-primary:latest at 16,384 instead of the preset table's qwen3.5:9b at 196,608, and the field battery's PRESETS row then failed). So the suites are bracketed: before they start the tool reads the lane's resident model+context from GET /api/ps on OLLAMA_URL (loopback only) and records it in the backend's _jarvis-logs folder, and after them it warms the recorded model at the recorded context when the suites left a different one - never a model or context it did not read. One LANE: line says restored / left alone / unreadable-and-nothing-restored. Because the desktop owns the run's bound and can kill the tool mid-suite, the record is what makes every ending safe: after any ending the app runs the tool's own --restore-lane mode from it, and the record is removed once the lane is back (or by that one retry) so a stale record can never override a model the owner picks later. A failed restore or a failed read is reported honestly and never guessed at.

- **A pending check is not a failure (2026-11-20).** The external review's ruling 5.2, from the owner's deploy #4: *"What is failing on pull request 1424?"* was answered "GitHub reports no check runs on pull request #1424 … 2 CI runs are on the head commit and at least one did not finish successfully. 2 failing check(s): CI: pending Jarvis client: pending" while `gh pr checks 1424` showed both checks **pending**. Cause: `_ci_words` treated every workflow run whose conclusion was not in the pass set as red, and a queued/in-progress run has `conclusion: None` - so an unfinished run was counted as a failure and labelled with its own status under a "failing check(s)" headline. `jarvis_github.py` now splits a pull request's head-commit runs with the same three-way judgement `_check_verdict` uses for checks (`_run_verdict`: completed + pass is fine, completed + anything else **failed**, anything not completed **pending**), and the answer groups them honestly: only completed non-pass runs are called failed, a commit whose checks are green but whose runs are still going says the runs are still going, and with no check runs and only pending runs it says "N CI run(s) are still going: names. Nothing is known about them yet - ask again when they finish." The failing headline counts only FAILED runs and says "failed" - never "did not finish successfully". The pull request form also reads the PR head's **commit statuses** (`GET /commits/{sha}/status`) after its three planned reads and merges them into the check list as check-run-shaped entries (`context` → name, success → completed/success, failure/error → completed/failure, pending → in_progress), so the answer is the combined set `gh pr checks` shows; a statuses read that fails is not fatal and the answer says the list is check-runs only. The plan keeps its THREE steps (the pull form's detection reads `steps[-1]`, the check-runs read) - the statuses read happens in `_ci_result`. `tools/field_battery.py` now tolerates `gh pr checks`' exit 8 (checks pending - the pending ground truth used to be thrown away as an error), asks for `--json name,bucket,state`, picks a **settled** pull request for the failing question (a failed check and no pending one) and a pending-but-not-failed one for the running question, counts a number only as its own number (the old substring test read the `1` in "#1400" as "1 failed check"), and never accepts "failed" for the running question. `backend/test_github_ci_count.py` (52 checks, rewritten: the still-going expectation now expects the pending sentence, with new cases for all-pending, failed+pending grouped separately, a status context judged with the checks, a pending status, an unreadable statuses read, and the plan's three steps), `backend/test_github_robustness.py`, `backend/test_github_own_repo.py`, `backend/test_github_tools.py` and `backend/test_field_battery.py` (self-test 30 → 37 cases) prove it; the twin `jarvis-backend/jarvis_github.py` is byte-identical; `test_base_matches_repo.py` 140, `test_base_regeneration.py` 39, `check_stale_twins`, `check_parity`, `check_no_source_pins` and `check_position_pins` clean.

That is not a finding that nothing exists."), and only a search that really ran produces the Redundancy Matrix. - **The patched-base file can be refreshed, and the two hand shims on the live `jarvis_models.py` are replaced by the published base's own definitions (2026-11-19).** The review ruling made the shims temporary debt to clear and said no third shim may be added; the deploy's cross-file guard (#1400) stays absolute and this tool is the clean path it points at. `tools/refresh_patched_base.py` is dry-run by default and writes ONE file at a time with `--apply --file <name>`. It refuses unless it can prove the target's bytes are exactly an older published base version from `jarvis-backend/<file>`'s own history (optionally plus the `$PATCHES` entries that write it, replayed in stack order), or that version plus a contiguous suffix of module-level gap-repair definitions - the hand-shim shape, accepted only when every name it binds is absent from the published bytes and bound by the current base, and only when the suffix contains definitions and no running code. A patch that was rewritten after the base version was published is recognised through `backend/patch-history`'s recorded older version (`gpu-offload.patch` is the real case), so an old shape is not mistaken for an unknown edit. The new file is the current published base plus any patch the target carries that the base does not yet; the tool refuses rather than writes if that would lose a module-level name, drop a patch the base cannot take, fail to bind one of the deploy's declared cross-file names, or not compile. On a copy of the owner's live folder (read-only, no `--apply`) the check proves `jarvis_models.py` is the 2026-10-06 published base plus the 3 appended shim definitions, and reports that refreshing it replaces `ollama_url_on_this_pc`, `is_pooled_model` and `probe_refusal` with the base's own, adds 11 module-level names and loses none; the deploy's cross-file guard passes on the refreshed file and still refuses when `probe_refusal` is taken back out. `backend/test_patched_base_refresh.py` proves all of it on temporary fixtures, including a real temporary git repository, and `docs/DEPLOY.md` section 2b documents the command, the refusals and the exit codes. The deploy itself is unchanged: it still never carries a patched-base file.

The row now names **`huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:30b-a3b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M`** (30.5B parameters, a mixture of experts) on the **pooled three-card lane at 32,768 tokens** - 19.520 GiB loaded ENTIRELY in the cards' memory (0.000 GiB spilled), a 55.1-66.3 s cold load and **about 21 tok/s - the median of three separate loads on a PC with no test load on 2026-11-19, published WITH its spread** - against the 27B's 9.04-13.05 under the same protocol. **Ruling 5.4** fixed how that speed is published: a 3-run median from a quiet PC, never a noisy busy-PC figure. Its blind eight-task quality is **20/24 - a TIE** with the 27B - and it emitted **22/22 correct tool calls** against the 27B's 18/19: the 27B dropped the pin on the two-effect squats sentence, and this model emits both effects. The row says the trade honestly rather than selling the win: **2.1 GiB more resident memory**, a ~10 s slower cold load, **no 49,152-token zero-spill headroom** (49,152 measured 0.226 GiB spilled, so 32,768 is the largest proven window) and **no vision** (it reports completion, tools and thinking only), plus one extra unrequested note on the mood-log sentence. **The 27B is not deleted:** it stays downloaded on this PC as the pooled lane's `creative` mode model and the smaller-footprint alternative, but no preset names it now. `muse-glimmer-uncensored:30b` is still described rather than chosen because it has NOT been benchmarked on this PC, and the one still-unmeasured MoE candidate (`TrevorJS/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-uncensored`) is named as future-only with no figure. - **The cloud answer is bounded, not truncated, and a coding turn that failed locally twice gets a third chance at the cloud (2026-11-19).** Two external-review rulings, each measured before it was written. **6.5 - bound the answer, do not truncate it.** One escalated turn on this PC cost $0.002747-$0.0039 and was almost all output (2,152 completion tokens against 84 prompt - about 99% of the bill), so a cost per turn is a length control; a truncated hard answer costs more than the tokens it saves, because the owner asks again. `jarvis_chatbot_api.cloud_request_body()` is now the ONE composer of a cloud request's messages and `max_tokens`: it sends `CLOUD_CONCISE_INSTRUCTION` as the request's single system message in front of the owner's newest turn (only user turns are ever carried, so the privacy cut is unchanged), and it bounds `max_tokens` to 4,096 for a standard escalation and 8,192 for a coding or deep-analysis one - generous next to the 2,152 the measured turn wrote. The tier is the existing signal, not a new classifier: the router's own 0-1 complexity score at 0.70 (its 0.40 escalation threshold is Stage 1) plus `jarvis_router.is_coding_turn()`, which reads the Coding preset's own trigger words, a coder model's name, or the caller's tool-in-play answer. The bound can only LOWER what `cloud_request_cap()` already priced for the month (a reasoning-inside DeepSeek lane was being sent cap + reasoning room, up to 16,000; now `cloud_request_cap` honours a `max_tokens_ceiling` the composer records, so the relay's own cap call can never re-inflate it). It is wired where every escalation is built - `_open` in the HUD relay, through `ollama-direct.patch`, so every hop of the degrade loop gets it, not one caller - and `backend/test_cloud_answer_bound.py` (29 checks) asserts the composed request body at runtime: 4,096 standard, 8,192 coding/deep, the instruction present on every cloud escalation and absent from a local one, money can only lower the bound, and the earlier-turn privacy cut still holds. **6.1 - a 2-strike fallback for coding tasks.** The deterministic `complexity >= 0.40` pre-gate is kept as Stage 1 and PAIRED with `jarvis_router.note_local_failure(conversation)` / `local_failure_strikes()`: after TWO local failures in the SAME conversation, a CODING turn may pass the complexity stage even under 0.40 - because two failures are direct evidence the local model cannot answer it - and it still runs every safety gate in the same order (cloud-model, no-lane, Lockdown, taint, image, file, screen, private, pasted secret, budget) and still needs the owner's yes or this PC's standing switch at gate 6. One failure does not fire it, a non-coding turn never does, and a private turn with two failures still answers on this PC. The count is keyed by conversation id so a new conversation starts at zero by construction, `reset_local_failures()` forgets one explicitly, the store is bounded to 128 conversations and holds counts only. `backend/test_router_strikes.py` (35 checks) proves the third attempt escalates, the two controls stay local, every one of the ten gates answers the same with and without two strikes, the count resets and is bounded, and that a twice-failed turn with no yes is still only an OFFER. **Deliberate scope:** the 6.1 router API has no HUD caller yet (recording a local failure needs the relay's failure points, a separate change), and the 6.5 patch line reaches a fresh install through `apply-patches.ps1`; the owner's already-deployed HUD needs the usual deploy step (`tools/reconcile_live_backend.py` was outside this change's brief). `backend/test_patch_delta_coverage.py` 22, `test_reconcile_live_backend.py` 842, `test_ollama_direct.py` 10/6 skipped, `test_reasoning_fallback.py` 54, `test_cloud_escalate_setting.py` 130, `test_cloud_say_yes.py` 73, `test_cloud_lane_taint.py` 127, `test_router_private_terms.py` 181, `test_cloud_degrade_chain.py` 32, `test_attached_file.py` 227, `test_no_source_pins.py` 5, `test_patch_history.py` 32, `test_base_matches_repo.py` 140, `test_base_regeneration.py` 39, `tools/check_stale_twins.py` and `tools/check_parity.py` are all clean.

- **The tool diet can no longer hide a tool the owner's own words name (2026-11-18).** The 17:57Z live battery asked eight real questions about the owner's own GitHub repository through `/api/chat`; "What is the latest commit on main in Epic-Jarvis?" was shown only `web_search` and `feature_guide` - every GitHub tool was dieted away, so the model could not call one and answered "I don't have direct access to your GitHub repositories", a false denial of an ability this backend has. It adds only card-free reads (never a write tool on its own), it is bounded by the owner's enabled list, and it touches no gate, no tier and no configuration: `check_call` still reads the allowed list, so a hidden tool can still be called and every GitHub write still raises its own card. `feature_guide`'s `is the ... on` hint was also anchored to the end of the sentence - it had matched its own words inside the commit question by accident. #1382 merged before this branch and gave two tools the words `commit` and `defect`, so on today's `main` the false-denial question is shown a GitHub tool again; what the floor still fixes is the class: nothing in any hint knows the owner's repository by NAME, and "branches" matched no hint (that question got a 29-tool full-list fallback). - **A test suite or probe can no longer write the owner's live money or model state (2026-11-18).** The review's ruling after a lane briefly wrote `~/.openjarvis/` while probing - it turned the standing escalation switch off and lowered the money cap to $5, then restored both - asked for a fail-fast guard, not only a harness rule. `jarvis_framework` now carries that guard: when `JARVIS_SUITE_RUNNING` is set - the marker `backend/_where.py` already sets for every suite, not a second mechanism - and a target resolves inside the owner's real `~/.openjarvis`, `refuse_live_config_write(path)` raises `LiveConfigWriteRefused`, in plain words naming the file, saying nothing was written, and saying a suite must pass a temporary `--config-dir` / `OPENJARVIS_CONFIG_DIR`. It is wired into the writers this branch owns: the monthly money cap and spending file (`jarvis_chatbot_api._save`, `chatbot/api-money.json`) and the current-model record (`jarvis_models`, `model-state.json`). A temporary settings folder still writes normally, and without the marker the owner's card-approved flow is unchanged; reads are untouched, so a test can still read the live settings and ledger. Honest limit, recorded in the decision entry: the escalation switch and cloud choice are written only by `jarvis_presets.py`, which this lane's brief puts out of scope, so those two writers are a small follow-up for its owner - the guard already refuses both live paths by name. Proved by `backend/test_live_config_write_guard.py`: 50 checks across the refusal (naming every live settings file, nothing created or changed), the temporary-folder write, the no-marker owner flow (including the untouched preset writer), and a live read.
- **A recording can be attached in the phone's chat - the owner's `.m4a` voice memo now attaches, and the PC transcribes it (2026-11-18).** The chat "Attach a file" row offered only the eight document types while `jarvis_media_read` already read eight audio formats, so the picker was narrower than the PC's capability: the row now offers `.wav .mp3 .m4a .aac .flac .ogg .opus .wma` (with `audio/x-m4a` beside `audio/mp4`, and the extension decides before any provider type, so a picker that reports `application/octet-stream` for an `.m4a` still attaches it), and `jarvis_attached_file` sends those bytes to that same local reader - transcribed on the PC, never on the phone and never sent anywhere - with its own sentences passed through unchanged, so a PC with no ffmpeg still answers `NO_FFMPEG` in exactly the existing words. A WAV is decoded in memory; a compressed recording is decoded through ONE private temp copy removed before the read returns. Fixed on the way: `jarvis_media_read`'s `if not samples:` raised `ValueError` on the numpy array the real decoder returns, so every REAL recording - and every real WAV - answered "could not be read"; and a recording never takes the picture path. Tests: `backend/test_media_read.py` (the bytes door, `.m4a`/`.mp4` names, a real `.m4a` decode where ffmpeg exists, the copy removed), `backend/test_attached_file.py` (all eight extensions route to the one audio reader, its refusals verbatim, a real WAV end to end), `AttachFileTest.kt` (the picker carries the audio types and `.m4a` resolves from the extension alone). The desktop attach row deliberately keeps its document-only list - ARCHITECTURE section 8 and JARVIS-API section 163.6 say why.
- **A preset switch can no longer load the pooled model on the everyday lane, and a preset no longer answers "applied" without reading the lane (2026-11-18, DEF-088).** Four faults made the A2 field test report success while port 11436 held the pooled `qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-ud-q3-k-xl` at 8,192 tokens with 3.76 GB spilled to the CPU, and each one is fixed with the traffic captured in a test rather than read for in the source. (1) `jarvis_presets._switch_for_the_owner` ran the tripwire smoke test on the **outgoing** model, through `jarvis_models._probe_asker`, against `jarvis_models.OLLAMA` - the everyday lane, one 12 GB card. It now asks `jarvis_models.probe_refusal` first, which is the existing `is_pooled_model` rule, so a pooled outgoing model is never sent there at all; the skip is reported as the tripwire's reason, so the app shows a sentence instead of a smoke test of nothing. (2) `_probe_asker` names `options.num_ctx` on every request **whose window can be established**, resolved by the new `jarvis_models.lane_num_ctx` from the lane's own configured window (`jarvis_big_coder.LANES`: 196,608 on 11436, 16,384 on 11435), from the applied pooled preset on 11450, or from what `/api/ps` says. Where the window cannot be established - an address this program does not know as a lane, which is what `OLLAMA_URL` unset (11434) means on a fresh clone and in CI - the request goes out WITHOUT the field rather than not going out at all, because a guard that silently stops the tripwire is worse than the gap it closes, and naming a guessed window would force a downgrade instead of leaving Ollama's own configured default in charge. (3) The carded `/api/models/switch` road had the same hole in `jarvis_models.switch_to`; its baseline and its after-swap probe now pass through the same guard. (4) `apply_preset` reads the lane back through `verify_lane` before it writes anything, and rolls back and reports the truth when the lane holds a different model, any spill, or the right model at a window smaller than the preset names - an EMPTY lane is not a failure, because the apply records which model chat should use and Ollama loads it on the next turn; a lane that does not answer is. That reader runs only in the real HUD process (`JARVIS_SUITE_RUNNING`, or `__main__` being `jarvis_hud.py` - the same test `_warm_on_startup` uses), because the first version of it read the owner's LIVE lane inside `backend/test_reversible_ui_choices.py`, which loads the base model steward directly and never sets the suite marker. The new `backend/test_preset_switch_lane_guard.py` drives the real apply against a fake lane on its own ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port and asserts, by capturing requests, that **zero** `/api/generate` requests name the pooled model at the everyday lane, that every probe whose window is known carries it, and that a lane holding the coder produces a failure rather than `ok`; the same suite drives `switch_to` and `_default_verify_lane` directly. On the unfixed modules it fails, and the carded road it drives sent 8 requests naming the pooled coder with no window.
- **Reflective Coach and Pictures & Screens now run on all three graphics cards (2026-11-18).** Two preset rows moved off the single 2060 card: Reflective Coach now applies `gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat` (measured 15.5 GiB, 0.68 GiB spilled, 52.0 s cold load, 49.26 tokens a second) and Pictures & Screens now applies `qwen3-vl:30b-a3b-instruct` (measured 19.88 GiB, 2.24 GiB spilled, 54.8 s cold load, 33.1 tokens a second), each on the on-demand pooled three-card lane at 32,768 tokens with its real 2026-11-09 receipt, never a re-estimate. Both are heavy rows: the everyday and Fast models are paused while they run and come back when another preset is applied. Picture quality for the new vision model is not measured, and nothing claims better answers. General and Fast deliberately stay on one card, because a pooled model's measured 31-55 s cold load and the paused everyday lane would make ordinary chat slower.
- **Pictures into ONE PDF, and one picture into another format (2026-11-18).** The `my_files` tool learns a `convert` action: one or more pictures become one PDF in the order given, or one picture becomes PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF or TIFF. Each conversion writes ONE new file and asks ONE approval card (its own action, `convert_images`, tier "ask"); a taken name gets a numbered sibling like `photo (2).pdf` and the card says so, a path the caller named that exists is refused, and the destination is opened with `O_EXCL` so nothing that exists can ever be replaced. The PDF half uses **img2pdf**, so a JPEG's own compressed bytes go into the PDF unchanged - the suite looks for the input bytes inside the output rather than trusting the claim - instead of Pillow's PDF writer, which re-encodes RGB through its JPEG encoder and defaults the page to 72 dpi. The picture half uses Pillow and tells the truth about quality: PNG and TIFF are lossless, JPEG/WebP/AVIF are **lossy** and the sentence says the copy is "not identical", and a picture with transparency saved as JPEG is flattened onto WHITE in those words. Sources are checked by sniffed content (a text file called `photo.png` is refused) and are never modified; the conversion runs in a bounded child program with a scrubbed environment. New dependencies `img2pdf` (LGPL-3.0) and `pikepdf` (MPL-2.0) are in `backend/requirements.txt` and the hash-pinned `backend/requirements.lock`, `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` gains those two credits plus the missing **FFmpeg** one (required, never bundled), and the feature is rowed in `features/features.json`. Honest limits: HEIC is not read, a PDF's page size follows each picture's own DPI, and this is chat-only (no new route, so both apps can ask).
- **Pictures & Screens now loads with nothing spilled: a 12B vision model on the pooled lane (2026-11-18).** The row first named the 30B `qwen3-vl:30b-a3b-instruct`, and measured on this PC's real pooled lane on 2026-11-18 it loaded **19.88 GiB with 2.24 GiB spilled into system memory** - and it still spilled **1.65 GiB at 16,384 tokens** while the three cards had 8.6 GiB free, so the spill is the model's own split and no smaller window fixes it. The row now applies **`gemma4:12b-it-qat`** at the same 32,768-token window on the same all-three-card lane: **8.70 GiB resident, ALL of it in the cards' memory (0 B spilled)**, a 20.3 s cold load and 28.1 tokens a second (the 30B measured 14.6-25.4 the day before). The measured picture test comes out the same way - it read a generated picture's words and shapes and a generated settings screenshot's Save button, server address and red banner exactly as the 30B did - and its general quality is the project's own blind eight-task battery's 21/24 (2026-11-17). Its own `worse` line says plainly what is NOT measured: picture quality has no scoring battery, so that is a reading test, not a score against other models. The pooled mode row now carries a **0 B spill allowance**, so the apply's lane read-back refuses any spill for this preset instead of accepting the 2.24 GiB the replaced model measured; the 26B rows keep their own measured 0.68 GiB allowance, which is what those rows measured. The bench's last promotion pair (`general_12b`, whose candidate was this 12B) is retired with the move - a pair whose candidate is already a shipped preset model is a dead row in the packet, not a pending promotion - so `jarvis_bench.PROMOTION_PAIRS` is empty and the promotion machinery stays tested on a fixture row. - **The phone's Help, preset and model screens stop promising things the app does not do (2026-11-18).** A wording audit of `jarvis-client` found seven genuinely misleading strings; all seven are fixed here. Help no longer tells the owner a notification has "never an Approve button" - it has offered Deny, Approve and Review in Atlas since the owner's 2026-11-02 ask (`service/ApprovalNotificationPolicy.kt`; every Approve requires an unlocked phone, a small read-only card can be settled by the tap, and App lock or hidden lists replace Approve with Review in Atlas) - and no longer says the app "never downloads or installs anything": Platform checks' This app card has Download update / Install update, checksum- and signature-pinned, and nothing downloads until Download is pressed. The on-device answer now names the optional Local AI chat (More, then Local AI) instead of denying it, and the About card says the same. The preset plate no longer says "Picking one that is not Coding or Medical switches at once; Coding and Medical raise one approval card" - both halves were false: every local preset click has applied with no card since 2026-11-16, and an apply stops the old model or lane and may start the three-card lane. It now says the change applies straight away with no approval card, gives the measured cold-load range (about 12 seconds to about a minute), and says a heavy preset fills all three cards while its own row says what that costs. The apply notice no longer claims "Preset applied. Your PC switched its chat lane; nothing else changed." from an HTTP 200 alone: the PC's apply body carries no sentence of its own, so the fallback now says the PC answered and the list is being re-read to show what is in use. The Brain's model plate no longer promises a "six to ten second" switch and the power helper no longer promises "5-15 seconds" after standby: both now say the measured cold load (about 12 seconds for the smallest model, about 50 seconds for the 26B, about a minute at worst), taken from the 2026-11-17 measurement on this PC. Under the owner's new naming rule the strings edited here that named the assistant "Jarvis" now say Atlas (the About heading and body, and the notification, update and Local AI answers); wake-phrase copy is untouched on purpose, because the shipped spotter (`hey_jarvis_v0.1.onnx`) cannot hear "Hey Atlas" - the owner's own recording peaked at 0.1744 with zero frames at the 0.5 threshold - so it moves when the new keyword model exists. The PC side stays deferred: `backend/jarvis_presets.py` (the preset sentences, in PR #1361's diff) and the older-PC `HEAVY_COST` fallback at `net/FocusPresets.kt:93-97`, which #1361's newest commit is already rewriting. Tests: `SendFileTest` now pins the model plate's no-card fact ("switches with no approval card") instead of the removed "switches at once" (the audit found "at once" misleading); `TouchTargetAndInsetsTest`'s two FaqScreen windows moved 522/551 -> 541/570 because the answers above them grew; `FocusPresetsTest`'s apply-answer pin now holds the new honest fallback. The phone's `testDebugUnitTest` suite is green (3,965 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped); the phone screen itself was not driven, so the notification's Approve/Review behaviour and a preset click's effect are proved from the code and the JVM tests, not from a device.

On the phone the Brain is ONE scroll with seven headings and no tabs, and those Settings cards are Brain plates there, so the same words now carry both places in one sentence - "PC: Brain, Work, Today. Phone: Brain, Money and time, Today." - and say plainly when the phone has no screen for something (`import-chats`) rather than inventing one. Three rows whose `surface` said `desktop` while the phone really draws the feature are now `both` (`reminder-actions`, `email-drafts`, `chatbot-money` - the phone can answer that card and read the chatbot spend while the keys and limits stay the PC's), and `read-aloud`, `find-phone`, `memory-known` and `calendar` now name the phone's real path (its own chat words, either app's chat, its same-named Brain heading, either app's chat) instead of implying a screen it does not have. A new rule 10 in `tools/check_feature_list.py` fails a `both` row that names a PC Brain tab and never the phone - it flags exactly the audit's 32 rows on the previous tree and none on this one, and `backend/test_feature_list.py` holds the five rows the audit ranked most likely to `BrainSections.kt`'s real headings and to the phone's Settings screen not having the sections they used to name.
- **The phone can ask Jarvis to update itself, and ONE card decides (2026-11-18).** The owner's ask: "the desktop program can update itself, but only at the PC, and only after Windows Hello there. I want the phone to be able to ask for that same update, with the phone's own fingerprint." Two routes (`GET /api/update/status`, `POST /api/update/request`) raise the SAME card the chat already raises - action `desktop_update`, tier "ask" - through the gate; nothing is downloaded, installed or changed before the owner's yes, and the request body cannot carry a command, a path or a version. The card is answered on the PC with Windows Hello as before, and now also on the phone with that phone's own fingerprint or PIN over a one-use challenge (`desktop_update` left `PC_ONLY_ACTIONS`, exactly as `raise_api_limit` did on 2026-10-11). After a phone's yes the PC runs `scripts/update-jarvis.ps1` in a detached helper that holds the shared `update-in-progress.lock`, so the desktop's own updater and this one cannot patch the machine at once. The phone's own screen for it is the next lane, recorded in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 as one-sided on purpose for now, and no real phone has driven the card yet - that field test is owed and JARVIS-API section 226.5 says so.
- **A package install can no longer scatter its temporary folders into the repository, and a checker now finds the folders if one does (2026-11-18).** On 2026-11-18 a delegated agent ran `pip` with the repository root as its working directory and TMP/TEMP inside the tree; pip left seventeen `pip-metadata-*` and `pip-unpack-*` folders at the root, untracked and one `git add -A` from being committed, until somebody noticed by accident. Two guards close it. `tools/check_package_install_context.py` refuses a `pip` OR `uv` install whose working directory is the repository root or whose TMP/TEMP (or `PIP_CACHE_DIR` / `UV_CACHE_DIR`, `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `UV_TOOL_DIR`) resolves inside the repository, naming the offending folder and saying "run the install from a scratch directory, or set TMP/TEMP outside the repo"; a context it cannot judge - an unknown manager, a platform that is neither Windows nor POSIX - prints "not checked: <why>" and exits 3, never passing. `--run -- <command>` wraps an install and refuses before the command starts; the audit job runs the guard immediately before its own `python3 -m pip install` step as a preflight, so the job cannot install after a working directory or TMP regression. `tools/check_package_manager_temp_artifacts.py` is the second half: it fails on a tracked or untracked top-level path matching pip's temp folders, a root `*.dist-info` or a TRACKED root `node_modules`, names every path and prints the `Remove-Item` / `rm -rf` / `git rm -r --cached` commands that remove it, and does not fire on a `pip-*` name inside a test fixture, under the ignored `.dsh-scratch/` or on an untracked `node_modules` (`.gitignore` line 36 already covers it). `backend/test_package_install_guards.py` (71 checks) proves both can fail on a real fixture repository it makes and removes, that the refusals carry the folder and the fix, that the wrapper never runs a refused command, and that both are clean on this tree; both guards are wired into the `audit` job.
- **Every shipped module asks the one lane resolver for its Ollama address (2026-11-18).** PR #1330 made `OLLAMA_URL` a checked value in `jarvis_models.ollama_url_on_this_pc()`, but it routed only the three reads its own commit touched; the review of that merge counted about fifteen shipped modules still reading `OLLAMA_URL` - or Ollama's own `OLLAMA_HOST` - straight out of the environment, so whichever port a lane task happened to export (or none, on 11434) decided where a health probe, a quiz, a hardware read or the personality draft asked. Seventeen modules and eighteen reads now go through the helper, with 11434 kept as the explicit fallback wherever it already was and the everyday lane's port (11436) used whenever `OLLAMA_URL` names it. The published base's direct reads fell from 20 to 2: the helper itself, and `jarvis_ollama_contract.py`, left on purpose because its own suite pins that read-only probe to the standard library. `backend/test_ollama_url_routing.py` proves each changed module returns the lane's port when `OLLAMA_URL` is set and this PC's loopback - not the remote address the variable names - when it is not, because the helper refused it; `backend/_where.py` gives a bare checkout a folder holding only `jarvis_models.py`, so the suites can import the modules that ask the helper without exposing the other owner files or importing anything before a suite has set its own config folder.
- **A card that cannot say what it would change no longer offers Approve - on the phone and in the desktop HUD - and a cloud settings card shows its detail again (2026-11-18).** The owner was shown a live `change_own_config` card asking to change his cloud settings that rendered with **no detail text** and a normal **Approve**: a blank cheque for a change nobody could read. The backend had sent the detail for both waiting cards; the phone dropped one on the way to the screen. `normalisePendingRow` (jarvis-client `net/PendingRows.kt`) derives the row's `summary` from the detail's first readable key and then **deleted `detail` when it "repeated" that summary** - and for the cloud provider card, `jarvis_presets.apply_cloud` sends exactly `{"text": …}`, a one-key object, so every key was the preview key and the detail was removed. The card never draws that derived `summary` either: `ApprovalCard` passes only `item.notice?.summary` / `notice.full` into `CardSummary.shown`, and those are built from the ACTION NAME (`jarvis_gate.notice_for`), so they can say "Jarvis wants to change one of its settings" but never which one. The sibling cloud card (the escalation switch, `{"text", "costs_money", "pid"}`) kept its detail because of its two extra keys - exactly the "drew one and not the other" the owner saw. Fixed at the cause: the read never drops a detail it can put in words, so the opened card says the actual change again. And the rule that makes the failure safe on both apps, in one place each: a card with **no readable detail** says *"Jarvis did not describe this change. Refresh, or deny it and ask again."*, draws a **Refresh** in Approve's place (a re-read; approves nothing), and keeps **Deny** - it never draws an empty body with a normal Approve. The same rule reaches the phone's **notification**: `ApprovalNotificationPolicy` offers **Review in Jarvis** there instead of an Approve for such a card, the shape a redacted card already had, so the lock screen is not the back door to the same blank cheque (the widget never offers Approve - it opens the app - so nothing changed there). The desktop HUD had its own version of the same hole (`apprDescribe` fell back to "(no detail)" and still offered Approve) and now draws the same rule. The sentence and the action are one shared copy for both apps (`backend/jarvis_card_words.py`'s `NO_DETAIL` / `REFRESH`, through `tools/gen_card_words_cases.py` into each app's contract fixture; the phone's `net/CardDetail.kt` and the HUD's copied constants read them), so the two screens cannot word the blank cheque differently. Nothing about what the backend sends, the gate, a tier or an approval route changed. Tests: `CardDetailTest` (10 new checks in jarvis-client; the measured provider row fails on the pre-fix tree with `item.detail == null`, the empty-detail shapes all expose Refresh and never Approve, and the composable's button row is pinned structurally because this project has no Compose UI test), `PendingRowsContractTest`'s command row now keeps its detail, `ApprovalNotificationPolicyTest` gains the by-notification check, `CardWordsContractTest` holds the new words to the PC's fixture, and the desktop's `tests/approvals-contract.mjs` + `tests/card-words.mjs` lift the HUD's own functions and drive the blank and described shapes, with `tests/csp-inline.mjs` still holding the three vendored HUD copies byte-identical.
- **A local turn can always answer: when the saved model cannot run on the lane it picked, the model that lane IS configured for answers instead (2026-11-18).** A private question on the owner's PC routed correctly to the local lane (`X-Jarvis-Route` gate `taint`, `where: local`) and then produced **no answer at all**: `model-state.json` said the everyday model was the Coding preset's pooled three-card model `qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-ud-q3-k-xl` (written by the live install's own preset apply - the repository half of that was merged as PR #1361 the same night), and `jarvis_agent.local_model_refusal` then refused, honestly and in the words the owner was shown, to load a pooled model on the one-card lane. Nothing left the PC and the privacy behaviour was right; the defect was that nothing had asked whether the model the router picked could run where it picked it. The fix has two halves that must ship together. `backend/rebuilt/jarvis_router.py`'s `choose()` now validates the chosen local model against the lane the turn will really use - the address asked for through `jarvis_models.ollama_url_on_this_pc()`, the one checked resolver #1360 puts every Ollama read behind, never a raw environment read - BEFORE the decision is returned, by asking the refusal authority itself (`jarvis_agent.local_model_refusal`; the "which models are pooled" predicate is not copied anywhere). When the saved model is the one class of refusal a different model can fix (a pooled model at a lane that may not hold it), the decision names **the model that lane is configured for** - read from `jarvis_big_coder.LANES` by port, else `[intelligence] default_model` in the owner's `config.toml`, else the everyday lane's own row - and carries the replacement in the route detail's existing `degraded_from` field: `{"lane": <asked for>, "model": <really used>, "code": "model_cannot_run_on_this_lane", "why": <the refusal>}`, with the reason naming both models. `degraded_from` is omitted on every ordinary turn, so no route header grows. The spill refusal itself is untouched: a pooled model on a one-card lane is still refused and never loaded. The second half is `backend/local-model-guard.patch` plus its line in `apply-patches.ps1` (one hunk in `jarvis_hud.py`, one rewritten line, immediately before `plugin-loader.patch`): the HUD decides "this is a local turn" as `lane == local_model`, so a router-only fallback made `use_tools` false and sent the turn to the plain cloud relay - which resolves a lane name it does not know through `jarvis_chatbot_api.lane_service()`, and an UNKNOWN name falls back to a **cloud provider** (`DEFAULT_LANE` is DeepSeek). Measured here: `lane_service("qwen3.5:9b")` answers `("deepseek_api", "deepseek-flash")`, so with a saved provider key a private prompt could have left the PC - rule 1 broken by a fix meant to protect it. The patch's one line is `use_tools = ((lane == local_model or decision.inject_memory) and _agent_ok)`: `inject_memory` is the signal because every local decision already carries it and no cloud decision ever does, and a new `Decision` flag would be a second thing to keep in step. A local turn whose model is fine is unchanged (absent `degraded_from`, exactly the same route detail), and a cloud turn is not pulled local. Tests: `backend/test_local_model_guard.py` (54 checks - the tainted turn answering with the lane's own model and passing the refusal `run_local_turn` would make; the pooled-model-on-one-card refusal still refusing; the ordinary turn's route detail keys unchanged; a cloud turn still escalating, even with a pooled saved model; the pooled lane unaffected; a cloud model named as local and a lane on another machine getting no substitute; the unknown-name cloud mapping; the patched HUD's own `use_tools`/`is_cloud` expressions evaluated for each case; and the patch applying and reversing on the stack's real pre-image). Also updated: the six suites that enumerate the patches written after theirs, `test_skill_scan_wiring`, `test_phone_app_allowlist`, the generated plugin catalogue, `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 228 and the `backend/README.md` section below. Not fixed here, and said so plainly: `jarvis_chatbot_api.lane_service()` mapping a name it does not know to a cloud provider is a second instance of the same disease, and it stays reachable from any caller that hands an arbitrary lane name to the plain relay; the narrowest safe change would be for the HUD's `_completions_url` to ask `lane_state` only for a lane in the caller's cloud-lane list, or for `lane_service` to answer nothing for an unknown name - both need their own measured change, not a quiet one inside this fix.
- **The lane launcher that decides a GPU lane's cards is now in the repository, checked against the live machine, and a lane table the machine cannot honour can no longer deploy or pass CI silently (2026-11-18).** On 2026-11-18 the worst confusion of the night was structural: the script that pins an Ollama lane's graphics card(s) lives at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\JarvisOllama\start-lane.ps1`, outside this repository, and two of its lines (`$env:CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES = $GpuUuid` and `OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS = '1'`) decide how every preset behaves. A pull request changed the repo's lane table to say the everyday lane on 11436 runs across all three cards; CI was green, and the machine could not do it - its logon task passes ONE `-GpuUuid`, and a measured load grew the RTX 2060 by 3,713 MiB and the other two cards by 0 MiB each. Now: `scripts/start-lane.ps1` is a tracked copy of the live launcher whose header says it is a copy, where the live file lives, and that editing it alone changes nothing on the machine, and whose TASK/GPU rows record the two logon tasks' exact `-GpuUuid` values and the three card UUIDs. `tools/check_lane_launcher.py` compares that copy with the live file and FAILS naming both paths, both line numbers and both differing lines (one changed character is enough); it also compares the tracked task table with Task Scheduler, the tracked cards with `nvidia-smi -L`, and the repo's `jarvis_presets.LANES` card claims with the cards the tracked tasks grant - printing "2-step deploy: update the lane task" with the exact task and the exact `-GpuUuid` value it should carry.
