The changes reuse the doors that already exist and add no route and no file writer: the service through `jarvis_presets.apply_cloud`, the switch through `jarvis_presets.cloud_escalate` (ON is ONE `change_own_config` card and writes nothing before the yes; OFF is instant and cardless, the existing rule), and the monthly cap through `jarvis_chatbot_limits.change` - the same door behind `POST /api/chatbot/money`, which is why the cap IS changeable from chat: an amount above today's cap raises ONE `raise_api_limit` card (tier ask, Windows Hello or the asking phone's own fingerprint) and writes nothing before the yes, while lowering it is cardless. A provider name the PC does not know is refused with the list read from `jarvis_chatbot_api.PRESETS`, never guessed at, and a known name keeps the older cloud-provider door so two doors never compete for one sentence. No key is read, shown or logged: the module never calls `key_saved` or Windows Credential Manager. Both apps need no client change - the answers and cards ride `/api/chat`. Tests: `backend/test_cloud_settings_chat.py` (99 checks over a temporary settings folder: every shape in every file state, the older doors keeping their sentences, the switch card writing nothing when denied, the cap card writing nothing when denied and the lowering cardless, the unknown-name refusal, and a runtime spy on the key store proving no answer reads it). Docs: `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 229.
- **A rate-limit or day-limit hit steps to a lane that exists, and the owner's stale `degrade_chain` is corrected on the next update (2026-11-18).** The owner's live `jarvis-framework.toml` still said `degrade_chain = ["jarvis-escalate", "jarvis-bulk", "jarvis-critic"]` months after the 2026-10-27 decision kept ONE cloud lane, because `scripts/apply-patches.ps1` never overwrites a line in an existing settings file. That was not only stale text: `jarvis_router.degrade()` returned the next name in the chain whatever it was, and `jarvis_chatbot_api.lane_service()` maps a name it does not know to the CHOSEN service - so one 429 walked the relay into two more real requests to the same provider under names that are not lanes, and the lane that finally answered was not in the caller's lane list so `jarvis_hud` did not count the call against the per-day budget either. `degrade()` now filters `[budget] degrade_chain` to names this module can serve - the lane(s) `cloud_lanes()` keeps from the caller's own list, plus the local model as the floor - and drops a name that does not exist (it was going to be refused by `cloud_lanes()` anyway), so a stale config can only ever push the turn one step closer to this PC. `backend/_apply_toml_tiers.py` (run by `apply-patches.ps1` on every update) now also repairs exactly one stale value - `[budget] degrade_chain`, and only when it names something that is neither in the shipped chain nor the configured local model - replacing that one line with the shipped chain, keeping every other byte, CRLF, comments and BOM, writing one backup first and refusing rather than guessing at an absent or multi-line value; `scripts/apply-patches.ps1` reports the correction as a real change. The repository's own `backend/rebuilt/jarvis-framework.toml` and its `jarvis-backend/` twin were already right since 2026-10-27 and are unchanged. The HUD page's offline demo graph no longer draws `jarvis-critic`/`jarvis-bulk` as "cloud lane · via proxy"; it draws the ONE lane with the service the owner chose (all three served copies of the page are byte-identical). Repro tests that fail on the pre-fix tree: `backend/test_cloud_degrade_chain.py` (32 checks - the live three-name chain stubbed, day-limit answered locally with gate "budget", the rate cap present with no budget file and binding once a call is recorded) and `backend/test_degrade_filter.py`'s new `t_a_rate_limited_turn_answers_on_this_pc` (the real `degrade()` with the stale chain must hop cloud -> this PC, not cloud -> "jarvis-bulk"). `backend/test_config_tiers_merge.py` proves the config repair (stale chain fixed; an empty chain, one naming the local model, or one split over lines left untouched). No new route, no new card, no auto-approval, and nothing may be sent anywhere it could not be sent before - every change here only refuses a destination that does not exist.
- **A claimed suite that passed nothing is no longer a pass (2026-11-18).** The claims register could still be fooled one way: `tools/check_claims.py` read the skips a suite PRINTS, so a suite that exited 0 having executed zero checks - a loop over an empty list, a guard that can never be true, a `main()` that returns before the first check - printed no skip to read and was indistinguishable from one that had verified the claim. It now holds `backend/run_suites.py`'s own zero-check rule, using the runner's own count parser (`run_suites.counts`, imported, not copied): a `test:` row is withheld when its suite exited 0 with `passed == 0`, and the failure names the suite, its counts and the two legitimate fixes - make the suite run a check, or record the environment skip with its reason and the date under `ENVIRONMENT_SKIPS`. That entry is the one exemption, and it needs the suite to have really printed the skip it covers: an entry records why a skip happened, it cannot document a skip that never happened. A printed skip is still never a pass, and a skip beside checks that really ran is unchanged. The plain register run now also reports how many checks the `test:` rows watched, so a green run cannot be read as one that watched nothing.
- **A feature question that quotes the row's exact name now reaches that row, never a neighbour that shares one word (2026-11-18).** The awareness audit's remaining 14 measured capability questions (166 of 180 after PR #1377) now all reach their own catalogue row: 180 of 180 with the harness tail removed, and 176 of 180 even with it kept (up from 136). Four of the 14 were answering the WRONG catalogue row, which is worse than no answer: "How much Jarvis may interrupt you" (attention-budget) was answered "Yes - Stop everything" because a safety pattern reads "interrupt you"; "Also on my phone" and "Open an app on your phone" (also-on-phone, phone-apps) were answered from call-recording because "called" stems to "call" and "call" + "phone" is that row's own name phrase "phone call"; "Jarvis starts the local model again by itself when it dies" (restart-the-model-lane) lost to start-the-model-lane's shared "start ... local model" words; and "asks me my saved study questions again on a schedule" (decks) lost to reminder-asks. The fix is one narrow lane in backend/jarvis_quick.py: when a question says "feature" and quotes a row's EXACT catalogue id, title or alias, that row answers it, before the limit lane, the reminder family, the goals lane, the feature guide and the read-a-link lane - the families that were winning on one shared word ("sound", "reminder", "ask", "ring", "read", "goal"). Exact equality only, never a shared word or a substring, so no other row's question is taken; the row that used to win each shared word keeps its own question, and the audit's three traps ("can you write a nice email for my boss?", "Can you send a file to my phone?", "Can you add 2 and 3?") still fall through exactly as before. An alias in features.json could not have fixed any of these 14 - each question already quotes the row's own exact name or alias, and an earlier family claimed the sentence before the catalogue lane ever ran - so this is a precedence fix, not a name fix. Measured with the real matcher (no model, no network): 166/180 -> 180/180 on the measured questions; a before/after sweep of every row's aliases, titles and id words in 35 ordinary question shapes (5,410 questions, both backend/ and jarvis-backend/) changed 53 answers, gained 47, and REGRESSED ZERO. Extended backend/test_capability_answers.py: a fixture per fixed question (row, its own what/where, the wrong row it must no longer name), the questions that must not be stolen, the three traps, and the full sweep as a per-row ratchet.
- **A question about an ability Jarvis really has now reaches its catalogue row, not the local model (2026-11-18).** An audit of the answer layer measured 74 of 183 catalogue rows reachable only by quoting an exact name, and 21 of the owner's 180 measured questions still missing their row - six of them falling straight to the local model, which is free to answer "I can't" about something that exists. Three measured causes are fixed in `backend/jarvis_quick.py`'s capability lane. First, `_explicit_feature_question` short-circuited on the word "and" before trying its own explicit shapes, so every feature question whose subject contains "and" went to the model - 49 catalogue rows, including all six measured fall-throughs ("typing", "chat-thread", "memory-people", "stale-link", "data-sandbox", "trust"). The short-circuit was redundant: the two-part matcher already ran earlier and this lane runs last in `match()`, so it could not be protecting an action path. The same lane also takes the speaker's frame off the subject ("a feature that lets you type..."), which was turning two of those six into a false "I do not have that one". Second, three measured false-denial questions now answer from their row's own words and its own rule: "Can you send a file from my PC to my phone?" (the `file-from-pc` row - the mirror of the one-way shape the file fix of 2026-11-18 already took), "Can you read my phone notifications?" (`phone-notifications`, including its off-by-default card rule) and "Can you add up my spending?" / "Can you check my bank export?" (`spending`, "Plain code on the PC adds it up"). Each is claimed only in the lane that runs after every action matcher, and each lead is only the words of its own question - a bare "can you ..." capability lead would claim "can you write a nice email for my boss?" as `email-send`, which `test_chat_honesty.py` pins to the writer's own path, so no generic "can you" lead was added. Measured with the real matcher (no model): all six measured fall-throughs now reach their rows, 7 of the 21 measured misses close (the sixth is "interrupt", which the "and" guard also hid), and 14 remain - each claimed by another deterministic lane or resolving through a neighbouring row, which this change does not touch. A before/after sweep of 4,488 feature questions shows only improvements: 80 sentences that reached no row now answer from the right one, two that answered `phone-notifications` now answer `phone-apps`, and no action path changed.
- **A question about what Jarvis can do is answered from its own feature list, and a reply can no longer say something was shown, opened or sent when that turn did neither (2026-11-18, the owner's phone report).** Asked on the phone *"Can you send a file for me to my PC?"*, the live app answered *"I can't send files directly, but I can help you move files between your phone and PC. Would you like me to show you how to do that?"* — while the catalogue carried the whole answer: the `document-from-phone` row's own `where` is the exact steps (*"On the phone: Settings, Folders Jarvis may look in, then Send a file from your phone..."*) and, since 2026-11-15, its aliases include "send a file from my phone to my pc". TWO causes, fixed separately. (1) **`POST /api/chat` never consulted the catalogue for this sentence.** `jarvis_quick.answer_turn` runs the fixed phrase grammar first and, when it has nothing, the local model answers — and `_CAP_LEAD`, the capability-question lead, deliberately did not take "can you ..." (that is how the owner asks Jarvis to DO things; `backend/test_chat_honesty.py` pins that a writing request keeps its own path), so the sentence had no tail at all and never reached `_cap_resolve`. Only the ONE measured shape — a "can you" file transfer *to this PC*, the direction no tool of ours starts (the phone's own Settings picks the file) — now strips the lead, so `send_file_to_phone` (the other direction, a real tool) keeps its own path. (2) **The direction rule gave up instead of choosing the honest row.** With a lead that did match (*"Can I send a file from my phone to my PC?"*), `file-from-pc` scored highest because its own id says "file from pc"; `_cap_direction_ok` rejected it as the opposite direction, and `_cap_resolve` returned None rather than take `document-from-phone`, which is the row that names that door. It now drops direction-wrong rows and answers from the best direction-correct one; a question that says "to my PC" also rejects a row that sends "to your phone". The owner's measured words are a catalogue alias now (`features/features.json` — the catalogue was regenerated, never hand-edited) and an exact alias of a row's content words names that row. The same report said Jarvis told him "it's on your screen" about something it had not put on screen: `jarvis_claims.surface_correction` is a new claim family in the EXISTING postscript shape (`backend/jarvis_agent.postscript_lines`, the same list the nothing-done and scheduler-refusal lines use), checking "It's on your screen.", "I've opened it on your screen." and "It's been sent." against the turn's own tool steps — a real showing/opening tool (`retirement_whatif` writes its table on the owner's screen, `product_check` opens a page, `conversation_open`, the acting tools) or a real sending tool backs it, and a bare-pronoun claim with neither gets one plain correction line. Questions, offers, future sentences and anything "already"/"earlier" are left alone, because a wrong correction after a true sentence is worse than a missed one. No route, no card, no auto-approval and no state read: reading the catalogue is not a gated action, and both fixes answer only a turn nothing else owns. Proved in the existing suites — `backend/test_capability_answers.py` (209 passed, 0 failed; the owner's exact sentence is now a fixture, and the same suite reads 7 failures against `origin/main`'s modules) and `backend/test_smarter_answers.py` (197 passed, 0 failed; the screen-claim guard and its real-turn line fail against `origin/main`'s modules).
- **audit job installs the same Python test dependencies as the backend job (2026-11-18).** `tools/check_claims.py` runs every suite a `test:` row names, and the `audit` job installed only `cryptography`. On PR #1366 the attach-audio suite's real-WAV check imports numpy, so in `audit` it printed `SKIP numpy is not installed ...` and claim C123 read as a broken BUILT claim - while the required `backend` job passed the identical tree with numpy installed. The `audit` job now installs the backend job's whole pinned test-dependency list (numpy, sherpa-onnx, onnxruntime, cryptography, pyyaml, pillow, fsrs), so a claim is checked in one environment and gets one answer. The skip rule is untouched: a skip about the code still withholds proof and fails the row, and the four Windows-only checks in `test_data_backup.py` still skip on the Linux runner and are still named on every run.
- **The advisories checker's own recipe now says Python 3.11.5 and names all six lock exceptions (2026-11-18).** `tools/check_python_advisories.py`'s docstring still told the reader to rebuild the lock with `--python-version 3.11` and **five** `--exclude-newer-package` dates, while the lock it documents had moved to Python 3.11.5 with a sixth, `soupsieve=2026-11-06T00:00:00Z` - so anyone following the recipe would have built a different file from the committed one. Both are corrected, and the paragraph now says plainly that those are `uv`'s flags and not this script's, whose one option is `--offline`. Verified rather than assumed: uv 0.12.9, the corrected command, regenerated the lock body into a temporary file and it matched `backend/requirements.lock` **byte for byte** (1,710 lines, no differences). No dependency moved, neither lock copy changed, and no checker behaviour changed - the docstring is the whole change.
- **A reply that says an approval card was raised is now checked against the cards the turn really raised (2026-11-18, DEF-089).** The field test measured the worst version of "do not claim more than the evidence supports": four live replies told the owner "I have raised the approval card" while `GET /api/pending` was empty before and after the turn, and no tool had run. The existing claim families could not see it - `CLAIMS_DONE` needs one of its own verbs after "I've" and "raised" is not one, and a card is not one of `_CLAIM_OBJECT`'s nouns - so the exact sentence passed every check. The new `jarvis_claims.card_claim` / `card_correction` covers the four measured phrasings ("I have raised the approval card", "I've raised a card", "Check your pending approvals", "I've sent that for your approval") plus the plain "Raised a card for you." / "Created an approval request." / passive "An approval card has been created for you." shapes, and is backed by the **turn's own card count** - `_TurnWatch.cards`, the same number `CARDS_PER_TURN` is enforced with and incremented by every path that puts a card on screen - never by the model's words. The correction says what is true and what to do, not just "I did not": *"no approval card was raised in this answer: nothing is waiting for your approval, and no card was shown in it. Ask again in a new message if you want me to try again."* The live waiting list (`jarvis_gate.pending()`, the same read `jarvis_briefing` makes) is consulted for two things only - the sentence may say "nothing is waiting" only when the list really is empty, and a card already waiting leaves the answer alone - and a caller that cannot see the count (`cards=None`) is never corrected rather than guessed at. It rides the existing `postscript_lines` / `_claim_corrections` list as kind `claim`, the mechanism both the local answer and the cloud relay already use, and the cloud lane passes `cards=0` because it offers no tools and cannot raise one. Questions, offers, futures, conditions, negations, "already/earlier", quoted text and code spans are all left alone. Tests: `backend/test_smarter_answers.py` (`t_a_card_claim_needs_the_turn_to_have_raised_one` - the measured shapes corrected with no card and nothing waiting, backed by a card raised this turn, left alone by a card already waiting, unknown turn untouched, one line not per sentence, every exemption; and `t_the_card_claim_gets_the_line_in_a_turn` - a real `run_local_turn` on the row's sentence, then `postscript_lines` with `cards=0` including a fake gate whose pending list is empty, `cards=1`, and pending non-empty) and `backend/test_cloud_honesty.py` (the same line on the cloud lane). Measured against `origin/main`'s own modules before this change: `claims_done` and `unbacked_claim` both answered False for the row's sentence, `surface_correction` answered `""`, and `postscript_lines` returned `[]` - so every new case would have failed. Deliberately NOT covered, so the close is not read as more than it is: the same reply also said "This is just a field test - no cards go through right now" on the turn that *did* raise card `640e98b6b984`, and that mirror false claim (a denial that cards work while one existed) is a different direction this guard does not correct; and the patterns are finite, so a phrasing none matches would still pass uncorrected - the missed-claim direction this module always chooses over a wrong correction.
- **the two merged lanes no longer steal a capability row's own question (2026-11-18).** The cloud-settings chat lane (#1376) claimed two ordinary `cloud-escalation` catalogue questions that #1379's before/after sweep requires: "what is cloud escalation?" (the row's id words in a "What is X?" shape) and "does jarvis escalate to the cloud?" (its "escalate to the cloud" alias in a "Does Jarvis X?" shape). Each lane passed alone; they met only on `main`, and `backend/test_capability_answers.py` measured `cloud-escalation 63 < 65`. The settings lane now requires the sentence to name the SWITCH ("escalation", "cloud switch") or WHAT goes up ("send/share/use things, questions, ... to the cloud"), so the catalogue row's own name in an ordinary question shape reaches its row again - 65/65 with 0 regressions across all 184 rows and no other row's sentence moved.
- **A note edit is classified, stays at `ask`, and the unclassified warning now says what actually happens (2026-11-17).** `edit_vault_note` - the one action the whole Obsidian editor raises (a whole-note save, an append, a tag change, a carded create) - had a tier line (`"ask"` in both shipped settings copies) and no `_RISK` row, so `risk_for()` gave it the unclassified fallback and its card said the action was "treated as permanent and able to leave this PC". Neither half is true of a note: no notes route touches the network, a model or a token, and a save is recoverable because the File Guardian copies the old bytes first and the write is refused if that copy cannot be made. It now has its own row, `("yes", "local")`, added by an end-of-file `_RISK.update({...})` block in `jarvis-backend/jarvis_gate.py` - the one region no earlier patch's hunk claims - and **no patch was written or edited for either half of this change** (the owner's 2026-11-14 ruling). The tier is deliberately unchanged: edits keep their one card (the shipped `"ask"` line and the contract that promises a card + File Guardian copy + Undo), and the row only replaces a fallback with a written decision, so the ordinary treatment of local, reversible change applies (a swipe may approve it, and "What asks first" may offer its switch). The generic sentence was also wrong, so `UNCLASSIFIED_WARNING` is reworded to "Unclassified action - never runs on its own, and a swipe cannot approve it" by a second end-of-file override, the same route: the original definition sits inside `backend/unknown-risk-approvable.patch`'s own hunk, and that patch is untouched, so the published base and the patch still rehearse byte for byte. The gate's worst-case RECORD (`"no"`/`"outbound"`, so no swipe, still forced to `"ask"`) is unchanged, so nothing about approval loosened - only the words stopped asserting what the gate does not know. Proved by `backend/test_gate_unknown_risk.py` (116 -> 136 checks: the footing still reverses the patch out of the base, the new sentence, and the note action's own row and its end-of-file placement) and by `backend/test_notes_edit.py` (144 checks: the action is classified, reversible and local, while its shipped tier stays `ask`). Files: `jarvis-backend/jarvis_gate.py`, both `jarvis-framework.toml` copies, `backend/jarvis_notes_edit.py` + base twin, `backend/jarvis_card_words.py` + base twin, `backend/jarvis_owner_check.py` + base twin, `docs/JARVIS-API.md`, `docs/CALL-RECORDING.md`, `backend/README.md`, `scripts/apply-patches.ps1`, `backend/test_gate_unknown_risk.py`, `backend/test_notes_edit.py`, `backend/test_connected_accounts.py`.

- **A Coding click that cannot prove its pause now refuses and puts both lane models back, instead of leaving the everyday lane empty (2026-11-17).** The owner's live PC (source `02332ecc`) answered a preset click on `POST /api/work/apply {"preset":"coding"}` with: *"the pooled lane did not start: Jarvis did not pause every model it must… still loaded - qwen3.5:9b on port 11436… The two models were not put back exactly as they were: qwen3.5:9b is not loaded on port 11436"* - the start believed `pause_lanes()`'s own `ok` instead of reading each lane's own `/api/ps`, and the failure that followed restored the lanes while the three-card server it had just launched was still up, with one attempt that did not come back, so the everyday model was gone from 11436 until something reloaded it. `jarvis_model_lanes.start_pooled_lane` now (a) reads both lane ports' `/api/ps` after the pause and refuses in plain words, naming the model it SAW, before anything is loaded, and (b) routes EVERY failure - a three-card server that will not start (whose own `server_start` pauses both lanes before it launches), a pause that is not proved, a load that fails or raises - through one undo: unload the pooled model, stop the three-card server FIRST, then ask both lane models back, retry once, and report only the restore the engine proved from `/api/ps` (`restored`, `not_restored`, `pooled_clear`). The uncarded click itself is unchanged (#1336), and the chat and voice road (`apply_from_body`) still raises the pooled lane's one `switch_model` card. Proven by `backend/test_pooled_lane.py` (125 checks; the live failure is reproduced against the old code - a fake pause that claims success while `qwen3.5:9b` is loaded started the pooled lane beside it, and a failed server start left 11436 empty - and both now refuse with the everyday model back) plus `backend/test_presets_owner_ui.py` (86), `backend/test_pooled_modes.py` (48), `backend/test_model_lanes.py` (161) and `backend/test_pooled_preload.py` (27). NOT TESTED: a real three-card load - every lane step runs against a fake `jarvis_big_coder`, because this checkout has no GPU and no live backend.
- **A note's name ends where the next instruction begins (2026-11-17).** The owner's own sentence "make a note for me called Mood Log and have this be one of my favorite notes" was filed as `Mood Log and have this be one of my favorite notes.md` with no favourite set, and "add to the mood log and make a note for today and put today's date and say that ..." answered "I could not find a note called \"mood log and make a note for today and put today's date and say\"", writing nothing. Both readers now cut the name at ONE named list of instruction boundaries, `_NOTE_NAME_BOUNDARIES` in `backend/jarvis_quick.py`, shared by the create reader and the append reader: `Mood Log` is created with `favorite: true`, and the append finds the existing Mood Log case-insensitively and adds the owner's words under a `## YYYY-MM-DD` heading for today taken from the clock - commas and the "didn't know when to call it quits, disappointed" clause kept as content. A name that is genuinely absent still fails with the same "nothing was written" sentence and creates nothing. `backend/test_notes_create_find_append.py` pins both of the owner's sentences verbatim and pins the other side too: "and" is only a boundary when an instruction follows it ("Salt and Pepper" keeps its and; "Poker and Mood and pin it" names "Poker and Mood" and pins it; "add to my Notes and Ideas that ..." appends to that note), and "It is favourited." is said only when `favorite: true` is really in the file (154 checks).
- **A note's "is it pinned" question can now take the folder it was asked about (2026-11-17).** Field-tested on the live install at SOURCE-COMMIT `02332ecc514c` (`FIELD-TEST-ALL-2026-11-17`, Step 4 row 6): `is my workout log note pinned` was refused with *"That name matches 2 notes … so nothing was changed - say the note's folder and name"* - false about a read, which changes nothing by definition - and the sentence that refusal recommends, `is my Workout Log note in Private & Shared/Workout pinned`, reached **no intent at all**, so the 8B model answered that it could not see the owner's notes. The folder is now an optional part of `_NOTE_FLAG_QUESTION`, and the intent uses it: the name is resolved by the one resolver and the folder then **chooses among that name's own candidates**, matching case-insensitively, accepting the folder's last segment ("in Workout") and any folder under the one named. A note at the very **top of the vault** has no folder of its own, so it is offered as *"Shopping" at the top of the vault* and selected by the word for the top (or by the vault's own folder name) - otherwise an answer could ask for a sentence that could not select one of its own candidates. Resolution deliberately no longer goes through the exact-path tier by way of a `folder/name` string, because that tier compares byte-for-byte and a folder typed in other capitals fell back to the basename tier, which cannot see a folder at all - so the reply's own suggested sentence asked for itself for ever. An ambiguous name is answered in READ words from the resolver's own candidate list, each note's title beside its folder and then *"Say the folder and the note's name, so one is chosen."*, instead of the write lane's *"nothing was changed"* and its write-shaped example; a list longer than six adds *"I have shown the first 6."* rather than claiming more than it shows; a folder that holds no such note is said plainly rather than ignored; and a yes/no question is never answered by reading a note's body. Three more repairs came out of the review of that path, all in the same read: front matter that never closes is now **unreadable** rather than *"Yes, pinned"* (`_note_flag_state` returned the value before checking the closing `---`, although its own docstring promised otherwise); a possessive or the flag word itself is no longer read as the note's name, so `is my note in the inbox pinned` asks *"Which note?"* instead of *"No note in your vault is called \"my\""*; and a missing notes editor is reported as itself rather than as an unreadable vault. Read-only throughout: no card, no write, no route, no setting and no tier changed, and every sentence that matched before matches as it did. Proved in the existing `backend/test_chat_wrong_answers.py` (198 -> 218 checks, two new tests driving real vaults: title ambiguity, ALIAS ambiguity, the no-body-dump rule, case, last segment, parent folder, a wrong folder, a note at the top, a seven-note list, no name at all, and unclosed front matter) and unchanged in `test_notes_surgical.py`, `test_notes_smart_create.py`, `test_notes_create_find_append.py`, `test_obsidian_notes.py`, `test_cut_off_note.py`, `test_chat_pins.py`, `test_note_capture.py`, `test_notes_resolve.py` and `test_note_and_vault_asking.py`; `backend/jarvis_quick.py` and its `jarvis-backend/` twin are byte-identical.
- **A GitHub repository, owner or branch the model INVENTED is refused, named, before anything is sent (2026-11-17).** On the owner's live install the local 8B model kept naming repositories and branches that were not on GitHub, and `backend/jarvis_github.py` built a request around the invented name anyway — so the owner got a 404 whose words were "there is nothing there - or it is private" (never naming what was wrong, so the model's invention was invisible), and, worse, an invented name that happened to be somebody else's real repository would have received a write-shaped request. Now `run()` resolves what a request names with GitHub BEFORE any of the request's own steps are sent: `GET /repos/{owner}/{name}` for the repository, and `GET .../branches/{name}` for the branch a card names (the CI branch question and both stages of `github_open_pr`, where a wrong branch used to read as "no CI run" or as a confusing git error). Four answers get four sentences and none substitutes anything: a 404 is *"Jarvis asked GitHub about "owner/name" and there is no such repository: either the owner or the repository name is wrong, or it is private and the token saved on this PC cannot see it. Jarvis stopped there and sent nothing else, so nothing on GitHub changed. Check the name exactly as GitHub shows it..."* — the invented name printed; a 3xx redirect or a 200 naming a different `full_name` is a renamed or moved repository, refused rather than followed; anything that is not an answer (no network, a refused token, a 5xx, a body that is not a repository) says *"Jarvis could not check whether ... exists"* and is never turned into "there is no such repository"; and a 200 whose own `permissions.push` is false refuses an ACTION (*"Jarvis found ... but the GitHub account saved on this PC cannot write to it"*) while still allowing the same repository to be READ, because a read changes nothing. There is no argument that skips the check — it is inside `run()`, `r.repo` is recorded by the very planner that built the address, and `run()`'s parameter list is pinned — and a file read's optional `ref` is deliberately NOT branch-checked, because it may be a tag or a commit id. Cost: ONE extra GET per action that names a repository, and it is the first thing that leaves the PC for that action. `github_create_repo` (no existing name) and `github_list`'s `repos` scope are the only tools without it. **And when NO repository is named at all, the answer is an ASK, not a guess:** the name is never filled in from a setting or a default, and nothing here reads a git remote to invent one, so every one of the fourteen repository-naming write tools refuses BEFORE a card is raised, in words that say what could not be resolved (*"Jarvis could not tell which repository this is about: no repository was named, and Jarvis never fills one in from a default or a guess ... Nothing was sent and nobody was asked."*). Proven by a new section of `backend/test_github_tools.py` (1145 → 1167 checks): every repository-naming tool refuses an invented name with that exact sentence and sends ONLY the one check; the invented owner, the invented branch (after exactly two reads and no CI read), the redirect, the substituted `full_name`, the write-permission refusal (and the read that is still allowed), the network failure and the refused token are each driven through the real `run()`; WITH NO REPOSITORY NAMED every one of those tools is an ask that raises no card; and the check BITES — with the pre-fix module restored in the same worktree, 7 checks fail, including the exact-sentence and "only the target check was sent" halves. `jarvis-backend/jarvis_github.py` is byte-identical (`tools/check_stale_twins.py` exit 0). The documented contract is the new 2026-11-17 paragraph in `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §190.1.
- **A client build on `main` is no longer cancelled by the next merge (2026-11-17).** `.github/workflows/jarvis-client.yml` cancelled unconditionally (`cancel-in-progress: true`), so every newer push to `main` killed the phone build of the merge before it, while `ci.yml:46` already refused to cancel on `refs/heads/main` for exactly that reason. Measured 2026-11-17: five merges landed between 22:13:33Z and 22:16:06Z, and the four `Jarvis client` runs for the first four were all cancelled - `44187914586` on `c2072ce6d`, `44187942667` on `96f85a3b3`, `44187968003` on `90e818084` and `44187994856` on `2ffe919a7` - so four merge commits never got a full client build; only the fifth (`b9325012e`, run `44188361355`) built, in 20.1 minutes. The line now carries `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, the same expression as `ci.yml`, so a pull request still cancels its own superseded runs (its `github.ref` is `refs/pull/<n>/merge`) and a build that has STARTED on `main` always finishes. What it does not do, stated rather than implied: GitHub keeps one running and one pending run per group, and a newer queue entry replaces the pending one whatever `cancel-in-progress` says (the docs' "any previously pending job or workflow in the concurrency group will be canceled"), so in a merge wave the first build and the last queued one survive while the middle merges can still lose their run - the queue cannot stack up to an hour of builds, but it also cannot give every merge its own verdict. `self-code-map.yml:43` was deliberately left alone: it is a 10-minute informational check of generated files on `main`, so only the newest run's answer means anything and superseding the older ones is correct. Checked: `py -3 -B tools/roll_changelog.py --check`, `py -3 -B tools/roll_decisions.py --check`, `py -3 -B backend/test_ci_emulator_install.py` (it parses this workflow with `yaml.safe_load`) and `py -3 -B backend/test_roll_decisions.py` all exit 0. NOT TESTED: no GitHub run has used the new expression yet - it first applies to the next push to `main` or the next pull request that touches the client's paths.
- **The twice-seen "Jarvis client" build flake is tracked as DEF-087, and not fixed (2026-11-17).** `EventStreamContractTest > cancellingTheCollectorEndsTheConnection` fails intermittently with `java.lang.AssertionError: cancelling left the stream coroutine running` at `jarvis-client/app/src/test/java/com/jarvis/client/EventStreamContractTest.kt:213`: the test holds the stream body open and requires a `launch(Dispatchers.IO)` collector to observe `cancel()` and finish inside a 15-second `withTimeoutOrNull` around `collector.join()`, so a slow runner reports the assertion with nothing wrong in the client. The occurrence read in full is PR #1348's - workflow "Jarvis client", run `44169740019`, job `134345343311`, step "Run unit tests" failed after 4m34s with `3956 tests completed, 1 failed` and `BUILD FAILED in 3m 52s`, and the six APK steps after it were skipped. `build` is not one of the seven required checks, so this flake cannot block a merge; it can only make a run red and hide a real APK failure behind the same job. The owner's 2026-11-17 ruling (Gemini, Q5) is to track it as DEF-087 in `docs/defect-register.tsv` and `docs/DEFECT-REGISTER.md` and fix it deterministically after P0, so this entry records the defect only: no fix, no quarantine, no retry wrapper and no test change, and the failure was not reproduced locally.
- **A required CI check can no longer open a Playwright browser: the four visible-browser suites now need their own switch for the window (2026-11-17).** The note that a CI log attributed a Playwright `Locator.click` timeout to `backend/test_chatbot_gemini.py` is **confirmed, not a misattribution**. That suite has no `.click(` of its own - the click is in the module it drives, `backend/jarvis_chatbot_web.py:914` (`box.click()`, the message box) and `:933` (`btn.click()`, the send button) - which is why a plain grep for `.click(` found only `test_browser_engine.py` and looked like the wrong suite. The chain was real and is measured. `backend-shard` sets `JARVIS_ALLOW_VISIBLE_BROWSER_TESTS: "1"` so the four suites' 441 code-only checks still run, and since 2026-10-27 (#925) that same required job also runs `python -m playwright install --with-deps chromium` for `test_browser_control_live.py`. So "is Playwright installed?" - the only browser-half gate each suite had - became TRUE in a required job, while `run_suites.py`'s skip-by-name layer was already disarmed by the opt-in, and all four suites really drove Chromium there. Measured on one green run of `main` (2026-11-17): `test_chatbot_sites.py` 486.4 s, `test_chatbot_gemini.py` 117.2 s, `test_support_widget.py` 54.8 s, `test_handoff.py` 12.1 s - against 0.3 s for a genuinely code-only suite in the same shard, and a code-only half cannot take eight minutes. The fix is a second, explicit switch: each suite now asks `JARVIS_RUN_REAL_BROWSER=1` BEFORE it asks whether Playwright is installed, so with only the old opt-in set it runs its code checks and prints one `SKIP the real-browser half: JARVIS_RUN_REAL_BROWSER=1 is not set ...` line. No job in ci.yml sets it, and the two comments that asserted the opposite are corrected - `backend-shard`'s ("this job does not install the package either") and `backend-windows`'s ("No Playwright browser is installed on a runner") - as is the same claim in `scripts/apply-patches.ps1` and `backend/test_browser_test_guard.py`'s own docstring. Proven by `backend/test_browser_test_guard.py` (70 -> 84 checks): every suite must name the new switch, read it itself with only `"1"` accepted, and ask for it on an earlier line than `playwright_installed()`; the sweep job must **still** install a Playwright browser, so the guard rests on the switch and not on a package's absence; and nothing in ci.yml may set the new switch. The owner's workflow is unchanged: neither `tools/update_backend.py` nor `scripts/apply-patches.ps1` ever sets the old opt-in, so a normal update still skips all four suites; running them by hand now needs both variables. Honest limits: no CI run was triggered for this change, and the browser halves were deliberately not executed - the code-only halves were run on this PC with Playwright's browser path emptied (`test_chatbot_sites` 291, `test_chatbot_gemini` 26, `test_handoff` 108, `test_support_widget` 10 passed), with three pre-existing `%TEMP%` access-denied failures that reproduce in three lines on unmodified code. **The other half, later the same day: the browser install itself is gone from the required job.** Giving the window its own switch stopped a *window*, but it left a Playwright *browser* installed in a REQUIRED job, so a required check could still launch one, and "nothing sets the switch" was a promise rather than a mechanism. The ruling was that required CI must not even be able to launch a browser, so `backend-shard` no longer runs `python -m pip install playwright` / `python -m playwright install --with-deps chromium`. What that install was for - `test_browser_control_live.py`, whose 66 checks are real and were NOT dropped - is handled twice over instead of silently: `backend/run_suites.py` skips it BY NAME when the `playwright` package is absent (printed as `skip` with the reason, counted as a skip, named in the run's `SKIPPED BY NAME` line, never `ok` - so this is not the old `ZERO_CHECK_ALLOWED` under a new name), and a new INFORMATIONAL `backend-browser-live` job in ci.yml installs Playwright and Chromium and runs that one suite for real on every push, demanding the runner's `ok` line so a broken install cannot pass as a skip. `backend/test_browser_test_guard.py` grew 84 -> 95 checks and now pins the opposite of what it pinned that morning: no required backend job installs Playwright, the only jobs that do are `frontend-shard` (required, and its own page tests ARE browser tests - named as the exception rather than hidden) and `backend-browser-live` (informational), nothing sets `JARVIS_RUN_REAL_BROWSER`, and the live suite's skip is the printed, counted, named kind. `backend-windows` loses `'test_browser_control_live.py'` from its array: that job never installed Playwright, so the line was a SKIP counted as a pass by its exit-code loop - the shape its opt-in exists to stop - and the name returns only with an install step. Measured at the desk, on this PC: with Playwright present and only the opt-in set, `test_chatbot_sites.py` ran its 293 code checks and printed `SKIP the real-browser half: JARVIS_RUN_REAL_BROWSER=1 is not set`; with `JARVIS_RUN_REAL_BROWSER=1` and the package shadowed it got PAST the window gate and printed `SKIP the real-browser half: playwright is not installed`, so the switch does not block a desk run that has a browser; and `test_browser_control_live.py` really passed its 66 checks against a headless Chromium here, through the runner. `backend/test_suite_report.py` went 93 -> 100 checks: its control now proves the named skip instead of a zero-check FAIL. Honest limits: no CI run was triggered for this change; the four browser suites' visible halves were not executed, so no window was put on the owner's screen; and `frontend-shard`, a required job, still installs a browser on purpose.

A second command, `npm run typecheck:bindings`, runs `tsc` over the generated file and the one module that calls it, so a page that disagrees with the Rust signature fails instead of failing at runtime on the owner's PC. It is a PILOT on purpose - the other ~593 calls are untouched, and the two checks are not yet wired into CI. Three things were measured and are worth knowing before any migration: a pure RENAME of a Rust argument does not break the page (the generated wrapper takes the value positionally, so the page never spells the IPC key at all - the old `valid_to`/`option_id` class of bug becomes impossible); a struct field with its own doc comment makes the JSDoc exporter emit invalid JavaScript, so `Bound`'s two field comments moved into the type's own doc; and the exporter cannot be a `#[test]`, because a test binary gets no Windows manifest and dies before `main` with STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND once it links enough of tauri to import `comctl32!TaskDialogIndirect`. - **The Python half of `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` is generated and checked now, so it can no longer go stale silently (`tools/gen_notices.py --python`, 2026-11-16).** This closes problem 3 of `docs/DEEP-AUDITS-2026-10-05.md` — *"Add a Python package, a model or a Maven library and nothing fails"* — for the Python packages: the Rust half already had a generator, and this extends it rather than adding a second convention. `--python` rewrites section 3 alone, from `backend/requirements.lock`: all **78 pinned releases**, each row carrying the licence that release's **own published metadata declares for exactly that version**, read from PyPI's JSON API (the same stdlib reader `tools/check_python_advisories.py` already uses, name and version only, generic User-Agent). It needs no cargo and no installed backend, which is why `--check --python` — which exits non-zero and **names every package that differs** — now runs as its own step in the **informational `audit` job**, not in a required one, on purpose. Nothing is guessed: `espeakng-loader` states no licence at all and reads **`unknown`**, and the 9 packages that declare only a vague statement (`"BSD"`, `"BSD License"`, `"Dual License"`, `"Apache Software License"`, `"Apache licensed, as found in the LICENSE file"`, or two licences at once) keep their own words and are listed again at the end of the section for a person to resolve — a licence never becomes MIT by inference. `pip-licenses` (MIT) is the second reader: it is pinned in a new **`tools/requirements-dev.txt`**, never in `requirements.lock` and never a Jarvis runtime dependency, and the generator prints a NOTE for any package where it describes the licence differently (it reads the *installed* set, which drifts from the lock — five of the 78 pins on this PC were installed at another version — so it cross-checks, it does not author the rows). Proved: three consecutive runs produce **byte-identical files** (sha256 `61F52676…50B5A720`), and a run with `pip-licenses` installed produces the **same bytes** as one without it; a planted wrong licence for one package makes `--check --python` exit 1 naming `cobble 0.1.4: the file says "MIT", the release says "BSD License"`; both `--check` and `--check --python` exit 0 against the committed file. **No existing licence row changed** — the only edits to existing text are the header's list and the section numbers (Apache-2.0 NOTICE files 3→4, licence texts 4→5). `--diff` now reads the Rust section only, so Python rows cannot be reported as removed crates.
- **A preset the owner clicks is uncarded, the heavy Coding preset included; the same preset asked for in chat still raises its card (2026-11-16).** The owner's report: *"when i change the model on the jarvis app it still sends me an approval card. that shouldnt happen if i manually press the preset change. only if i ask through chat"*. The 2026-11-09 manual-click rule (Gemini Q2: a reversible thing clicked in either app's own UI is not carded, and the same thing asked for in chat is) already covered every local preset except the heavy rows, because the one condition was `direct_owner = bool(owner_ui) and not heavy` (`backend/jarvis_presets.py:1840`). A Coding click therefore fell to `_default_start_lane` (`:2023`), which called `jarvis_model_lanes.start_pooled_lane(mode="coding")` with no gate, and the pooled lane raised its OWN `switch_model` card before it unloaded anything. Now a preset clicked on `POST /api/work/apply` applies uncarded whatever its weight: `_start_lane_for_the_owner` starts the pooled lane with `_OwnerPressed` as its gate - the press IS the approval, in the shape a card's verdict has (`allowed`, `outcome`, `reason`) - so no `jarvis_gate.check()` is reached on that road, the lane still announces, pauses and loads in the same measured order, and the `preset_apply` receipt still makes the click undoable (now also when the preset it replaced was Coding or Medical). THE MODEL ROAD IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: a heavy preset still records through `_default_adopt` on BOTH roads, because `jarvis_models.switch_to` runs the tripwire's smoke test at the one-card everyday lane and a 14.8 GB coding model would either be loaded twice or evict the model the pooled lane just loaded, with its "did it work" answer about the wrong lane. THE CHAT AND VOICE ROADS ARE UNCHANGED and still raise exactly their one card: `jarvis_models.switch_to`'s `switch_model` on a named lane, and the pooled lane's own `switch_model` card for Coding or Medical; the Cloud row still asks on every road. The tier table is untouched (`switch_model` stays `ask`), no request body can ask for the uncarded road, and `owner_ui=True` is still set by ONE caller - `install()`'s POST wrapper, after its origin and token checks. Proven by `backend/test_presets_owner_ui.py` (86 checks: a Coding and a Medical click raise no card, start the pooled lane through the real `jarvis_model_lanes.start_pooled_lane`, record the loaded model through adopt and write an undoable receipt; the same Coding request from chat asks exactly one card and a denied card unloads nothing; the eight presets on a named lane are unchanged; Undo works in both directions; a lane that will not load refuses in plain words and changes nothing) and `backend/test_reversible_ui_choices.py` (136 checks: the allow-list's two sides, plus the heavy row's two roads meeting the pooled lane with a consenting gate and with no gate). NOT TESTED: the real three-card load - every lane step runs against a fake big-coder module, because this checkout has no GPU and no live backend.

- **An over-window prompt is refused instead of sent, and a long file is read as numbered lines with the range to ask for next (2026-11-16).** Two ways text was silently lost are closed. (1) When the prompt estimator said a pooled-lane prompt was over the window, `jarvis_agent.py` announced a warning and sent it anyway, so Ollama dropped the FRONT - Jarvis's rules and the earliest turns. Measured before the change at origin/main `7c3c58736`: an 8,192-token window, an 11,328-token prompt, the warning line, a request to `/api/chat` and the answer "ok". The branch now runs ONE aggressive re-trim (every tool result but the newest stubbed, `fit_messages` to 60% of the window) and, if the prompt plus the offered schemas still does not fit, refuses with one plain sentence before any request ("Prompt exceeds the 8,192-token local window ... Shorten the input, chunk the file, or escalate to DeepSeek"); the old warn-and-send line is gone. `max_tokens` is clamped to `min(client value, n_ctx // 4, 8192)` so an app cannot collapse the prompt budget. (2) `file_read` used to return up to 200,000 bytes from the front of a file, and the 8,000-character tool-content cap kept the first and last 1,500 characters OF THAT SLICE - for a file longer than the cap the model never saw the real end, and the tool had no argument to ask for the rest. Measured before the change on a real 1,020,029-character file: 200,000 characters returned, the real last line absent, 3,436 characters handed to the model, `file_read` arguments `['path']`. It now returns numbered line slices ("1: ...") with `start_line`, `end_line`, `total_lines`, `truncated` and a `more` footer naming the next range, and takes optional `start_line`/`lines` with the same names and defaults as `project_read` (400 lines, at most 2,000), so the model can ask for the exact next slice. The slice is capped at 6,000 characters so the footer survives the tool-content cap. The saved tool-schema fixture (`tools/tool_eval/jarvis_tools.json`) moves with the new schema, and `test_tool_text.py`'s measured-tools budget moves 2,970 → 3,050 (measured 3,023). Tests: `test_chat_window.py` 22, `test_agent.py` 453 passed 1 skipped, `test_smarter_answers.py` 180, `test_tool_text.py` 185, `test_tool_schema_wiring.py` 22, `test_security_pc.py` 234, `test_protection.py` 166, `test_pooled_preload.py` 27, `test_lane_integrity.py` 29, `test_reasoning_room.py` 29, `test_measure_prompt_stack.py` 43 - all 0 failed. Not in this PR, deliberately: the six-file estimator unification (structured payloads at 2.5 characters a token) was measured to move more than the three expected budget pins - `my_files` is pinned at 330 tokens and measures 329, `more_tools` at 520 and measures 511 - so it was stopped per the lead's instruction and belongs in its own PR. No live install has carried this yet.
- **One gate decides whether anything leaves this PC, and closed means refused (2026-11-16).** Jarvis is local-first, not local-only: six named cloud services can carry a request off this machine, and until now each of the four senders decided for itself whether it was allowed to. That decision now lives in ONE place - `backend/jarvis_egress_gate.py`, asked through `check_egress(caller, target_url, payload, surface, local_only=None)`, which never raises and opens no socket. The order is the order a person would ask: a loopback address (this PC talking to itself) is always allowed and reads no setting; then `local_only=True` refuses something that must stay here, which is how rule 1 (email, files, credentials, stored memory) is carried; then Lockdown; then the standing cloud switch (`escalate-cloud.json`); then the service's monthly money cap in `chatbot/api-money.json`. Closed means REFUSED: an absent, unreadable or corrupt switch is off, a damaged Lockdown file is on, and an unreadable money file, a service with no limit, or a host this PC has no settings for all refuse - a cap that cannot be read cannot be a yes. The chatbot's API adapter and the quiz's "Grade this better" send now ask it about the exact URL their socket is about to open (`request_url()` is the one place that builds it), and a refusal ends the conversation or the quiz as `egress_blocked` in the gate's own words with nothing sent. Review found one real bug in the first version: `_money_refusal` was called with `target` twice, the `TypeError` was caught by the gate's own never-raise belt, and every non-loopback request refused as `config_unreadable` - a gate that refuses everything is exactly as wrong as one that allows everything, so two suites now prove both directions (a refusal sends nothing, and a loopback send really goes). The published-base twin had been left at that pre-fix version and is byte-identical again. Two senders remain and are deliberately NOT wired in this change - the web search in `jarvis_search.py` and the HUD, which relays a cloud lane's request from an address it is handed at runtime. `tools/check_egress_gate.py`, now run by CI's `audit` job, lists the web-search sender (both copies) with that reason so a second lane cannot miss it; the HUD spells no cloud host at all, which the checker says out loud it cannot see, so that gap is written down here instead. The same checker fails if any file under `backend/`, `jarvis-backend/` or `tools/` names one of the six hosts without asking the gate or being on its allow-list with a written reason.
- **`OLLAMA_URL` is checked to be this PC at every place it is read, and a cloud lane whose key read came back empty is answered here instead of sending Jarvis's own token to the provider (2026-11-16).** Three files read the variable straight out of the environment and used whatever they found: `jarvis-backend/jarvis_models.py:71`, `jarvis-backend/jarvis_extract.py:42` and `jarvis-backend/jarvis_hud.py:74` (the third is the live `jarvis_hud.py`'s repo twin). Everywhere else in Jarvis "local" means loopback, so an `OLLAMA_URL` naming any other host would have sent the owner's conversations, extracted facts and notes there while every document still said the model runs on this PC. **One function now does the check - `ollama_url_on_this_pc()` in `jarvis-backend/jarvis_models.py`, the module that already owned the local model's address - and all three reads call it; there is no second copy.** Unset, empty and loopback values behave exactly as before (unset returns `http://127.0.0.1:11434`; empty stays empty, as it did; a loopback value is returned byte-for-byte and each caller keeps its own `.rstrip("/")`). A value naming any other host is refused, not used: this PC's loopback default answers instead, and one plain line on stderr says `OLLAMA_URL is '...', and its host '...' is not this PC, so it was refused and http://127.0.0.1:11434 is used instead (it must be 127.0.0.1, localhost or ::1).` **The `_auth_headers` audit found a real seam and it is fixed in the same PR.** The live builder (`jarvis_hud.py:1711-1725` after the stack) ends `bearer = _api.last_lane_state().get("key") or JARVIS_API_KEY`, and the address it is paired with is chosen separately at `:5919` (`return _state["url"]`). `jarvis_chatbot_api.lane_state()` fills `url` from `cloud_lane()` - whose `ready_for()` reads whether a key is SAVED - and then fills `key` from `lane_key()`, a SECOND Credential Manager read (the module's words: "`lane_key(state["lane"]) or ""`"). A lane that is ready but whose second read comes back empty therefore produces exactly the dangerous state: a provider's address with no key. `_auth_headers` would then fall back to `JARVIS_API_KEY`, so this PC's own pairing token would be sent to `api.deepseek.com`. `backend/ollama-direct.patch` now takes a provider address only when that same resolved state carries a non-empty key (`if _state.get("url") and _state.get("key"):`), so no key means no address and this PC answers instead - the same promise the function already made for a lane it cannot pay for. Tests are in the existing suites: `backend/test_gpu_offload.py` (66 passed, 0 failed) pins unset, empty, three loopback spellings and four refused values including `http://127.0.0.1@evil.example.com/`, and `backend/test_ollama_direct.py` (10 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed) drives the real stack-built `_completions_url` with a provider lane whose key came back empty. The six skips are the suite's pre-existing checks that need a real `jarvis_hud.py` on the machine; the new check reads the patch stack's own text, so it runs in a clone. The owner's live install was not written to or restarted: the change reaches it through `jarvis-backend/` and the patcher like any other base change, and the defect row stays open until a live probe shows the refusal.
- **One resolver for every note tool, and the vault's daily-note settings (2026-11-16).** The architect's Wave 1 ruling kept `jarvis_notes_edit.py` as the SOLE vault writer and moved resolution to `backend/jarvis_notes.py`, where `resolve_note(name)` is now the one place every note tool routes through. Its tier order is adapted, as a pattern, from Vinzent03/obsidian-advanced-uri (MIT): the exact vault path the owner named, then the file name matched case-insensitively, then an exact value of the note's own YAML `aliases:` list, then a refusal that lists the candidates. There is no daily-note fallback in any tier - the resolver has no branch that knows what a daily note is - and an explicit test asserts it cannot return one. `jarvis_notes_edit.find_name()` is now a thin `(row, why, matches)` compatibility shape over that resolver, so the chat read/append/tag/rename/move doors and the editor share one implementation. The refusal vocabulary is adapted, as patterns, from cyanheads/obsidian-mcp-server (Apache-2.0) and coddingtonbear/obsidian-local-rest-api (MIT): `case_variant_exists` (the Windows case-collision trap, naming the file that differs only by capital letters), `content_preexists`, `ambiguous_section` with a `candidates` list, and `not_found` with near candidates. The two options those projects expose as request headers - `create_target_if_missing` and `reject_if_content_preexists` - are boolean arguments on `jarvis_notes.create_target()` and on `POST /api/notes/create`, never a second HTTP surface; Epic Jarvis still never overwrites, so False only allows filling an EMPTY existing note. Separately, `jarvis_note_capture.py` now reads `.obsidian/daily-notes.json` for `folder`, `format` and `template` and applies a configured template to a NEW daily note (the note follows the template's bytes), following the behaviour, as a pattern, of liamcain/obsidian-daily-notes-interface (MIT) `settings.ts`/`createDailyNote`. A vault with no `daily-notes.json` - the owner's vault today - behaves exactly as before: `YYYY-MM-DD` in the top folder, a new note holding just the owner's words, the card saying no template is set, and no settings file invented. `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §170.13 records all of it, and `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` carries the four credit lines. `backend/test_notes_resolve.py` (69 checks) pins each tier separately, the two-match refusal naming its candidates, the case collision, the create options, no daily-note fallback, and the absent/present/broken settings cases; `backend/test_notes_create_find_append.py` grows the chat-level no-fallback assertion (102 checks).
- **A spoken sentence is refused as a note's name, and a capture with no words makes no file (2026-11-16).** The capture path (`jarvis_note_capture.plan`) derives a Joplin note's name from the owner's own words, and it used to take the first line whole - cut at 80 characters and closed with an ellipsis - so a dictated command like `Workout Log, pin it, and add using todays date that i used the punching bag` became the note's name, and any line past 80 characters became a plausible-looking half of one. A name that joins a second instruction (`and`, `then`, `but`, `plus`), asks Jarvis to do something (`add`, `append`, `delete`, `remove`, `pin`, `unpin`, `rename`, `move`, `set`, `remember`, `make`, `create`, `write`, `put`), trails off in an ellipsis, or runs past 10 words / 80 characters is now REFUSED with a 400 that quotes the sentence, says it is a sentence or an instruction, and asks for just the note's name - never truncated. A name that already means one of the owner's notes is refused in the ONE resolver's own words (`jarvis_notes.resolve_note`: "there is already a note at ...", or its own two-candidate question), so no second note with that name is made; and `run()` now refuses an empty body, so a Plan built by hand can no longer leave an empty journal or daily-note file behind. Measured on `origin/main` 4dd144d5e: `plan("joplin", <the sentence>)` returned the sentence as `title`, a 148-character first line came back cut at 80 with `…`, `run(Plan(target="logseq", text="   "))` returned ok True and made a file, and a fake Joplin received the sentence as the note's title - with the fix the plan refuses, no call reaches Joplin, no file is made, and `backend/test_note_capture.py` reads 114 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped against 85 passed / 29 failed on the unmodified module (34 new checks).
- **The owner's own memory is not outside text (2026-11-16).** A note write and a setting change after a memory-injected turn were both treated as if a page or an email had shaped the turn: `make a new note called Field Test Groceries and pin it` waited on an `edit_vault_note` card, and a cloud-escalation question refused itself as "shaped by something outside of your direct input". Memory still stays on this PC: a memory-injected turn passes `lanes=[]` to the router, and a cloud lane is sent user-role messages only. A page, an email body, a document and the pasted file's own gate/mark latch exactly as before, 30 minutes and re-latched every turn. The published base fix reaches a live install through four literal deploy deltas in `tools/hud-deltas/`, proved to reconstruct the base byte for byte.

- **A background job can be moved to the front, by one sentence (2026-11-16).** The owner asked to "prioritize it through chat". Each job row now carries a priority - low, normal (the default, and what every row written before this became) or urgent - and the queue takes the highest first, then the same `due` order it always used, so a database of ordinary jobs behaves exactly as it did before. "What jobs do I have" numbers the list in the order the queue runs it and names each job's priority; "make job 2 urgent", "do job 1 first", "make job 2 normal" or "lower job 2" moves one, and the answer echoes the job's label because the list can shift between the read and the write; "which job runs next" answers from the queue's own query. A bump grants nothing: it never runs a job before its time, never widens what the job may do, and a job parked for the owner's approval still waits for it. The owner may move a job and a model may not - no route and no model tool reaches the setter. Both apps still do not draw the priority; that is a later PR, and the field is already on `GET /api/jobs` for them.
- **A background job that ends now tells you, in both apps (2026-11-16).** The owner asked for a notification when a long task he started finishes. The PC already published a `job` event carrying the smallest honest copy — the job's label and its state, never the result and never the params — and its durable outbox already re-announced a completion that a crash had interrupted; what was missing was a client that listened. The phone dropped the event as "unhandled", and the desktop's own Windows toasts had no kind for it. Now one notification (phone) and one toast (desktop) say only the job's label and that it ended, deduplicated by the job id so a replay replaces its own notice, and tapping either opens the Work pane or Work tab where the answer already is. The event's failure text is gone as well: `_finish` used to put `error[:120]` into the frame's `note`, which is arbitrary handler text and in the suite's own probe was the result itself. The phone and desktop halves are NOT-TESTED on real hardware until CI builds and the owner installs them.

- **The Hardware screen's two remaining false sentences are fixed: the answer after choosing a setup no longer promises an approval card for every step, and the Details list no longer calls its own measured line calculated (2026-11-16).** The desktop and phone pages were corrected in #1309 and #1305, but both sentences are printed by the backend and were deliberately left there. `choose()` now says what is true in every state it answers in - nothing has changed yet, the steps are in order, a step with a card asks you first, and the settings step is a line you run on this PC, which `_steps()` gives `route=None` so the page draws no Ask button for it. - **A dev-only probe prints what Jarvis can do with nobody asked, and what a plan card or a trusted window would add (2026-11-16).** `tools/github_trust_probe.py --reachability` reads `jarvis_gate.py`'s own `_TOOL_ACTIONS` and `_RISK` tables and the shipped `[autonomy.tiers]` lines, folds in the `<table>.update({...})` blocks the way Python builds them, and prints the zero-touch baseline and the diff for each approved change in 0.2 seconds with **zero model calls, no network and no extra package**. - **The CI answer counts only the runs it actually read (2026-11-16, DEF-078).** Asked about a pull request, `github_ci_status` judges the head commit's check runs, and when GitHub reported no check runs it fell back to judging the workflow runs on that commit - with the sentence "More than one CI run is on the head commit of pull request #N in owner/repo and at least one did not finish successfully", whatever the list held. With exactly ONE red run and no readable check runs, that was a false count about the owner's own repository, and it asserted a number the reader never managed to verify. The failed-commit sentence now says what was READ about the checks ("GitHub reports no check runs on ...", or "GitHub did not answer with the check runs on ..." when that read could not be parsed) and counts only the runs in the answer - "one CI run is on the head commit" for a list of one, "N CI runs are on the head commit" for N - so "more than one" is only ever said when it is true. The branch form keeps its own newest-run sentence and both are rendered by the one `_ci_words`, so the two answers cannot drift apart. `backend/test_github_ci_count.py` is the proof: the false count is pinned by name, and 7 of its 22 checks fail against the old renderer while all 22 pass with the fix.

The `/v1` wire's `usage.completion_tokens` and Ollama's native `eval_count` are the same field, read by one line and summed over the turn's tool rounds; the speed row's `tokens`/`token_source` follow it when the model reports one, so the speed record and the cloud cost of an answer (`jarvis_chatbot_api.cost_of`'s completion term, through `Meter.finish()`) read one number. after, it reads that note). - **Four awareness questions stop being the model's guess (2026-11-16).** An audit on 2026-11-15 asked the live backend nineteen awareness questions and checked each answer against the machine; eleven had no fixed answer at all and fell through to the 8B model, which cannot measure any of them. PR #1292 fixed two. This lands the four of the remaining eleven that a real local read can settle: *"what models are loaded"* now reads Ollama's own `/api/ps` and says **"Nothing is loaded right now"** when it is empty, quoting the loaded model's memory, card share and context when it is not; *"how many models are installed"* (and which) reaches the existing installed-model answer that already leads with the count; *"what is my disk space"* reaches the PC-facts disk answer ("how much disk space is left" already got it) and so names **every** drive - the audit's gap there was the wording, not a missing read, and a narrower one-drive answer was dropped rather than added beside the wider one; and *"is ollama running"* reports whether the lane's own server answers, using the same `/api/tags` probe both apps' lane warning makes. Every answer names the read that produced it, keeps to a phone-sized sentence, and when the read fails says plainly **"I could not read ... so I cannot tell, and I will not guess"** - it never falls back to the model, never invents a number, and never upgrades the configured model into a running one (it is **set to use**). But this file is the stand-in for `@tauri-apps/api/core` — its whole job is to forward a name it does not know to `window.__TAURI__.core.invoke`, and the real names live in the generated `bindings.js` and `hotkeys-bindings.js`, which the check reads as literals.
