- **The preflight now says which commit each piece came from, and warns MIXED COMMITS when they disagree (2026-11-15, Gemini's ruling Q8):** three pieces the owner runs were measured at three different commits - the desktop release 0.2.458 was built from `7a8fe7d`, the Android APK from `2aacc71ba`, and the live backend's `VERSION` said 0.2.456, from `04d4748cf` - and nothing told him. Each piece now records its own source commit, in the metadata it already had: `latest.json` (the desktop's updater manifest) carries a machine-readable `commit` field, a program-readable copy of the "from commit ... on main" line the release notes already wrote, filled from the build's own `$GITHUB_SHA`; the live backend folder gets a `SOURCE-COMMIT` record written by `tools/reconcile_live_backend.py` from the commit its bytes were deployed from, BESIDE `VERSION` and never inside it (that file is the shared release marker the desktop HUD compares character for character, and every other reader parses it as a bare version number); and the phone's APK already recorded its commit in `client-latest.json` and in its own `BuildConfig`, so it needed nothing. The preflight (`py -3 backend\selftest.py --preflight`) gains a `commits` check that reads the desktop app's start-up log line (which now names the commit `build.rs` read at build time), the backend's `SOURCE-COMMIT` (only while it still agrees with `VERSION`, so a stale record is never passed off as the current one), and prints **"MIXED COMMITS: the desktop app came from 7a8fe7d, but the backend came from 04d4748"** when two pieces that DO name a commit disagree. It is visibility, not a gate: a mismatch is a WARN, a piece that does not say is a WARN in those words ("the desktop app does not say which commit it came from"), and nothing here can FAIL, block an update, raise a card or fetch from the network. The phone's installed APK is the one piece this PC cannot see (the file stays on the phone), so it is reported as unknown rather than guessed at or fetched. Evidence: `backend/test_selftest_preflight.py` drives the desktop log and the backend record through temp folders - a mismatch, a match recorded short and long, an older-than-the-files record, junk, and a build that names no commit - and `backend/test_reconcile_live_backend.py` pins the new record's shape, its "unchanged" second run and the "skipped, never guessed" case; `jarvis-desktop/tests/updater-manifest.mjs` pins the manifest field and that the release workflow passes the same `$GITHUB_SHA` the notes use.
- **A feature pull request no longer commits the self-code map (2026-11-15).** The map of Jarvis's own code used to be regenerated by every pull request, because it records every tracked file - and every pull request owes a changelog fragment and a decisions fragment. So two pull requests always wrote the same 330 KB file: six landed in one night and the map forced a full conflict plus a fresh CI round on every one, turning eight merges into about nine hours (the owner's ruling Q1). Now a pull request only has to keep the tree COHERENT - every tracked file owned by exactly one subsystem, every key module, suite and document the generator's table names present - which `backend/test_self_code.py` proves in the required backend job without reading the map at all, and `py -3 tools/gen_self_code_map.py --coherence` runs the same check at the desk. A pull request that adds a module edits the generator's `SUBSYSTEMS` table (that edit is the whole cost) and regenerates nothing. The map itself is a snapshot of `main`, re-taken by one command on a branch off main after a merge. A new workflow, `.github/workflows/self-code-map.yml`, runs the strict `py -3 tools/gen_self_code_map.py --check` on main after every merge and goes red, naming that command, until the snapshot is done - so the map can be one merge behind, never silently wrong. The generator also refuses to WRITE on a dirty tree now: its file lists come from the index while the commit it records comes from HEAD, and a map generated during an in-progress merge was measured on main recording a commit that never had the files it listed. Nothing a person asks Jarvis changes: the map, its reader and its four answers are the same file and the same code.
- **A pull request no longer re-takes the recent-changes module - main does, after the merge (2026-11-15).** `backend/jarvis_recent_changes.py` and its `jarvis-backend/` twin are generated from `changelog.d/`, so every pull request that owed a fragment rewrote the same two lines of both files, and two such PRs always conflicted - the last whole-tree conflict left after the owner's ruling Q1 took the self-code map out of pull requests. The owner's ruling Q2 moves it the same way: a PR adds its fragment and stops there, and `.github/workflows/self-code-map.yml` runs `py -3 tools/gen_recent_changes.py --check` after every merge, naming the one command when main is behind. The check that a PR cannot satisfy is replaced by one that measures honesty instead of freshness: `backend/test_self_knowledge_honesty.py` now proves every bullet the module carries is a real run of the record's own order (an invented, re-worded or dropped bullet still fails), and demands the exact bytes only when `JARVIS_RECENT_CHANGES_STRICT=1`, which the workflow sets. Nothing the owner reads changes: the answer to "what changed in your last update?" is the same sentence from the same shipped module, and a stale module on main still goes red the same day.
- **A read-aloud now carries on when you leave the app, PiP and the lock screen included, and long answers are read to the end (2026-11-15).** Pressing HOME, switching to another app, putting Atlas in picture-in-picture or locking the phone used to stop a read in progress. It no longer does: a media-playback foreground service keeps the voice going for the rest of the answer and puts one line in the shade with "Stop talking". A long note used to stop part-way as well - a 24-sentence cap ended the read, and a paragraph with no full stop was one slow request, which is what the gaps were. Long answers are now read to the end, in pieces the PC can synthesise quickly, with the next piece fetched while the current one is spoken. Nothing about what may be read changes - a locked phone, App lock and a stale link still refuse to start one.
- **The phone's ten focus presets open at one line, with each row's prose behind one tap (2026-11-15).** The phone audit of 2026-11-15 measured the "Focus presets" plate printing five blocks of prose on every one of its ten rows - **9,703 characters with every word out, and 1,944 for Coding alone** - so the list read as one wall of text and the presets looked alike. A row now opens with its title (CHOSEN mark included), the `focus` line, the model/lane line, a heavy preset's cost sentence, the blocker when there is one, and the "Use this" button; `what`, the second-worker line, "What it is for:" and "What it is worse at:" wait behind one "Why this one" / "Hide why" tap **per preset**. Nothing was removed: every word is still drawn once a row is opened, and the closed list is 1,752 characters instead of 9,703. No route, no contract and no desktop surface changed, and the whole phone unit suite (`.\gradlew testDebugUnitTest --offline`) is green.
- **The General preset stops claiming the model "answered nothing" without thinking (2026-11-15).** The preset's own caveat said the model's thinking "has to stay off for ordinary turns, or it answered nothing in the measured run". That is measured false: with the benchmark suites' 1,024-token answer budget, `qwen3.5:9b` answered 6/6 general, 5/5 tool-calling and 1/1 vision, and the old sentence came from a harness that asked for 64 tokens and recorded its own budget running out as the model failing. The caveat now says the true thing - a thinking turn spends the answer's own budget on its reasoning first, so a very small budget can come back empty - and the generated preset contract both apps render was regenerated from the source rather than hand-edited. The same branch records two measured live defects without repairing them: DEF-071, the Coding preset advertising a 49,152-token window while the running lane measured 8,192, and DEF-072, an approved `github_merge_pr` card that merged nothing and reported nothing; and three more from the same live GitHub read run, filed for `gh-robust` and not repaired here - DEF-073, `github_ci_status` calling pull request #1263 "passed" while `audit` and `backend-shard (3/4)` were red, DEF-074, the `github_list` scope `runs` that can never answer because its 20-run body is 273,833 characters against a 200,000-byte read, and DEF-075, a `github_read_file` of a directory that reports the cut sentence instead of "That path is a directory, not a file" (three further findings from that run were already repaired by the unmerged PR #1264 and are noted in the rows rather than filed).
- **The preflight now says which commit the desktop, the backend and `main` each came from, in one row (2026-11-15).** Three pieces of this program can be at three different commits — the desktop app, the live backend folder and the branch every release is built from — and until now nothing said so out loud: a deploy could land half of a change and every check would still read green. The new preflight row is *"Which commit did each piece come from?"* and it prints the three short ids on one line: identical ids are a PASS, and ids that disagree are a WARN that names which piece is behind rather than just failing. It reads only the refs already on the PC (`git rev-parse`, so an offline PC answers and nothing is fetched), and a folder that is not a git checkout, or a PC with no git at all, says so instead of naming a guessed sha. Nine lines of `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §5 say the same. Proved by `backend/test_selftest_preflight.py`, which drives the row three ways: all three agree, the backend is behind, and the ref cannot be read.
- **The all-features list stops promising a typed path that already works (DEF-038, 2026-11-15).** `tools/gen_feature_directory.py` stamped "Settings control today; typed path still being wired." on every planned row a multi-field board named, without ever asking whether the row's own sentence resolved, so the desktop's "All features and abilities" list promised a gap that had already closed: measured on origin/main `3beaa66b9`, 18 rows carried the note and **all 18** of their own example sentences resolved through the real matcher. The note is now COMPUTED from that sentence - through the generator's own `_resolves()` - and printed only while the sentence does not resolve, so a board can never stamp it again; both generated files were regenerated and only the 18 note lines change. After the fix **0** rows carry the note while all 32 noted rows still show a note, because the 18 fall back to the contract's own `label_note`, so no row lost its words and the nine "Still being wired (owner: ...)" rows are untouched. `tools/check_feature_controls.py` now reads the printed page back, takes `PLANNED_NOTE` and `_resolves` from that generator itself (no retyped string, no second copy of the rule), and fails any row that carries the note while its example phrase resolves - pointed at the pre-fix generated file it fails on all 18 rows by name. A new bite case in `backend/test_feature_controls.py` gives an enforced row the note and fails, while the old checker accepts the same tree (exit 0), so the case really bites. Nothing under `jarvis-client/` changed: the phone's generated list carries no such note at all, and the two apps no longer disagree about the same contract row.
- **The phone tells Jarvis which phone it is, so answers can be phone specific (2026-11-15).** The Android app now sends `X-Jarvis-Device` beside the two headers it already sent: the handset's model, Android version, screen size and app build, in one bounded line of five known keys. The shipped gate that every request already passes reads it once, and the one system sentence the model is given names the phone and asks for an answer sized to it. Without the header - the desktop, an older app, a script - every answer is byte-for-byte what it was.
- **Deleting a conversation on the phone now asks the PC first, and nothing is deleted until you approve its card (2026-11-15, DEF-047):** the History screen's Delete still showed its own "are you sure?" but the request went to the old uncarded `POST /api/history/delete`, so the two-phase approval card its own words described was never raised - an irreversible action was presented as gated when it was not, against the owner's non-negotiable that the app never auto-approves anything. Delete now posts the carded `POST /api/conversations/clear` (one conversation id, and nothing else): the PC raises ONE `conversation_clear` approval card naming that chat, its message count, that it cannot be undone, that the facts Jarvis learned are KEPT and that older backups age out, and answers 202 `waiting: true` - which the phone reads as a waiting card, says so, and keeps the row. When the card leaves the queue the list is read again from the PC: still there means the answer was no and the phone says "Not deleted", gone means it was approved and only then does the phone say "Deleted from your PC". The confirm's one sentence now says a card comes first, and a PC whose Jarvis is older than the app (a 404 with no route) deletes nothing and says to update it rather than falling back to the uncarded route.
- **The phone's API contracts are proven on the JVM, so a broken route fails a check that is required to merge (2026-11-15).** `ApiContractTest`, `EventStreamContractTest` and `PicturesConfirmContractTest` moved from `app/src/androidTest` to `app/src/test`: 44 tests that assert which route, which header and which body one tap produces, and none of that needed a phone. They used to need one because `JarvisApi` took `ClientSettings` and `TokenStore` directly and both want an Android `Context`; it now takes two one-method interfaces instead - `HostSource` (`baseUrl`, `baseProblem`) and `TokenSource` (`token`), which those two classes already implement - and the suites answer with `FakeHost` and `FakeTokens`. `FakeHost` normalises and judges the address with the same `BaseUrl.normalise` and `PhoneAddress.problem` the app calls, so a test address is measured by the app's own rule, with one deliberate difference: `allowLoopback = true`, because the suite talks to a MockWebServer on 127.0.0.1. The point is which job runs them: the emulator job lives in `Jarvis client`, which is path-filtered on `pull_request` and is not one of the seven required checks, while `testDebugUnitTest` runs in the required `phone-unit-tests` job on every pull request. Two things were needed to make the move real, both measured rather than assumed: the three suites set their host to `127.0.0.1` instead of `server.hostName`, because on a plain computer that name is the machine's own DNS name (here `kubernetes.docker.internal`) and `PhoneAddress` refuses it as off-network - that alone failed 41 of the 44 tests - and `org.json:json:20240303` is now a `testImplementation`, because `testOptions.unitTests.isReturnDefaultValues = true` makes android.jar's `org.json` stub answer null instead of parsing, which failed the other 8. Full JVM suite after both fixes: 3,943 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped. The Keystore path is still tested on a device, by `TokenStoreTest`.
- **The phone stops printing a command it cannot run, and stops explaining an Android 17 slider on an Android 15 phone (2026-11-15).** The 2026-11-15 audit of the app on the OnePlus measured the two longest pieces of copy that cannot be acted on where they are drawn. Brain -> Hardware printed **565 characters of PowerShell in full on every visit** - the single longest thing on any phone screen - while its own note underneath says the line is for the PC and that the desktop app's Copy button is what runs it; it now sits behind one "Show the command" tap, with that pointer line always visible, so nothing is lost and the plate opens at one line. Settings' Voice section printed a paragraph about **Android 17's per-assistant volume slider on a phone that reports Android 15** (SDK 35), where that slider does not exist, so the owner was told to look for a control that could not be there; it is now drawn only from **API 37**. The desktop app is untouched, no route changed, and the whole phone unit suite (`.\gradlew testDebugUnitTest --offline`) is green.
- **Create, find by alias, and append a dated entry in Obsidian notes (2026-11-15).** Three measured failures in the owner's vault are fixed. First, "Make a new note for me that's called my workout log and pin it and remember ..." appended the TAIL of the sentence to that day's daily note and created no note: `jarvis_quick._NOTE_TEXT_SPACE` saw "note", took every word after it, and `_CREATE_NOTE_HEAD` did not read "that's called". The sentence is now a `note_create` (`_CREATE_NOTE_HEAD` accepts "for me that's called" / "that is called"), the daily-note pattern refuses any create-shaped text (two guards), and the "remember that ..." clause is not written into the note. Second, the 2026-11-08 sentence produced a 0-byte file named after the whole sentence; `_NOTE_CREATE_NAMED` still took every word after "called" as the title, so a title that is really a sentence (a comma or semicolon, a continuing clause, or more than twelve words) is now refused with a plain request for the name, and the create path checks it before any file is made. Third, "add to the workout log that today I did light cardio" got no lookup at all: a new `_NOTE_APPEND_TO_THAT` shape resolves the note and appends the words under a `## YYYY-MM-DD` heading, creating it when missing and keeping days newest last. The registry is the note's own YAML `aliases:` list, which Obsidian reads natively: `jarvis_notes_edit.find_name()` reads exact path (only when a path is named), then an exact alias, then the title, then a title that contains the words; an alias beats a file-name lookalike, and two matches ask instead of guessing. In the owner's real vault "my workout log", "the workout log" and "workout log" all resolve to `Private & Shared/Workout/Workout Log.md` - read-only, with no model and no earlier conversation - even though an unrelated root file is also called `Workout log.md`. A new note lands beside the note its name points at (`Private & Shared/Workout/` for "my workout log") and in the vault root when nothing matches; a collision is a 409 before any card and never an overwrite. The dated append accepts an optional `"dated": "YYYY-MM-DD"` on `POST /api/notes/append`, asks exactly ONE `edit_vault_note` card, takes the File Guardian copy first, and writes by INSERTION only: a true `O_APPEND` when the block belongs at the end, a checked splice otherwise, so no existing byte is rewritten. `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §170.12 records all of it. `backend/test_notes_create_find_append.py` proves it on a temporary vault with a fake gate (94 checks); the existing notes suites are unchanged and green (83 + 146 + 215 + 29 + 27 + 120 + 80 + 144 + 58 + 116 + 30 + 29).
- **The spoken-interruption mute switch now lives beside the numbers it changes, on Brain's Attention budget, and the Inbox keeps only its count line (2026-11-15).** The switch used to sit on a card in the Inbox, while the numbers it acts on - the spoken interruptions left, the daily limit and the "Muted until tomorrow" pill - are all on Brain's Attention budget plate, so one setting had two homes. Nothing else changes: the Inbox's one line still says how many spoken interruptions are left, the quick-settings tile still toggles the same setting, and there is still no mute-forever.
- **The phone's Measure line no longer contradicts the dated lines above it, and the audit that found it is now in the repository (2026-11-15).** The Measure block ended *"Not measured yet: every number above is calculated"* while the preset rows directly above it print *"Measured 2026-10-18: cold load 18.5-20.5 s, 45.6 tokens a second at 8k"* - two statements about the same screen, both drawn as current fact. It now reads *"Not measured by this check yet; any dated line above is an older measurement"*, which is true whether or not a dated line is present. The audit itself (`docs/AUDIT-2026-11-15-ATLAS-ANDROID-PHONE.md`) - 801 labelled rows, 52,367 characters of copy, the duplicate surfaces and the three contradictions, captured screen by screen over `adb` on the connected OnePlus - is committed here so the findings outlive a Downloads folder, with its own status block naming what has since been fixed (phone-awareness, the un-runnable command, the Android 17 caveat) and what has not (the presets' prose, the duplicate controls, which card runs the model).
- **The History sidebar's per-chat menu draws at normal size again, and every chat can now be exported as Markdown or copied as plain text (2026-11-15).** The owner photographed that menu: each icon was enormous and every label was clipped to two or three characters ("O…", "Pin …", "Move t…", "Arc…"). The measured cause was CSS, not the markup - `hud-history.js` builds every menu icon through one `icon()` helper that sets only `class="glyph"`, `viewBox` and no width or height, and the `.hh-menu` rules had no `.glyph` rule at all, so each SVG fell back to the replaced-element default of 300x150 and flex-shrank until the label had a few pixels. Every other glyph on the page already has its own size (`.hh-head .glyph{width:13px;height:13px}`, `.history-open .glyph{...}`); the fix is the missing rule, `.hh-menu .glyph{width:16px;height:16px;flex:0 0 auto;}`, in the same stylesheet block as the other `.hh-menu` rules, so the row menu, the "Move to project" submenu, the delete confirmation rows and the archived list's menu all read as icon + label again. The same menu now offers **Export as Markdown** and **Copy transcript** on every chat, on the live list and on the archived one (an archived chat can still be read out): Export writes ONE Markdown file into the owner's Downloads folder and says its full path in the panel's own status line, numbering a repeat (" (2)", " (3)") rather than overwriting, handling a title of Windows-forbidden characters (`\ / : * ? " < > |`) and a chat with no messages; Copy puts the same transcript on the clipboard as plain text through `navigator.writeText` - the same call the answer menu's "Copy answer" makes - so there is no HTML flavour and no dialog. Both actions read the chat through the **same** `/api/history/conversation?id=` request Open already makes and change nothing on screen; the words are only ever written to Downloads (one new narrow command, `hud_history_export`, granted in the HUD's existing `hud-history` set, no new capability set, no route, no network request, no approval card) and it is refused while "Hide memory lists" or App lock is on. The labels live in `history-actions.js`'s one `ACTION_LABELS` table, and the menu's height clamp moved from 280 to 360 so the two extra rows stay on screen. The Brain's History tab and the phone deliberately get neither item - the Brain builds its own row actions from a different path and the phone has no such panel, so there is nothing to wire (ARCHITECTURE.md §8; `tools/check_parity.py` clean) - and a plain browser, served by the backend, has no file writer, so Export there says it needs the desktop app while Copy still works. Proved by 52 checks in `jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-history.mjs` (the new menu items on both lists, the filename rule for every forbidden character, the empty-chat export, the copied text carrying no markup, the reused read, and the Rust command's presence in the handler, the manifest and the HUD's set) plus three Rust unit tests for the name rule and the numbering; the drawing itself is CI's Playwright `hud.mjs`, which cannot run here (no Playwright installed).

They never were: Ollama's default server uses one card (its log: "found 1 CUDA devices ... RTX 2080 SUPER") while a second Ollama lane serves the RTX 2060. `jarvis_hardware._found_sentence()` now appends one plain clause - "This is the default Ollama server's lane; a preset on another card names that card in its own row." - and nothing else moved: no count, no card name and no other sentence changed, and the clause sits before the existing "Ollama's log was not found" sentence, so that one still ends the line when the log is missing. `tools/gen_hardware_cases.py` regenerated the desktop and phone golden fixtures (its `--check` confirms them against the real code), so `backend/test_hardware.py` and both apps' contract tests read the new words.
- **The grant engine behind "one plan card per job" and trusted mode exists, and is wired to nothing yet (2026-11-15):** `backend/jarvis_grants.py` and its byte-identical `jarvis-backend/` copy hold the owner's two new permission modes as pure logic with an injectable clock. `PlanGrant` is one card naming every write a job may make - repository, pull request or branch, file, and for a merge the pinned head commit - and a write it did not name, or a target that moved, raises a new card; a divergence voids the rest of the plan. `TrustedSession` is the one-hour GitHub-only window, opened by one card: an exact eleven-action allowlist (comment, open_issue, rerun_workflow, create_repo, merge_pr only with passing checks and a pinned head, fix_and_push, open_pull_request, issue_labels, edit_pr, pr_review never an APPROVE, issue_state), 20 uses per action by default with a hard ceiling of 30, expiring at exactly sixty minutes, dying with the process that opened it (no disk, no setting, no way to recover one), voided the moment the event stream goes stale, never answering a card that was already waiting, and refusing each of the owner's nine banned verbs even when an allowed tool carries the banned thing as an argument (`method="squash"`, `event="APPROVE"`, `force=True`). The cap is a resolved value, not a constant: a caller may name one for one session (clamped to 30), otherwise the owner's `[grants].max_actions` setting decides (declared as `jarvis_limits.LIMITS["trusted_actions"]`, 1..30, shipped at 20), otherwise 20 - and it is resolved when a window OPENS, so changing the setting reaches the next window and never one already open. The engine only READS that setting: changing it is the existing limits route's gate action, and the chat and Jarvis Live sentences that name it arrive with the wiring PR. The three audit events are not copied: one lazy call writes `jarvis_gate`'s own `grant_made` / `granted` / `grant_ended`, and a window that cannot be logged is refused rather than opened unlogged. Nothing imports the module and no caller reads it; the card words, the chat sentences, the gate's one call and the bar in both apps are a later pull request. Evidence: `backend/test_grants.py` proves each rule against an injected clock and a stand-in gate - the 20-use boundary and the 21st refusal, the 99-to-30 clamp, the caller/setting/20 resolution order and a setting change reaching only new windows, each banned verb, all eleven allowed shapes, a file write not covered, a pending card not swallowed, a stale stream voiding the window, the sixty-minute boundary, a restart, a pinned-head mismatch and a closed window never reopening.
- **A question that names Gmail is answered about email, not about the calendar (2026-11-15).** The owner asked the phone *"how do I connect a Gmail account to you?"* and got the four-path account inventory, which opened with **"Your calendar is not connected on this PC yet"**, listed the Google two-way setup, the private iCal link and GitHub, and reached email only as its fourth line - calling it **"not built yet"**. Two things were wrong with that: it answered three questions he did not ask, and email is not unbuilt - the desktop's Settings, Accounts collects the IMAP server, port, mailbox, username and password (`jarvis-desktop/src/account-secrets.js`, `jarvis_accounts.py`), and `jarvis_email` reads the inbox with them. What is missing is a connect card for email on the **phone**, which is a different fact. A sentence that names email or Gmail and not the calendar now routes to a new `accounts_email` answer: whether this PC has a mail server saved, the boxes to fill for Gmail (`imap.gmail.com`, 993, `INBOX`, your Gmail address), the **app-password** rule that Google really enforces over IMAP with 2-step verification on - said as Google's rule and not as a measurement of his account - what it then enables, and the one place the password may go, which is a box on the PC and never the chat. The four-path answer is unchanged for every calendar or mixed sentence, and `test_hud_fieldtest_answers.py` now holds both shapes apart (567 checks), with `test_calendar_answer.py` (159) and `test_connect_account.py` (272) updated to the new rule.
- **The GitHub tools are a switch you can say, ask about, and change by talking.** The twenty-tool master switch had a card and a writer but no spoken name, so "turn on the GitHub tools" reached the AI model, which offered to raise a card it had no door to raise, and "what GitHub tools are switched on" was answered "I don't have access to a list of which GitHub tools are currently switched on for you" — a denial of a fact this PC holds. Now the group is a name in the registry's closed-world tool table (a single tool's own name still wins), the switch grammar accepts the plural "tools", and "enable the github tools" is no longer answered as a request to save a token. "What is enabled" has its own short answer — the live count from `jarvis_asks_first.tools_status`, then the exact sentence that changes it — and it never offers to switch on what is already on. ON is still ONE card plus Windows Hello and writes nothing until a person answers; OFF is still instant and cardless. A model-driven `change_setting` call reaches the same group card, and only that one: every single-tool switch keeps its two existing doors. (`backend/test_github_tools_by_chat.py` pins all of it, plus the provenance rule that made the first readings of this measure the model instead of the fast path.)
- **The GitHub tool layer refuses hostile input, bounds every answer, and cannot report a false green (2026-11-15).** A new adversarial suite (`backend/test_github_robustness.py`, 511 checks) drives every GitHub planner and the transport boundary with the arguments and answers a hostile model or a hostile network would produce, and it fixed what it proved. Refused now, in one plain sentence and before anything is sent: a repository named `owner/..` (a path step in the URL, not a repository), the direction-override characters that make one line draw as another in a title, body, review, label, commit message or reason, an issue, pull request or run number of 0, and a branch written as `refs/heads/main`, `HEAD`, `main/`, `main.` or `feature/.secret`. Every request is checked against the module's own `https://api.github.com/` prefix at the boundary, so a step built with `@evil.example/x` is refused before a socket opens. No answer is a silent empty list any more: a cut 481-file `pulls/{n}/files` list says what was left out, an unreadable list says it could not be read, a captive-portal page is not "no pull requests", a binary file is not shown as mojibake, and a redirect is named as the reason the token is never followed. Three defects proven against real GitHub the same day are fixed too: a pull request's CI answer now reads the head commit's checks and cannot say "passed" while `audit` is red, the runs list asks for five runs instead of twenty so the scope can answer at all, and reading a directory says it is a directory even when the listing is cut. A 403 rate limit that carries `Retry-After` now says how long to wait. And the pull request scan (`github_pr_scan`) names the checks that are not green on each row instead of only the aggregate one: `blocked - backend finished as failure; also not a success on that commit: audit (failure), backend-shard (3/4) (failure)`, at most three names and then "and N more", and never "running" about a commit whose checks have already failed.
- **One renderer answers both CI questions, so a branch and a pull request can no longer describe the same red check two ways (2026-11-15).** `backend/jarvis_github.py` answered "which checks are red, which are still running" twice - `_ci_words` for a branch or repository read and `_pr_ci_words` for a pull request - and two functions answering one question is how two answers drift apart. There is now ONE: `_ci_words`, parameterised by the evidence the caller has. `who` names the commit and selects the commit sentences, `checks_doc` hands it that commit's own check runs, and a branch or repository read passes neither and judges the newest run. Both call sites in `_ci_result` use it. `_scan_checks` already decided red/running for both and `_ci_failed_lines` already named the failing checks for both; a new `_red_lines` prepares that evidence the same way for every failed-commit sentence. Every user-visible sentence is unchanged, proven by driving the OLD module from `HEAD` side by side with the new one over 695 sentence pairs - both forms, every status and conclusion, every evidence shape, every check/runs combination: all 695 identical. The two old renderers did disagree on 30 of those pairs, and both wordings are kept because the evidence really differs: a pull request with no readable check runs judges every run on its commit ("More than one CI run is on the head commit of ... and at least one did not finish successfully") where the branch form reports only the newest run, and an unreadable runs answer says "GitHub answered without saying anything about CI" to a branch but "There is no recent CI run there to report" to a pull request. Those differences are now one named parameter instead of two code paths that could each be edited alone. `backend/test_github_tools.py` gains `t_one_renderer_answers_both_ci_questions` (10 checks): the module defines exactly ONE CI-word renderer and `_pr_ci_words` is gone, a stand-in that answers a sentinel is what BOTH questions answer back (the pull request case is a red check the old pair never shared), the same evidence gives the same sentence character for character, and the one failing-detail renderer serves both - and 5 of its 10 checks fail against the two-renderer code. Local proof on this tree: `test_github_tools.py` 1010 passed / 0 skipped / 0 failed, `test_github_parity.py` 705 passed / 0 failed, `tools/check_stale_twins.py` all 342 files matching (343 repository copies compared), `test_base_matches_repo.py` 140 passed / 0 failed, with `test_github_robustness.py` 511, `test_github_self_knowledge.py` 166, `test_tool_profiles.py` 115 and `test_self_code.py` 95 also green. `backend/jarvis_github.py` and `jarvis-backend/jarvis_github.py` are byte-identical again.
- **The GitHub fix-flow cards say what they will do, and refuse a pull request they cannot push to (2026-11-15).** Two of the nine defects the fix-flow field test measured were the kind that cannot be seen until they happen: the push card did not say which host the saved key reaches, and a marker branch that is not a valid ref could reach a push card at all. The prepare, write and push cards now name both hosts in plain words - `api.github.com` for GitHub's API, `github.com` for the clone, fetch and push - so the two the key reaches are the two the card states. A pull request that is already merged or closed is refused before the clone, and a branch name that is not a valid ref is refused before a push card exists. The git timeout is raised to 900 s after measured clones of 257-297 s, a failed copy is retried and, if it is still there, named for the owner to delete; and checks that had not finished when the folder was prepared are now named as unfinished instead of being reported as no failures, which is the difference between "nothing failed" and "nobody knows yet". The write and push cards also carry the pull request's title and base branch, the exact push command with `HEAD` and `refs/heads` said in plain words, and how to abandon the change.
- **The feature matrix checker can no longer pass while 18 planned rows already work (DEF-037, 2026-11-15).** `tools/check_feature_controls.py` promised that "a planned grammar gap that has since been fixed is a FAILURE", and never checked it: a planned row was asked only for a known owner and its desktop or phone evidence, so 18 rows kept saying "planned" while `jarvis_quick.match` resolved their own displayed sentences to their own keys, and the checker printed `OK` and exited 0. It now re-runs every planned row's displayed phrases through the same matcher an enforced row goes through, and fails when one already changes the row's own control. The 18 measured rows are named in a `STALE_PLANNED` ratchet: they are reported by name on every green run, the set may only shrink, and a row that starts working outside it fails on the spot. Two new bite cases pin both edges - new staleness fails, and a recorded row that gets fixed fails too. Reclassifying the 18 rows to `enforced` remains DEF-037's own work, in the phone pass.
- **Both feature-directory generators now run in CI, and the phone's directory is no longer stale (2026-11-15).** The `audit` job gains two read-only steps - `python3 ../../tools/gen_feature_directory.py --check` (the desktop's "Abilities & commands" directory, `jarvis-desktop/src/feature-directory.js` and its fixture) and `python3 ../../jarvis-client/tools/gen_feature_directory.py --check` (the phone's `FeatureDirectory.kt`) - and each failure now prints the exact one-line command that clears it (`py -3 tools/gen_feature_directory.py` and commit the two files it writes; `py -3 jarvis-client/tools/gen_feature_directory.py` and commit the one file it writes) instead of "run this generator". `audit` is informational and gates no merge; it is the job whose own contract is "reads only the repository", and this is a tripwire that goes red on the merge that drifts a directory rather than a week later. The gate earned its keep before it was even wired: run on a clean worktree of `origin/main` `3beaa66b9` the phone's check exited 1, because `052072133` ("Jarvis knows every paired device") moved a `where` sentence in `contract/feature-controls.json` and re-ran no writer - so `FeatureDirectory.kt` still described the old Devices row, and its android-builder row still said there was no way in after the `android_app` tool had become one. The row count had not changed, so nothing noticed; that is exactly what the count cross-check in `FeatureDirectoryTest.kt` cannot see. The file is regenerated in this same change, by its own generator and never by hand, and only those two rows move (2 lines, +2/-2). - **An approved GitHub card now merges, or says in code's words why it did not (2026-11-15).** Last night an approved `github_merge_pr` card for pull request #1261 executed nothing, and the explanation the owner got was invented. The model had echoed a head commit from an earlier scan, so the card pinned a commit that was not the pull request's head; the run correctly refused it, said "the pull request moved since you looked" (false - its head had not moved), and the only account that reached the owner was the model's own, which described a duplicate-call rule that does not exist. Three things change. `github_merge_pr` can be called with just the repository and the pull request number: Jarvis then reads the pull request itself, pins the head commit GitHub reports, and the card shows that exact commit - approve it and it merges, with the pin still re-checked at run time. A `head_sha` that IS supplied but is not the pull request's head is refused before any card is raised, in plain words naming both commits, instead of becoming an approval that cannot merge. And when an approved GitHub write's run fails, Jarvis puts the module's own reason into the answer itself, so the owner reads the real cause and not only the model's account of it. Nothing is auto-approved, there is still one card per action, and the merge is still pinned to one exact 40-character commit.

The tested limit is unchanged: no email has reached a real mail server, and §26.5's bullet saying so is untouched.

- **Send a video from your PC to your phone (2026-11-14).** The ceiling on a file sent from the desktop to the phone rises from **10 MiB to 2 GiB**, and a **"Send to my phone…"** button in Settings → folders starts one by opening a normal file dialog. You pick the file, approve ONE card that names it, and the phone finds it in Settings → "File from your PC" and saves it to Downloads. The file travels in 1 MB pieces, so a long video shows a progress line instead of one long wait, a dropped connection can retry the same piece instead of starting over, and a transfer only counts as done when the last piece arrives — the phone checks the whole file's SHA-256 before it saves anything. Nothing is downloadable until you approve the card, the card is still one per file and cannot be turned into a standing yes, and no file path ever reaches the phone. Files from the phone to the PC already had the 2 GB ceiling since 2026-11-13.

- **Three GitHub reads now hand the model real data instead of a guess: a state filter on `github_list`, the actual unified diff in `github_pr_detail`, and the failing checks by name in `github_ci_status` - plus a measured "Changed files (0)" bug that was hiding a pull request's whole file list (2026-11-14).** `github_list` already had `issues` as a scope; it now takes a `state` filter for `pulls` and `issues` - a closed set of three names (`open`, the default, so every older caller reads what it read before; `closed`; `all`), checked on every scope before any address is built and refused by name when it is not one of the three, with a state on `repos`/`runs` refused rather than silently dropped. `github_ci_status` names every failing check ("rust: failure") instead of only saying the run failed, and shows ONE bounded excerpt (at most 2,000 characters) of the FIRST failing check's log; the run's jobs are one extra fixed GET, made only when the newest run failed, and the log is the same `_job_log` read the fix flow uses - the 302 is read, never followed, and the signed address is fetched with NO Authorization header. `github_pr_detail` shows the changed files' own `patch` (the unified diff) between the one sanitizer's data delimiters, bounded to 20 files and 60,000 characters, with ONE line naming exactly what was left out (files past the cap, files whose diff found no room, and binary/too-large files GitHub sends no patch for). **The bug the field test found is fixed and pinned.** At 23:17 PT the live app read PR #1261, returned the right head commit and base branch, and reported "Number of files changed: 0" while `gh pr view 1261 --json files` said 61 files. Measured with `gh api`: that files answer is **481,180 bytes for 61 files** (GitHub puts every file's `patch` in it), the read layer stops at `MAX_BYTES` (200,000) and marks the answer cut, a cut answer cannot be parsed, and `_read` returned it as "no document, no error" - so `files` became an empty list and the count came from its length. Now a cut answer is an ERROR rather than an empty document, the changed-files page is 20 (178,021 bytes for this PR, under the cap) and is retried at 10 / 5 / 1 if even that is cut, and the count always comes from the pull request's own `changed_files` field - so a page that could not hold every file can never read as zero. Nothing was loosened: no auto-merge, no gist, no admin bypass, and the token is still never printed, logged, put in a git argument or written to a file. `backend/jarvis_tool_profiles.py`'s dossiers now say what the tools really do: the issue-label dossier no longer claims closing an issue is "permanently banned ... no code path" (the owner's 2026-11-10 23:00 decision made `github_issue_state` close ONE issue on its own card), and the CI dossier no longer says "Jarvis never reads the failing log - GitHub keeps it". `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §190.1/§216.1 records the widening and the 481 KB measurement. Tests: four new functions in `backend/test_github_tools.py` (state filter incl. the closed set and the issue list; the real bounded diff; the cut-page regression driven with a REAL cut answer from `_capped_text`, never a typed marker; the failing-check names and the one log excerpt) and one in `backend/test_tool_profiles.py` that reads its numbers from the code's own `MAX_DIFF_FILES`/`MAX_DIFF_CHARS`; each fails on `origin/main` and passes here. The sentence that points a failed run at the fix flow now asks the owner to "fix and push" in plain words instead of naming the raw tool id, so it stays out of the zero-jargon ratchet.

- **The benchmark can no longer record a thinking model as an empty answer (2026-11-14).** `backend/jarvis_bench.py` asked four of its five suites for 64, 64, 48 and 400 tokens, and a thinking model spends that whole budget on its hidden reasoning before it writes anything: measured on this PC, `qwen3.5:9b` asked "How many days are in a leap year? Reply with only the number." came back `done_reason: "length"` with an empty `response` and 266 characters in the separate `thinking` field, so every model scored 0/6 general, 0/5 tool-calling and 0/1 vision, and every scorecard read `answered ''` - the harness failing, recorded as a model failure. The general, tool-calling and vision suites now ask for `ANSWER_TOKENS = 1024` and coding for `CODE_TOKENS = 1200`; with 512 tokens the same model answered "366" in 201 tokens. A budget that runs out is now named as the budget running out, in the suite's reason, in the per-task reason and in the coding suite's "no code" sentence, and `answer_tokens` travels with the result and the stored scorecard so a reader can see the terms it was measured under. It is still a failure, never a skip: a model that cannot answer a one-line question within the budget has not answered it. Tests: `backend/test_bench_suites.py`, the new `t_a_cut_off_thinking_reply_is_the_budget_running_out` and `t_every_answering_suite_asks_for_thinking_room`. The General preset's own `worse` line said its thinking had to stay off `or it answered nothing in the measured run` - that was the old 64-token allowance talking, not the model; it now says thinking is on and names the 1,024-token allowance every window gets, with the 6/6 general, 5/5 tool-calling and 1/1 vision results behind it (owner ruling Q5, 2026-11-15).
- **The desktop's own copy says Atlas, and the Android builder finally has a way in (2026-11-14).** The Brain window's headings, view labels, notes, tooltips and button labels now say Atlas (15 files, prose and its test pins together), the tray's offline sentence reads "Atlas is not running at …" instead of "Jarvis is not running", and six places that told the owner there was no entry point now describe the one that exists: a model tool `android_app` with `build` and `install`, **one approval card per act**, which ships switched off under Settings → Raw and powerful. `DEF-068` stays **open** — the tool exists and 118 checks prove it, but nothing has been built or installed on real hardware, and a screen is not a test. The model writes data and never code: the whole spec is checked against closed key sets before a byte of the project exists, so an unknown key, a ninth screen, a screen id outside the pattern, or a button that opens a screen that does not exist is refused with a sentence rather than drawn. A task that carries no `app.json` is the WebView app it has always been, and the task's own files choose the kind, so there is no flag that can drift out of step. Measured on this PC: a real `gradlew.bat assembleDebug` through the module's own build path, **BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 23s**, a **2,479,127-byte** debug APK, sha256 `4BA8FD8718067FE117E391F28E121738D2A3DB98675FD91B99C3727319D9159F`. It is not, and the feature list says so: turn it on in Settings, Voice (that raises ONE approval card on the PC), then tap Listen on the phone; turning it off is instant, and the phone's listening is never on by default or after a restart. - **The undo notice after an approved card times out after 15 seconds (2026-11-13):** the owner asked for the notification that says an action cannot be undone to disappear by itself. Before this, the one sentence `JarvisRuntime.decide` puts up after an approval (`"This cannot be undone."`, or a shorter sibling such as "Inbox tidy: 10 minutes to undo.") stayed on screen until something else replaced it. It now goes through `JarvisRuntime.showUndoNotice`, which keeps one 15-second timer (`UNDO_NOTICE_TIMEOUT_MS`), clears the notice only while it is still that same sentence (so an old timer can never wipe a newer, different notice), and restarts the 15 seconds when the same sentence is set again. Every other notice caller is unchanged: error and problem notices still persist until dismissed or replaced. Covered by the new `UndoNoticeTimeoutTest` in the phone's JVM suite - still up at 14.9 s, gone at 15.0 s, a newer notice survives an older timer, a repeated sentence restarts its own 15 s, and an error notice opens no timer - with the full suite green at 3,672 tests, 0 failures. A mutation that changes the timeout to 15.001 s and removes the identity check turns three of those tests red, so the assertions are live. No device was driven and the app on the owner's phone was not touched, so the visual behaviour on the handset stays unverified until the CI APK is installed.

- **A photo can be sent from your phone into "From my phone", exactly as a document is (2026-11-13).** The owner asked Jarvis on his phone to "send this file which was a photo to the computer" and was told Jarvis could not send files between devices at all. That sentence was false about documents and, until now, true about photos: Settings, Folders Jarvis may look in, then "Send a document" opened the eight document types only. The row is now "Send a document or a photo" and its picker also offers JPG, JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, HEIF, GIF and BMP. A photo takes the SAME route as a document, lands in the same "From my phone" folder inside the folder you already listed, unchanged byte for byte, behind the same ONE card on the PC and the same 50 MB cap - no new route and no new approval. It is a plain file copy: on this path Jarvis does not open the picture, does not read words from it, does not run vision on it and does not show it to a model; only its first few bytes are checked, to be sure it really is a picture. - **The phone can now save its own settings to a locked file, and an update download is checked against a checksum published with the build (2026-11-13, the copy-over wave; adapted from Mobile-Harness, MIT).** Settings -> "Phone settings backup" writes THIS PHONE'S settings - the face and colours, the menus shown, the voice and display switches, which apps Jarvis may open, and which apps may tell Jarvis about a notification - into one password-locked file through Android's own document picker, and restores them onto a new or wiped phone. The file is a versioned container: a small plaintext header, then the typed settings snapshot cut into AES-256-GCM segments bound to their index and a final marker (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 210,000 rounds, a fresh salt per file; `jarvis-client/.../data/EncryptedBackup.kt` and `data/SettingsBackup.kt`, adapted from Mobile-Harness's `BackupCrypto.kt` under MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Mobile Harness Contributors, credited in THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt and the APK's own notices). **The pairing token is provably not in it:** it lives in a different preferences file, that file is not on the backup's list, the writer only walks the listed files, and the reader refuses a snapshot naming any file it does not back up - so a restored phone pairs again, exactly as after a reinstall. Chats, saved memories, pictures, caches and logs are excluded for the same reason, and a wrong password, a tampered byte, a truncated file, a foreign file and a newer format each fail closed with plain words and leave the phone untouched; the whole file authenticates before a single preference is written. Separately, the phone's existing update download now also reads `client-latest.json`, which `jarvis-client.yml` publishes beside the `client-latest` APK with the APK's `sha256` and `sizeBytes`, and it is offered for install only when the downloaded file matches BOTH that checksum and the signing certificate pinned in the app (`jarvis-client/.../update/ApkUpdater.kt`, adapted from Mobile-Harness's `AppUpdater.kt` under MIT). The manifest is fetched before the APK, so an unreadable checksum downloads nothing and reports "could not check", never "up to date"; a mismatch is deleted with the reason shown; nothing downloads without the owner's tap and nothing installs itself - the install step is still Android's own installer prompt. Limits, said on the screens: a forgotten backup password cannot be recovered, and restoring needs the app reopened before every screen shows the new values. Neither feature adds a route or sends anything to the PC, so `tools/check_parity.py` classifies nothing new; the docs are `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 222 and the one-sided note in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8. JVM tests: `EncryptedBackupTest` (round trip of every value type, wrong password, tamper, truncation, foreign/unencrypted file, newer container and snapshot, unknown file/type refused, token absence from plaintext and ciphertext, source pins) and `ApkUpdaterTest` (strict manifest parse, URL policy, sha256/size/wrong-file refusals, "no installer code", Install drawn only for Ready, and CI's manifest fields and versionCode pinned to `build.gradle.kts`). No new third-party dependency was added.
- **The phone can run a small AI model on itself, in its own Local AI screen (2026-11-13).** A `.gguf` model you put on the phone answers there with no PC and no internet, behind a switch that ships OFF. The screen says "On-device model: runs on this phone, not your PC", never downloads a model, never loads one until you tap Load, tells you before you load it whether the phone has room, and shows each reply's measured tokens per second or says "not measured". The field test on the owner's phone (2026-11-13) drove the real screen: Qwen2.5-0.5B, 1.5B and 3B Q4_K_M each answered `Hello, who are you?`, at 27.1, 13.8 and 7.7 tokens per second as shown on the screen and matched by the engine's own `generated N token(s) in M ms` log line. Two things the test found are fixed in the same change: the model now stays loaded for **5 minutes** with nothing asked instead of 5 seconds (the 5-second window unloaded it 16 seconds after Load, before a person could start typing), while the 180-second per-reply limit is unchanged and leaving the screen still frees the model at once; and the draft field and **Send** stay on screen with the keyboard up instead of being clipped out of the accessibility tree, with a small **Clear** action beside Send to discard a draft that survives leaving the screen. It adds no route to the PC, needs no permission, and leaves the ordinary Jarvis chat that uses your PC exactly as it was. Honest limit: the in-app **Import** (system file picker) was not exercised - the test models were copied over adb - so that path is NOT-TESTED, not a pass.
- **The phone's microphone now stops Jarvis when you press it, on by default (2026-11-13).** Before this, pressing the talk button while Jarvis was speaking did nothing: while a reply was still arriving both microphone buttons were greyed out, and once the reply had arrived but its last sentences were still playing `VoiceSession.begin` answered "Still finishing the last one." and returned without touching the speaker. Now a press during speech silences the reply at once - the same `VoiceSession.stopSpeaking()` the "stop" word already calls, which pauses the audio track and stops the phone's own TTS - then drops the old turn the way "hey Jarvis" does (`speakStreamed`'s job is cancelled and its `Turn.silenced` latch stops any further sentence), and starts listening exactly as an ordinary press does; the words still go to the PC's own voice route, so the phone transcribes nothing. This is the behaviour the desktop's talk button has always had (`jarvis-desktop/src/main.js` `startPushToTalk`: `noteCutOff(); stopSpeaking();`), so the phone was the missing half. The new switch is Settings -> Voice -> "Stop speaking when I press the mic", ON by default and this phone's own; OFF gives the old behaviour back exactly, including the "Jarvis is answering" line and "Still finishing the last one.". It is separate from the existing "Interrupting Jarvis" setting, which is about the phone listening by itself while Jarvis talks. The local JVM/contract suite is green (3,679 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped); NOT tested on a real phone - in particular the "stops within a tenth of a second" claim rests on Android's `AudioTrack.pause()` (the stop word's existing path), and the first few milliseconds of the new clip could still catch the cut syllable when the speaker is on the voice-call route.
- **A restored phone keeps its own desktop address, and a backup file cannot pick a huge password-hashing cost (2026-11-13).** The phone's settings backup no longer carries the desktop's address (`host`): the pairing token stays behind the Android Keystore, so a restore that wrote an address would send a credential the phone already holds to whatever desktop the file named - and a backup made before this change, or a crafted one, has its address dropped when read rather than applied. The address is typed again when the phone pairs, exactly as after a reinstall. Two sentences that promised more than the code could keep are corrected with it: a restore that fails while writing a preferences file now says that some settings may already have been restored and the rest were not (the files are written one at a time), and a backup file may no longer ask for more PBKDF2 rounds than this app writes (210,000), so a small crafted header cannot make the phone run millions of rounds before the first tag check fails. `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 220 now says which failures share the "damaged" sentence and that only authentication is all-or-nothing.
