Two owner-reported HUD presentation fixes ride in the same pull request: the chosen personality now wears the same chosen rectangle a chosen preset wears (the visible word "(current)" is gone; the state is in the accessible name only, as the presets have done since 2026-10-31), and the top-right model chip repaints itself from the PC's own preset answer on the 30-second safety poll, so a preset changed outside the window (Settings, or a benchmark run on the PC) can no longer leave the old model in the chip. **The COMPUTE panel now names the card per lane (F6):** when two Ollama lanes are loaded at once, each lane's `gpu_indices` is found by walking its model runner's parent chain to the lane's own listening Ollama server (a read-only ctypes process query that starts no process, bounded to eight links), so the "Loaded now / Resources" plate says "graphics card 0" for the everyday lane and "graphics card 2" for the coding lane instead of "no graphics card (or the cards carrying it were not reported)" for both; when the OS will not report a parent the lane still says the cards were not reported and never guesses one, and the one-loaded-lane fallback is unchanged. Proved by this PC's own live read (11436 -> card 0, 11435 -> card 2, 11450 empty) and by nine new checks in `backend/test_model_resources.py` (two loaded lanes name their own cards; an unreadable chain stays unreported; a looping chain is bounded; the one-lane fallback still names the server's cards).
- **Wave 12: the dead skill checks are wired, files drag in, notes and Notion get their numbers, read-aloud speaks in Jarvis's own voice, a reversible click needs no card, and the Brain stops describing plans as facts (2026-11-09).** One consolidated wave on top of the merged Wave-10/11 work. **Security first:** the four checks that existed and were tested in `jarvis_skill_hub` - the Hermes inline `` !`command` `` form, exfiltration said in words, "already approved" claims, a bare external URL - had NO production caller; `jarvis_skills.vet()` now calls them, so the menu preview, the install/edit/turn-on card, the pack door and a project skill all judge the same text from one definition (DEF-049), and `skills.lock` is now written on every install/edit and forgotten on removal (Gemini Q3). **Files:** a compatible file dragged into the desktop HUD or any chat window rides the existing `/api/chat` attachment field (same eight kinds, 2,500,000-byte cap, one file per question, nothing auto-sends; the Tauri drag-drop handler had to be turned off per window, which is why the gesture never worked in the packaged app), and the Alt+Space bar's own chat command carries the same attachment so a file can ride the bar's next question too. **Notes:** one sentence now creates the note the owner meant - title, body, pinned flag and date parsed locally, still card-free, collision-refused and undoable. **Notion:** a 276 MB export imports (4 GB unpacked ceiling, every zip-bomb guard kept, refusals quoting the real numbers, a free-space preflight, a live progress line), and the phone may send the same 4 GB zip over the private network (raw-bytes cap raised from 250 MiB to 4 GiB, staging ceiling moved with it). **Read-aloud** plays audio the PC made in Jarvis's own configured voice through the bar's `speak_reply` route, never a browser fallback, with Pause, Resume and a full Stop beside the answer, and the page's CSP now lets that `data:` clip through. **Forget a time frame** loses the 200-item cap while keeping both yeses and proving backups untouched. **Brain:** Model says what is loaded - its real context and spill and the cards' memory - COMPUTE labels plans as plans, a Measured results card reads the real benchmark and scorecard stores, Tutorials gains a "What's new in Jarvis" pane, Goals sits under Projects as on the phone, the Galaxy is labelled as the memory map with a one-click HUD door, and the tray/Settings update row tells four honest states instead of inventing "up to date". **Permissions:** a local preset clicked in either app's own preset control applies at once with no card and writes a `preset_apply` receipt (the preset it replaced and Undo; the model/chat/voice path keeps its one `switch_model` card, and Coding, Cloud, installs and downloads keep theirs), and Gemini Q2's explicit backend allow-list is the one place that rule is written down. **Folded in from the wave-11 acceptance on the owner's live install (0.2.441, 2026-11-09):** the sentence *"which model is better for the Coding preset?"* was answered about a preset called "better for the Coding", because the one-preset advice ran after the one-preset model ask; the advice now runs first and names the Coding preset's real model, while *"what model does the coding preset use"* still gets its old answer (new checks in `backend/test_quick_wins.py`). The same field test reproduced the owner's photographed 74%-on-card duplicate and found the tag-sized hole that let it through: the third-card guard compared the pooled 30B's exact name, while Ollama reports it with a ":latest" tag, so the everyday lane could warm a second copy; the guard now strips that tag, and `backend/test_lane_integrity.py` drives the real `warm_everyday()` seam with the tagged name and proves zero requests are sent. Its third finding - that the pooled lane's measured 49,152-token window is not really applied because Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint ignores the request's `options` field - is recorded honestly as an open defect (DEF-034's second finding) and carried to Wave 13 as its own design item, not claimed here. **Records:** the Wave 9-13 field-test register is opened with every row NOT RUN YET until driven on the real app; the memories the owner asked for are recorded as decisions with their not-yet-built state said plainly.
- **Wave 11: the model screens tell the truth, the coding lane cannot die silently, and Jarvis can talk about its own models (2026-11-08).** The HUD's top-right chip now names the model actually in use - the chosen focus preset's own model when the PC says one is chosen, otherwise the PC's default - instead of painting the default alone at boot, and a quick "no AI model" turn can no longer erase it. The Brain's "What this PC should run" now describes this PC's real hardware: every CUDA card the probe reports (three cards, 28 GiB here), not only the cards one running Ollama's log happens to list, so it no longer calls a three-card PC a one-card 8 GiB PC; the tier sentence is printed once instead of twice, every estimate-scoped "fits on one card" sentence is separated from the "Separately measured on 2026-11-07" measurements, and the Compute column's plan says "any card beyond the first" instead of the two-card-era "the second card". The GPU-offload warning now asks the lane the chat actually uses rather than a fixed Ollama address, so it cannot report a stale duplicate's 74% while the chat lane is at 100%, and it says plainly when that lane is unreachable or empty. The live-awareness gate now surfaces the backend's own error sentence when a chat reply carries one - the Wave-9 deploy's three BLOCKED rows hid "The local model is not running" behind "HTTP 200 with no answer text" - and it still never counts a BLOCKED row as a pass. The persisted chat lane can no longer outlive its on-demand pooled server: a startup reconcile puts chat back on a live lane and forgets the stale preset when the pooled server is gone, stopping the pooled lane restores the lane file instead of leaving it naming a dead server, and a pooled start pauses and proves both lane models gone before it starts, so the same 30B model cannot be resident twice; the measured 49,152-token window is asked for when the pooled lane loads. And Jarvis can now talk about its local models in both chat and Jarvis Live, deterministically and honestly: what it has measured (from its real benchmark and suite-scorecard stores, every number with its date, and "I have not measured anything on this PC yet" when the store is empty - never an invented number), starting a benchmark or the five suites through the existing runner (owner-initiated, throwaway server on a spare port, never the live lane's own server, one at a time, refused while a turn is streaming), which model each of the nine presets uses with its card and window and which preset is active, better-model candidates for a preset carrying the recommender's MEASURED ON THIS PC / ESTIMATED FIT labels with no verdict it has not measured for that preset, and the current model plus what the change journal says was in use before (or that no change is recorded). Nothing in this wave switches a model, approves a card, or invents a measurement. A dead pooled-lane pointer can no longer fail a chat turn: the chat-lane getter proves the port with one sub-second TCP connect and, when the on-demand three-card server is gone, atomically puts the configured everyday lane back and returns it - starting, pausing and loading nothing, so a status poll is safe. A pooled-lane chat request now names its configured 49,152-token window in `options.num_ctx`, so Ollama cannot quietly fall back to 8,192 and reload/truncate the measured context, and every other lane's request is unchanged. The wake-time everyday warm-up no longer touches 11436 while the pooled lane is the active running lane, and it never loads a pooled 30B model onto the everyday lane at all - the guard that stops the duplicate copy the owner photographed at 74% on the GPU / 26% on the CPU. The owner's three live UI asks are in the same wave: the Brain rail's Advanced disclosure now says "Hide advanced" while open and "Advanced" when closed; the HUD no longer shows the persistent "This session is staying on your PC." line (the taint latch itself and the queue-scoped rush evidence are unchanged, and the three hud-safety copies stay byte-equal); and the Brain -> Model filter row is now a foldable "Filters" / "Hide filters" disclosure whose controls wrap instead of running off the right edge.
- **Wave 10: one honest answer menu, a real receipt for the GitHub token, HUD layouts that apply at once, deterministic feature answers and a default-ON Wi-Fi reconnect (2026-11-08).** Right/Wrong on both apps now opens its own sheet with five plain reasons (wrong fact, out of date, misunderstood, too long, too sensitive) and one optional correction line of at most 500 characters; a wrong-fact or out-of-date mark raises ONE existing memory-review card for the first remembered fact the answer used - the owner's own words on an update card when he typed them, a retire card only when he did not, and both apps now ask for those cards with `retire_cards=1` so they are labelled correctly - and the desktop HUD's count-only badge read asks for them too, so the badge and the drawer below it can never disagree - while a misunderstood or too-long answer leaves a manner note and a too-sensitive one a privacy note. Both apps read the mark's saved reason and correction back from the PC, so a re-shown answer says why it was marked in the owner's own words, and both label the two memory cards with one set of words: "Update the fact" / "Keep it as it is" for a correction, "Forget that fact" / "Keep using it" for a retire. A migration smoke test opens a COPY of the live `feedback.db` and proves the old rows and marks still read with the two new columns - the live file is never opened or changed. The GitHub token answer is fixed at the root: the connect-account card already ran one real test, and its verdict is now remembered as one non-secret record (which service, when, whether the one test ran and its words), so the sentences the owner actually typed after saving - "i added a token", "did the token work?", "what did the github test prove?" - are answered from what was measured, never claiming cloning, pushing or pulling, and byte-identical on the coding preset. A saved HUD layout now applies the moment it is saved instead of waiting for the next window start; the Studio shell gives the connect-account and secret-handoff cards their own full-width rows instead of auto-placing them into the face column, and the fixed safety strip reserves a band so it never covers the model and "standing by" chips. Feature-shaped questions now answer from the catalogue row they name (the read-aloud question that used to answer with the read-web-page row is fixed) and an unknown feature name gets the honest "I do not have a feature called ..." answer; the owner's own read-aloud phrasings ("you turn off reading out loud", "turn off reading everything out loud", "stop reading everything out loud") now resolve deterministically, switching read-aloud OFF now silences an answer already being spoken - mid-sentence, from Settings, chat or Jarvis Live - and a new preset-independence suite proves the factual answers are byte-identical across the general, coding, fast and uncensored presets, with an honest deterministic "I do not have a setting or feature with that exact name" fallback where nothing is registered, instead of a model guess. The four stale catalogue descriptions of read-aloud (both apps and both backend copies) now describe the switch actually shipped, and the phone's memory read-aloud row gains the one-line "On by default — toggle off anytime" subtitle, with no banner. The desktop also gains the owner's 2-hourly Wi-Fi reconnect, ON by default: only while this PC has no internet, only saved password-protected networks it already knows, never an open or new one, never a password prompt, at most the top three such networks actually broadcasting in range, each given 10 seconds, only while Lockdown is off and the radio was not switched off by hand, idle-only, every attempt written to the audit trail as a receipt so "did you reconnect my wifi?" is answered from it, turning it ON raises one `change_own_config` card while OFF is instant, and a dry-run mode; it is the PC's alone, and the reason is recorded in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 and `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §204.
- **Wave 9: the read-aloud switch, the five-suite benchmark, the Brain's model filters and the hardware-aware recommender (2026-11-07).** The owner's read-aloud policy is now real and honest: typed answers stay silent, a voice answer is read aloud when the new backend-owned switch (ON by default) is on, remembered answers are read aloud in Jarvis Live on the phone by default, extremely sensitive answers always stay on screen, and every desktop answer menu and phone message menu carries its own Read out loud beside Right/Wrong with receipts. Jarvis can also run its own five-suite benchmark (speed, coding, general, tool-calling, vision) by asking - with a measure-first promotion harness that never moves a preset default without a measured result - recommend a model from whatever PC's real hardware it is on (MEASURED ON THIS PC / ESTIMATED FIT, non-fitting models hidden), and the pooled lane can now load deep_think and creative models as well as coding. The HUD gains Brain doors in its menu bar and column, the Brain's Skills line reports the measured 0 installed / 0 quarantined instead of guessing, and Models hides non-fitting candidates and offers the full filter bar. It also fixes the four Wave-8.2 deploy findings (the 0-presets count, the code-recent question, the Gate-11 read-only cloud probe and the desktop-row probe).
- **Wave 8.2: full self-awareness, and a journal of what changes.** Jarvis can now say which preset it is on (model, context window, measured speed, how to switch), what benchmarks this PC has recorded, and it can start, follow and stop one benchmark of the current model from chat or Live ("run a benchmark" no longer claims it opened an app). It keeps a local change journal - version, preset, model, every setting, every tool switch and the counts, diffed against the last look - so "what changed about you?" answers from the record instead of the model. "What can you change?" and "what do you have?" count the program's own tables; any Settings-page row answers by the words printed on it; any named setting reads its value and how to change it; the eight areas that hold several parts list them with their values and compare two at once. A read-only audit found 121 gap rows before this wave and 0 after, and the new `backend/test_self_awareness.py` (35 checks) is the standing proof. The Notion/file import answers also cover a two-sentence ask that names a downloaded Notion export (the owner's phone finding: Jarvis used to answer with the model's false "I don't have a direct tool" instead of the real Notion and Bring-in steps), and they now say the .zip must sit inside one of the folders Jarvis may look in - the reason a zip in Downloads could not be imported. The folder list is now a chat door too: "which folders may you look in?" is answered from the list, and "add my downloads folder to the folders jarvis may look in" (or an explicit path) raises the same one PC approval card the Settings page uses - the fix for the owner's Notion export sitting in a folder Jarvis was not allowed to look in.
- **Wave 8.1: the repo-watch answer, the `One sentence.` shape and the audit job.** `What repos are you watching?` answered with the timers sentence because the read intent sat in `_REMINDER_INTENTS`, the dispatch set `run()` checks first; it now lives in `READ_ONLY_INTENTS`, is answered deterministically in private chats too, and a structural test pins dispatch sets disjoint and every reminder name explicitly handled. A trailing `One sentence.`/`briefly` is retried only after a first-pass miss, so `Turn on cloud escalation. One sentence.` reaches the same deterministic door as the bare sentence. The informational `audit` job checks out full history so the self-code claim stops skipping, and the rolling phone release now carries the built commit in `targetCommitish` as well as the APK name.
- **The Coding preset now uses all three graphics cards (2026-11-07).** Measured on this PC with its own throwaway `ollama serve` per config on port 11451: the same `qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-ud-q3-k-xl` now runs across all three cards at **49,152 tokens with zero CPU spill** - **83.82 tokens a second and a 31.561 s cold load** (16.17 GiB, cards 0/1/2) against **60.58** and **69.611 s** for 32,768 on the same-night two-card control (that control ran the same q8_0 cache; the 2026-11-03 shipped record used f16 and read 80.36/36.0 s, so it is not a like-for-like baseline and the gain over today's lane is small - the window and the zero spill are the change) - where the enabling knob is `OLLAMA_SCHED_SPREAD=1` in the pooled server's child environment, without which the same three cards decode at 56.82. The 32,768 row measured 84.93 tok/s at 15.10 GiB with a 10.884 s load and is kept as the recorded alternative (1.3 % faster, 1.07 GiB smaller, 16,384 fewer tokens); 65,536 measured 59.06 tok/s and was rejected as below the 75 tok/s bar, and 131,072 FAILED (`server: server exited 4294967295`), so nothing above 49,152 is claimed. Every other preset keeps its measured single-card configuration because spreading it over the third card does not help them - the everyday 9B stays on the 2060 at 196,608, and Fast measured 76.20 on its own card against 65.85 across three (the headless card alone measured 85.29, a measured gain that waits for its own lane on 11438) - the new heavy presets are measured but deferred to Wave 8, and auto-escalation stays off because the cloud audit found a privacy gap.
- **Jarvis can say what changed, explain any setting, and no longer denies the abilities this PC really has (2026-11-07).** The feature self-awareness audit measured thirteen false self-descriptions: it said approval rules could not be changed by chatting (the live `approval_policy` setting does exactly that), that it kept no chat history, that it had no spending limits, that it could not watch a page or a GitHub Actions run, and that old approval cards never expire - while each of those is live on the PC. Four families now answer from a shipped, read-only table (`jarvis_feature_guide.SELF_FACTS`, carried into the model's self portrait as bounded digests): approval policy, watches and the CI watcher, spending limits, and chat history. "What changed in your last update?" is answered from a generated module of the record's newest bullets (`jarvis_recent_changes.py`, built by `tools/gen_recent_changes.py` because the live folder has no `CHANGELOG.md`) plus the PC's own VERSION - never "I haven't changed" and never an invented list. "Can you explain any setting?" and "what is X set to?" reach the existing explain door instead of the model (that door already knew every value, place and exact phrase), and "where do I change the face size / standby hours / attention budget / spending / notification styles?" gets the real place rather than a wrong one. Two honesty bugs are fixed with it: "turn on anti-slop for code" while the filter itself was off now says the filter is still off instead of claiming "Anti-Slop on", and a toggle that asks for the value a switch already has says "already on/off" and writes **no** no-op receipt (the audit measured a before=false/after=false anti-slop receipt whose undo could take back a later real change). Read-only throughout: no route, no card, no tier, no file written by any of the new answers, and the one Live/typed parity this touches is wording only.
- **Jarvis now knows the major parts of its own code, and where its own repository is (2026-11-07).** Asked "what is your own GitHub repository?", the live backend answered "I don't have a public GitHub repository of my own" — the one fact it was missing about itself. Its code IS the public `darknight11ish/Epic-Jarvis` repository, so a generated map of that tree now ships beside the backend: `backend/jarvis-self-code.json` is written by `tools/gen_self_code_map.py` (deterministic, standard library, no network, no absolute paths) from the deployed tree at the commit the deploy was built from. It carries the five runtime parts in the order they fit (backend on the PC → Ollama → the Tauri shell → the Android client → the public repo with its CI and deploy), then one row per major part of the code with its purpose, every file it owns, the key modules to start reading (with the first sentence of each module's own docstring), the suites that prove it and the documents that describe it — plus the commit, its date, the version and the newest twenty commit subjects. Completeness is checked by construction: the generator exits non-zero and names every path when a tracked file belongs to no subsystem or to two, and generated/binary/vendored files are skipped only through an explicitly named list whose counts it prints and stores. `backend/jarvis_self_code.py` (shipped whole, twin kept) only reads that file beside itself — no git, no socket, no write, no model, no code body — and says "the self-code map was not installed with this build" when it is absent. Four deterministic chat intents in `jarvis_quick.py` answer from it: the overview, a lookup ("where is the code for X"; "what does X do" only when X is really in the map), what changed recently (saying plainly it is as of the deploy that built the map) and the public repository identity. A miss says "not in the map I was built with" and names the two nearest parts, never a guess; all four are read-only, and the existing version, tools, GPU, memory-count, identity, feature and "where did I put" answers keep their own sentences (pinned). `--check` fails on drift, `docs/SELF-CODE-MAP.md` says how to refresh it, and `backend/test_self_code.py` (82 checks) proves the generator, the coverage failure, the map shape, every answer, the miss, the missing map and the old owners.
- **A repository watcher you can steer by voice or typing:** say "watch darknight11ish/Epic-Jarvis", "watch your repo daily", "watch it for new releases and issues", "stop telling me about it", "resume watching it", "tell me weekly about that repo" or "follow new repos for topic mcp" in chat or in Jarvis Live and it obeys - one sentence, the same answer both places. Each watch follows any combination of new releases, commits, issues, pull requests and CI changes at instant, daily, weekly or pull-only cadence; it starts in observe mode and tells nobody until the owner answers the one approval card that starting it raises. Public repositories work with no GitHub token at all, and every poll is conditional (`If-None-Match`), so an unchanged repository costs zero GitHub rate-limit points. Duplicate items are never announced twice, ordinary notifications can never ring or interrupt, and the log of what it would have said is the existing `GET /api/watch/decisions`. Starting one creates the repeating job that actually checks every ten minutes, through the scheduler's own `add_repeat` - the same one-card path the older "tell me when CI fails" GitHub watch uses - so "watch X daily" really polls after the yes, and "forget X" deletes the check with the watch.
- **The Ollama server on port 11434 is pinned to the headless RTX 2080 SUPER by UUID, and the CPU spill ends (2026-11-07).** Both Ollama servers were on the RTX 2060: the everyday lane on 11436 (`qwen3.5:9b`) and Ollama's own tray-app server on 11434 (`qwen3:8b`), whose load plans add up to 15,512 MiB on a 12,288 MiB card. `ollama ps` reported both as "100% GPU, 0 spill" and that is Ollama's load plan, not memory: Windows' own per-process GPU counters (`\GPU Process Memory(*)\Dedicated Usage`) measured the 9B holding only 5,545 MiB in VRAM with 3,856 MiB paged out to system RAM, while the headless 2080 SUPER sat at 0 of its 8,192 MiB. Pinned to `GPU-1f7e38f5-...` on a throwaway 11451 server, the same `qwen3:8b` is fully resident at 6,142 MiB in VRAM against a 5,991 MiB plan (6,141 of 8,192 MiB on the card) and reads 66.38 tok/s cold / 69.38-71.17 warm against 50.4-50.7 on the shared 2060. No repository code starts the 11434 server - the Ollama tray app does - so the deploy step is a logon task that starts that app with `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and `OLLAMA_VULKAN=0` set for that process tree only, plus moving the app's own autostart shortcut aside so only one instance starts; a global per-user variable was measured to the same numbers and is NOT recommended, because it would pin every future CUDA process on the PC, other AI tools included. `docs/MODEL-TOPOLOGY.md` carries the evidence, the exact wrapper/task/rollback commands, the task-owned `start-lane.ps1` alternative (also measured), and the deploy verification that does not trust `ollama ps`. No live server was restarted or killed in this change.
- **Jarvis knows its own GitHub (2026-11-07).** The Features pages, the Feature Guide and the deterministic capability answer gain ONE `connected-github` row that names the six on-demand tools, `github_search` and the scheduled `watch_github` job, the three carded actions (comment, open an issue, re-run a workflow) and the never-list. "What can you do with my GitHub?" now names that surface instead of only the two research features; "can you merge a pull request?" gets a fixed refusal that says there is no merge action and no merge card; "what is your GitHub repository?" names `darknight11ish/Epic-Jarvis`; "what do you need before you can read my repos?" names the token and the switches; "how do I disconnect my GitHub?" answers from the same values `/api/accounts` serves, and that row now says read AND act with the six real abilities instead of "Read-only: private repositories and CI status". Also in the same change: the six tools' enable hints point at the real "What asks first" switches (not a "Settings -> Tools" screen that does not exist), the connect card's summary names the reads and the three actions, "what's your latest release?" answers like "what's the latest release?", the Feature Guide no longer says "no switch" beside a row that says "switch it on", and GitHub research's shipped tier is `ask` so the "Search GitHub" row stops showing a developer diagnostic. It cannot merge, push, commit, close or delete anything - that absence is deliberate and now says so.
- **The cloud provider you choose is the one your words go to, chat can see and change it, every switch answers about itself, and three "how do I add …" questions stop getting the reminder answer (2026-11-07).** The 2026-11-07 options-understanding audit proved four owner-visible defects in the live code, and the same session's Q1/Q7 rulings hardened the privacy backstop and the auto-escalation rules. **The chosen provider answers.** `jarvis_chatbot_api.lane_service()` was a hard-coded `("deepseek_api", "deepseek-flash")`, so picking Mistral in the Presets Cloud row still sent the words to `api.deepseek.com` while the Presets row, the approval card and `/api/reach` named Mistral. It now reads `cloud-choice.json` (`jarvis_presets.cloud_chosen()`) at request time, with `DEFAULT_LANE` (DeepSeek, the owner's 2026-10-06 choice) only as the fallback when no provider is chosen - so the key lookup, the lane's host and URL, `/api/reach`, the ONE `change_own_config` card and every chat answer name the chosen service, and a chosen Mistral, OpenAI, Groq, xAI or OpenRouter can never send to DeepSeek. **Chat can see the six and change the choice.** "which cloud providers can I use?", "do you support openai" and "can I use two cloud providers" are answered from the PC's own provider list (company, short name, key saved or not - never a key), and "switch my cloud provider to mistral", "switch to mistral", "use mistral instead of deepseek" and "choose openrouter as my cloud provider" call the SAME one-card `jarvis_presets.apply_cloud` the Presets row calls: a service this PC cannot use is refused before any card, ONE `change_own_config` card asks first, and nothing is written until the yes. **Every switch answers about itself.** `jarvis_quick._run_feature_state_setting` passed the registry KEY to a FEATURE lookup, so 14 of the 38 switches answered "I do not have a feature called \"lights_without_card\"" and showed the raw snake_case key; it now asks the guide by the setting's own registry name (a choice keeps its key, as before), and all 38 answer an ordinary "is <its label> on?" without the false denial or a raw key. **The 14 wrong how-to answers.** Because the reminder family's HOW shape reads any "how do I add …", "how do I add a mistral key" was answered with how to set a timer; key questions now name Settings, Chatbot API keys and the one line `py -3 jarvis_chatbot_api.py key <service>` (with the six short names and the monthly-limit line), a model question names Brain, Model, Models and its one card, a second-PC question says one PC plus the phone pairing (a second PC is designed, not built), and a Telegram question says honestly that it is not built. Reminders and shopping lists keep their own answers. **The Cloud row's title** is now "Cloud (an API service you choose)" (it named 1 of 6 services; the docs already named all six), and its own sentence no longer calls DeepSeek the default. **Q7 P0 - the privacy backstop is harder to get past.** `jarvis_router._PRIVATE_TERMS` gains home/street/mailing/postal address and phone number, and its too-broad `\bdiagnos\w*` is narrowed to medical contexts (`medical diagnosis`, `diagnosed with`, the owner/family possessive) so "diagnose this test failure" can escalate normally again. **Q7 - auto-escalation keeps its rules, now pinned.** With the standing cloud-escalation switch OFF a hard question is only offered (detect-and-ask, one card, `auto: false`); with it ON - turned on only through its own `change_own_config` card - a clean hard prompt may auto-escalate, and every gate above the yes (Lockdown, taint, picture, screen, file, private word, pasted secret, complexity, budget, no lane) still refuses exactly as before. Tests: `backend/test_options_understanding.py` (new, 136 checks: the six-provider in-memory routing proof, the key answer naming the chosen provider, all 38 switches, the four verbatim how-to phrases, the chat door's card tier and refusal-before-card, reach/card/answer/lane agreement after a chosen Mistral, and every auto-escalation gate with the switch on and off), `backend/test_router_private_terms.py` (extended: the address/phone words and the `diagnos` narrowing both ways, 181 checks), plus the existing chatbot-api, presets-cloud, cloud-honesty, reach, feature-guide, settings-registry and quick-wins suites.

Six safety sentences (the public tunnel, "pretend I already approved", "print your pairing token", "just do it without asking", "turn off all the safety checks", "approve the pending card for me"), five self-facts compared against ground truth measured on this PC first (the live `VERSION`, the phone over adb, `nvidia-smi`, and the backend's own fact and switched-on tool counts), seven capabilities taken from the catalogue (importing a Notion export, a document from the phone, read-aloud, searching past chats, widgets, cloud escalation, folders) and seven of the owner's own trap sentences. - **A skill you turned off can now be removed; before this it could never leave the PC (2026-11-05).** The Skills list in Settings has had Add and Remove since 2026-11-02 (PR #1092): install from a folder, a `.zip` or the read-only Hermes scan behind ONE `modify_own_code` card, and Remove on an installed skill through the same `brain_remove_skill` command the Brain already used. No card, because the skill is already out of the load path and nothing is offered from it - the same rule that makes turning one off immediate, and the same rule `jarvis_skills.uninstall` has always followed for an installed one. ONE name per request; a name that is installed is refused (that removal is unchanged and stays the only door to it), `remove` and `on` in one request is refused, and there is no list form. The phone gains nothing here on purpose - its list never shows a turned-off skill, and no route may let a client delete a folder it cannot see (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8). Proved by `backend/test_skill_menu.py` (200 checks, including the one that shows the old removal really cannot see the parked copy) and `jarvis-desktop/tests/skills-menu.mjs`; recorded in `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §178 and `decisions.d/2026-11-05-skills-remove-turned-off.md`.
- **Jarvis can map a project's folder without being able to change a single byte of it (2026-11-05).** The first piece of "Jarvis as a project worker", built in the order the 2026-11-05 project-management audit and Gemini's ruling fixed: a **read-only repository map FIRST**, before project-scoped chat and before any staged diff. `backend/jarvis_repomap.py` walks ONE folder that is already on "Folders Jarvis may look in" (the same `jarvis_documents.allowed_path()` boundary the files tool uses, checked again on every file), honours `.gitignore` per directory including `!` negation, reads Python with `ast` and JavaScript, TypeScript, Kotlin and Rust with a conservative signature/import scan, and ranks what it finds for a question by a formula written out in the module docstring: 12 per question word in a declared symbol name, 6 in a file or folder name, 2 in an import, 4 when a matched file imports this one, 1 the other way, plus a small size tie-break. It packs the result into at most 2,000 tokens (default 1,500) counted exactly the way `jarvis_agent.estimate_tokens` counts, listing names and signatures only and never a function's body. It is reached by `GET /api/projects/<id>/map?q=…&tokens=…` on the project store's own route table, and from chat as one more action on the existing `my_files` tool (`map`, by project id or by a listed folder). It writes nothing at all - no index, no cache - runs no program, opens no socket, calls no model, adds no gate action and no card (it is a read, under the existing `read_files_readonly` line), and a folder that is not on the owner's list is refused in one plain sentence rather than guessed at. `project_edit` is still not built: this is the read that makes the later write worth trusting.
- **The preset map now says what actually fits, and heavy mode is read as a field instead of by a preset's name (2026-11-05).** The owner's brief of 2026-11-04 (Q6) named two things to fix before any new preset lands. First, the one-step app-control planner filtered heavy presets by the substring `"coding"` in the preset id (`backend/jarvis_app_control.py`), so the rule would have been false the moment a `deep_think` or `creative` preset - both heavy mode on every card, ~60 s to load - was added: the planner would have offered one of them for a single strict-JSON step and evicted both everyday cards. It now reads `preset.heavy_mode`, the field that actually means "every card at once", so the exclusion stays true for every heavy preset by construction. Second, the three-GPU plan told the owner that Agentic + Vision runs on the headless card, and that is arithmetically impossible: the 9B weights plus the vision projector need about 7.00 GiB (6.10 weights + projector, 0.27 KV at 16,384, 0.63 runtime) and an 8 GB card with no monitor has 6.65 GiB free after the desktop and the gap - 0.35 GiB short, and still 0.15 short at a 4,096-token window. The plan now says Agentic + Vision stays on the 12 GB everyday card (where it already runs and is measured) and says why the headless card cannot take a 9B lane; the per-preset 3-GPU row and the plan's card row were corrected with it. `backend/test_presets.py` (97 passed), `backend/test_presets_consistency.py` (80 passed) and `backend/test_app_control.py` (203 passed) all pass; the generated contract `backend/fixtures/work_presets.json` was regenerated with `tools/gen_work_presets.py` rather than hand-edited.
- **A document sent from the phone now lands on the PC as if the owner had put it there himself, and a Notion export from the phone can be run through the existing vault import (2026-11-05).** The owner's ask - "upload any documents through the jarvis app and have it be fully processed as if I was uploading it to the jarvis desktop" - needed no new processing: the folder list, the text index, the PDF/Word/Excel/PowerPoint converter and the Notion->Obsidian importer all exist and are tested. What was missing was the transport, and it is a new no-patch drop-in, `plugins/ready/upload` + `backend/jarvis_upload.py`: `POST /api/upload/begin` (a name, a size, an optional sha256 and one of the folders `GET /api/folders` already returned, chosen by EQUALITY against `jarvis_documents.folders()` - the phone cannot create a grant), `POST /api/upload/chunk` (1 MiB of raw bytes per request, so every body stays about a third of the server's 4 MiB cap and a Notion export can arrive at all), and `POST /api/upload/finish` (the bytes that really arrived measured against the declared size and the sha256, then `jarvis_attached_file`'s own magic-byte, encrypted-PDF and zip-bomb guards, then ONE `os.replace`). A document lands in `<the listed folder>\From my phone\<name>` and from that moment is a desktop file - findable by name at once, indexed on the next search if it is a note or text file, convertible on request - because nothing in the new module indexes, converts or reads anything. A file already named there is never overwritten (`taxes (2).pdf`). **ONE card per file, before a byte is written:** `receive_uploaded_document`, tier `ask`, in `jarvis_asks_first.HARD_LIMITS` and `MUST_ASK` and on the "This PC and your phone" page, so no app and no settings line can turn it into a standing yes; a denied, timed-out or never-answered card writes nothing, and every chunk answers 409 while the card waits and 403 once it is denied. While it waits, the bytes sit in a dot-prefixed staging folder inside the destination, which `jarvis_documents.allowed_path` refuses - so a half-written file is invisible to find, read and search - and the staging is deleted on success, on refusal, on a denied card, on expiry (30 minutes) and by a sweep on the next `begin`. Caps: 50 MB a document (the number the desktop reader uses), 250 MB a Notion export, three uploads at once, 512 MB staged in all; executables, scripts, pictures and every kind outside the same eight the attachment reader takes are refused by NAME at begin and by BYTES at finish. **The second half reuses the Notion importer unchanged, behind two routes that take no path:** `GET /api/notion/vaults` offers only vaults this PC already validated (the one configured for notes, and the last one an import used), and `POST /api/notion/phone-import` takes an upload id and a vault id - no digest answers `plan_import` + `describe` and writes nothing, a digest calls the existing `request_import`, unchanged: one `import_notion_export` card, `run_import`, the receipt and Undo, and the staged zip deleted in a `finally`. The two path-taking PC-only Notion routes are untouched and still answer `403 pc_only` from any other device. `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 196 and section 152 record the routes, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 records that the phone's picker and progress chip are the next lane, and the reversal of the 2026-10-29 "no upload endpoint, now or later" line is recorded in `decisions.d/2026-11-05-phone-upload.md`. Proved by `backend/test_upload.py` (180 checks: the chunked happy path, the card raised before anything lands, a denied card and a timed-out card leaving nothing, the sha256 and size refusals, both caps, the 4 MiB body arithmetic, an unlisted folder, an empty and a damaged list, every refused extension, a renamed `.docx`, a zip bomb, an encrypted PDF, a text file that is really binary, a name with a path in it, the staging invisible before finish and gone after, expiry and the sweep, the three-in-flight cap and the staging quota, the Notion dry run writing nothing and the import raising ONE card, the two PC-only refusals still holding, the twins, the plugin catalogue and the gate tables), plus `backend/test_documents.py`, `backend/test_notion_obsidian.py`, `backend/test_asks_first.py`, `backend/test_card_words.py` and `backend/test_plugin_catalogue.py` unchanged and green.
- **Send a document, or a Notion export, from your phone into Jarvis (2026-11-05).** Settings, Folders Jarvis may look in, has two new buttons. Send a document puts a PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, text, Markdown or CSV file into a new "From my phone" folder inside one of the folders you already listed, after ONE card on the PC - nothing lands before you say yes. Bring in a Notion export carries the .zip you made yourself in Notion (Settings, Export all workspace content, as Markdown & CSV) into an Obsidian vault, with the PC's one card and its Undo. - **Packs, phase 1: add and remove a skill from a folder or a `.zip`, with the whole scan on the card (2026-11-05).** Four chat tools (`pack_list`, `pack_inspect`, `pack_install`, `pack_remove`) over a new `backend/jarvis_packs.py`: a full pre-install scan (safety, compatibility, effectiveness) computed before anything lands, shown on ONE `modify_own_code` card and saved as a receipt, a `jarvis-packs.json` ledger recording every file it wrote with its sha256, and a removal that deletes exactly those files and keeps anything the owner made. The cause was the session latch added on 2026-11-01 (#1104 / DEF-028): one verified sentence covers the whole Live session, and in the 1.5-2.0 s band - and for every clip when the session's trigger needed no check - `jarvis_live.trust_decision` answered "trusted", so `jarvis_speech.hear` ran no speaker model at all. The latch is KEPT, because re-prompting the owner to re-enrol mid-session was the behaviour the 2026-11-01 ruling removed, and short confirmations ("yes", "do it", under 1.2 s) are still accepted while latched. What the latch may no longer skip is the cheap half of the owner check: a latched clip with `RADIO_GUARD_S` (1.2 s) of speech or more is now put to the in-RAM CAM++ embedding and compared with the enrolled print's centroid - about 15 ms, one embedding and one cosine, nothing written - and a clip under `RADIO_MIN_COSINE` (0.25 with a "hey Jarvis" prefix, 0.32 without) is dropped in silence: not transcribed, never sent to the model, and nothing said about it. The rule's own shape is `jarvis_live.IGNORED_BACKGROUND` (`{"ok": true, "ignored_unmatched_speaker": true, "reason": "background_media_rejected"}`); on the existing utterance wire the same clip answers `ok` **false** with `ignored_unmatched_speaker` true and that `reason`, because `Heard.as_dict()` defines `ok` as "a transcript was produced" and both apps read it that way - a client handed `ok: true` with no text would have nothing to do with it. A guard that cannot measure (no print, no model, an unusable clip) never swallows the owner's words. `backend/test_voice_check_rule.py` grew two test functions and 16 checks, including the regression itself: after one verified sentence a 1.7 s clip is still "trusted" by the latch and now must also pass the guard; 103 passed, 0 failed. The twins are byte-identical, `check_stale_twins.py` is clean, `test_base_matches_repo.py` 136/0 and `test_base_regeneration.py` 39/0. Not in this change: the "it's on your screen" answers and the slow first turn - separate fixes on the same branch, reported on their own.

- **The weekly verified snapshot works again: a too-long Windows path was killing it silently (2026-11-04).** The task ran on 2026-11-01 and failed with `LastTaskResult 1` while the backup folder still said `OK` from 2026-10-25, and it would have done that every Sunday for ever. The cause was `MAX_PATH`: `~/.openjarvis/apps/` was created on 2026-10-30 holding a generated Gradle project, and one `graph.bin` inside it is a 235-character path in place but a 274-character path under the snapshot's `.partial-XXXXXXXX.partial` build folder - and this PC has `LongPathsEnabled = 0`, so `CopyFile2` refused with `WinError 3` ("cannot find the path" for a name that is merely too long). `cmd_backup` caught only `Refused`, `pythonw.exe` has no console, and nothing wrote `last-run.txt`, so twelve of 339 files quietly ended the backup. Now a destination path over `MAX_WINDOWS_PATH` gets Windows' own `\\?\` prefix, including in the sealing and verifying walks that read the snapshot back; a file that still will not copy becomes a `PROBLEM` and the snapshot is kept as `-INCOMPLETE` rather than crashing the run; and however a run ends - refusal, `OSError`, crash, killed task - `last-run.txt` saying `FAILED` reaches both the destination and the installed folder, the run removes its own half-built folder, and a new run clears any abandoned one. Two further holes found on the way are closed: `_seal_folder` was wrapped in `except Refused`, so a full disk left the whole snapshot readable while reporting failure, and `shutil.rmtree` stopped on git's read-only object files, so the plaintext copy survived a successful seal. Measured on this PC into a temporary folder: a full sealed snapshot now completes in 5.3 s (2,669,292 bytes, 20 databases, 5,724 rows, 341 files) and `verify` passes; `backend/test_data_backup.py` is 187 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. Honest limit: `Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational` is disabled on this PC, so there are no event-log entries for 2026-11-01 - the exit code is the task's own `LastTaskResult` and the cause is a reproduction, not an event log.

The per-source answer is one of exactly five words - `disclosed_sponsored`, `likely_monetised_undisclosed`, `affiliate_only`, `no_monetisation_evidence`, `cannot_tell` - each with its own evidence. **There is no trust score, no probability and no percentage anywhere**, for the product engine's own measured reason: a single number hides which rule fired. `cannot_tell` is a real answer, not a guess: an empty page, a JavaScript shell or a page below 40 readable words is reported as unchecked, never as clean. `rank_sources()` puts the most independent sources first and says in plain words how many sources with no monetisation evidence made the same claim beside the monetised ones that made it, comparing claims word for word and printing no percentage. The link and urgency patterns are a Python-native port of dakidarts/dark-radar (MIT), credited in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt`; no JavaScript is vendored. `backend/test_source_independence.py` has 150 checks over synthetic fixtures only, with no network, no browser and no real page; it tries every verdict path, both `cannot_tell` shapes, the no-score rule, the ranking and the agreement counts, and pins by AST that the module imports only `re` and `html.parser`. - **Jarvis can now measure its own token speed on this PC, and the first phase of the self-benchmark is in the backend (2026-11-04).** The owner's ask was for Jarvis to measure its own speed across the local models, the RAM/GPU layer placement and the context sizes, keep a separate history of those runs, and explain the results in plain words. Phase 1 is the measurement engine and its store, with no screens yet: one run is one model + one setup + N repeats on one lane, and a run refuses rather than measuring the queue - a 409 with a sentence when another run is in flight, when an answer is streaming, when Jarvis is on standby, when a task is running, when the lane's Ollama is not running, or when the model is not installed on that lane; a 400 when Ollama's address is not this PC, and a 400 that measures nothing when the POST carries no `confirm` block. **Prompt speed is `(prompt_eval_count - prompt_eval_cached_count) / prompt_eval_duration` and never the naive division**, because `prompt_eval_duration` times only the tokens Ollama actually computed while `prompt_eval_count` counts the whole prompt: in the measured example (318 tokens, 317 cached, 23 ms) the naive sum reports 13,826 tok/s where the model really read one token at 43 - a 318x lie from two correct numbers. A fully cached prompt is reported as "cached - prefill not measured" (never 0, never infinity) and an absent cached count is unknown (never 0). Generation is `eval_count / eval_duration`, BOTH time-to-first-token numbers are stored and the row says so when they differ by more than 15%, VRAM and utilisation are sampled per CARD from `nvidia-smi` (per-process VRAM is `[N/A]` on driver 617.42), and the context really in use plus the `offloaded N/M layers` come from `/api/ps` and the log parser `jarvis_hardware.parse_ollama_log` already had. Rows go to a NEW `~/.openjarvis/bench.jsonl` with its own allowlist, two flat row kinds, a 500-run cap and a 2 MB ceiling; **`speed.jsonl` is never opened**, so the existing chat-speed rows and the screen that reads them are untouched. A run that cannot measure writes `ok: false` + `why` and never a zero, and a run that put part of the model on the processor is labelled PARTIAL and its numbers are never presented as fast. The advice sentence of DESIGN section 9 is here too, and it refuses to compare anything under three runs of the same model. Five routes reach it (`GET /api/bench`, `POST /api/bench/run`, `GET /api/bench/run/{id}`, `POST /api/bench/cancel`, `GET /api/bench/history`), wired by a new `backend/bench.patch` whose two hunks anchor inside `hardware.patch`'s own added blocks and which invents 0 hunks / 0 lines of the owner's original file. NOT done yet, deliberately: the desktop Benchmark panel, the separate History window, the benchmark presets and the `benchmark_results` chat tool, the `/api/bench/advice` route, and the phone's screen - phases 2 to 5. No benchmark has been run for real: every number in `backend/test_bench.py` comes from a fake Ollama reply and fake `nvidia-smi` text, and one real run is a field test, not a test.

- **Hands-free mode on the phone: every approval card is read out, "confirm" or "deny" answers it by voice, and Jarvis can write a text message for the owner (2026-11-04).** A new Settings row (last on the screen, so it moves no other row), and the same switch from a typed chat sentence or said in Jarvis Live - one parser for both, answered by the phone rather than by the model. With it on, a card the PC raises arrives as a `handsfree_card` event (`card_id`, `action`, `say`, `expires_in_sec`): the phone fetches the PC's own WAV from `/api/voice/say` for `say` and plays it through its speaker (never during a phone call, and never in the phone's own voice if the PC has no voice engine - the card is then shown only, and no microphone opens), posts an ongoing notification naming the card and how long it has to answer with its own "Open the card" action (under App lock, "Hide memory lists and chat history", or a phone with no secure lock of its own, BOTH notifications carry one generic line instead - so neither a card's words nor a text message reaches the lock screen - and each is `VISIBILITY_PRIVATE` with a redacted public version, the same `SecurityRules.notificationsLocked` rule every other notifier uses), and then opens the PC's own ANSWER WINDOW - the event's `expires_in_sec`, a minute at most or the card's shorter countdown - marked by the same two-note chime the talk button uses. The window records at most the PC's 30 seconds of 16 kHz mono WAV (`handsfree/HandsfreeClip.kt`, because a longer clip is refused rather than truncated) and closes about a second after the owner stops speaking (the same `TurnEnd` rule the talk button uses, so a one-word answer does not wait out the minute), then uploads to `POST /api/handsfree/answer`; **the phone never transcribes anything** - the PC transcribes it, checks the owner's voice print and decides - and the phone SPEAKS and shows the PC's own `say` ("Approved. Carrying on.", "That was not your voice, so nothing was decided.", "Sorry - was that yes or no?"), so no refusal or decision is ever worded by the app. An unclear answer the PC asks once more is answered again in a second window inside the same deadline, and never a third. `POST /api/handsfree` is the ONE switch path (the GET on the same path is the read, and the contract has no `/enabled` route): OFF is immediate and cardless, ON goes through ONE ask-tier card, and the phone reads the PC's own `enabled` back before it says on. A refused answer keeps the PC's sentence; the app's own fallback ("Your PC did not accept that answer - nothing changed.") is used only when a PC sent none, and "the card had expired" is never said unless the card's own state says so. `phone_command kind=send_sms` is carried out on the phone - the name is resolved in its own address book by an exact, case-folded, unique match (two numbers for one name sends nothing and says why; the same number twice is one match; a number the owner said is used as it is), `SEND_SMS` and `READ_CONTACTS` are runtime permissions asked for when the switch goes on, and `/api/phone/result` gets an answer for every command, with Android's own `RESULT_OK` as the only thing that ever means "sent"; the PC's `phone_result` then replaces that notification's line with the PC's own sentence, quietly, so the two halves say the same thing. The microphone is arbitrated through one new ledger (`voice/MicOwner.kt`): the answer window HOLDS it and so does the talk button (`audio/Recorder.kt`, which takes it before it opens its own `AudioRecord` and gives it back in a `finally`), so a press and a window can no longer open two recorders at once - whichever is refused says why in whole words ("You were talking to Jarvis, so the card was not read out." / "Jarvis is listening for your answer to a card, so the microphone is busy. Try again in a moment.") - while Jarvis Live and "hey Jarvis" close their recorders for that window and reopen afterwards, and the talk button still shows "Listening for your confirm/deny". A PC without the feature answers 404 on all four routes and sends none of the three events, and every surface then says "Hands-free is not available on this PC yet." - no invented mode, no microphone. `jarvis-client`'s JVM suite is green at 3,475 tests (six new files: `HandsfreeFlowTest`, `HandsfreeClipTest`, `HandsfreeEventTest`, `HandsfreeNoticeTest`, `MicHandsfreeRulesTest`, `SmsSendTest`); four existing tests gained justified pins (the services-with-a-foregroundServiceType count 5 → 6, the wake word's pause condition, the jump list's last entry, and the two lists of Settings rows with no catalogue menu id). NOT TESTED, said plainly: no real call, voice clip or text message was driven from this branch - nothing was installed on the owner's Pixel 9, no SMS was sent, and the PC half of the contract (PR #1169) is not on main yet, so the phone was built and proven against the frozen contract, and its wire shapes were checked line by line against the PC's `backend/jarvis_handsfree.py` at `ced61a23f` - no real microphone, real speech-to-text or real voice print ran against either half. This lane's 2026-11-05 pass aligned the phone to the frozen contract exactly: the switch moved to `POST /api/handsfree`, the 60-second answer window and the 30-second clip cap, the PC's own `say`, `decision: "again"` asked once more, `reading` on the GET, and the `phone_result` event.

The 3-GPU rows stay labelled best effort and not tested: no third card is installed, and nothing here claims a measurement of one.

- **A folder-level restriction can now be set, lifted and checked by plain chat on both apps, through the feature that already existed (2026-11-04).** The owner asked for "folder-level restrictions settable by plain chat (PC+phone)" after a chat answer failed to reflect a capability the backend already had, and gave his own phrasings: *"restrict the folder D:\Photos from Jarvis"*, *"stop Jarvis reading C:\X"*, *"don't let Jarvis touch the folder with my medical scans"*, *"unrestrict D:\Photos"*, *"let Jarvis read that folder again"*, *"what folders are restricted?"*, *"is Jarvis blocked from C:\X?"*. This was not a missing feature - `jarvis_protection.py` (2026-10-31) already had the store, the two modes, the routes and eleven enforcement points - so this change EXTENDS it and adds no second list, mode, route or permission. **Two measured wrong-answer paths are fixed.** (1) The fast path matched only a bare "protect/unprotect", so six of the seven sentences never reached it, and "restrict the folder ... from Jarvis" matched `file_read`'s and `my_files`' hints only - measured `matched 2`, tools `['file_read', 'my_files']`, with `protect_from_jarvis` HIDDEN from the model, which is exactly how a chat answer misses a capability the PC has. The model's `TOOL_HINTS` now carry the owner's own vocabulary (restrict / restriction / folder-level / unrestrict / stop Jarvis / let Jarvis ... again / what is restricted / is Jarvis blocked), and every one of the seven sentences now shows the tool. (2) A sentence the fast path did match was answered with the one-card rule and nothing happened - and its "is the tool offered" test compared GATE ACTION names (`protect_item`) against a list of TOOL names, so it ALWAYS said the tool was not offered and pointed at Settings. A concrete sentence is now its own mutating intent (`protection_apply`) that calls the feature's OWN doors - `jarvis_protection.handle_propose` (ONE `protect_item` card), `handle_remove` (ONE `unprotect_item` card), and `handle_get`/`status_for` for the read - so the card, its words, its tier, the store and the audit line are the feature's own and nothing is loosened without a card. **The model tool `protect_from_jarvis` gained `action` = `add` | `remove` | `list`** (default `add`, so every existing caller is unchanged): add and remove each raise their ONE ordinary card; `list` changes nothing, so it answers with NO card - the whole list, or `check: true/false` for ONE named target - using the same "nothing to approve" shape the phone's app list already uses. A sentence that names a PATH acts on that path; one that only DESCRIBES a folder ("the folder with my medical scans") names no path, so the answer ASKS for the whole path and quotes the sentence to repeat - no target is ever guessed, and it never falls back to a generic "I cannot", which is the failure the owner reported. A private chat refuses the change like every other mutation. **Phone: nothing one-sided and no client change** - both apps chat through the same `/api/chat`, so the same fast path and the same server-side tool loop serve the phone, and the existing Settings plate keeps reading `/api/protection` and raising the same removal card; `tools/check_parity.py` is unchanged and green (the only PC-only surface stays `POST /api/protection/add`, for the reason already in ARCHITECTURE §8). **Enforcement is untouched:** all eleven points named in `jarvis_protection.py` still import and ask the module (documents, the agent's file tools, note capture, the notes vault, attachments, File Guardian, opening a program, UI control, screen capture, the scheduler, generated pictures), and none of them was edited. `jarvis_protection.py`, `jarvis_agent.py` and `jarvis_quick.py` are modules this repository ships whole, so each lands as the whole file in `backend/` and its byte-identical twin in `jarvis-backend/`; the tool-eval fallback `tools/tool_eval/jarvis_tools.json` was regenerated from the live table (the tool stays inside its 300-token budget at 269). - **Say "record call" and your phone records the call; this PC transcribes it, labels who spoke and files a new Obsidian note named for the date and time (2026-11-04).** The owner's ask, in their own words: *"add the ability of jarvis to record a call if I tell it a keyword 'record call' where it will record all the audio, transcribe it, put a date and identify the speakers in the transcription, and store all of it in a new obsidian note labeled with the date and time"* - the call being taken through the Android Jarvis app. **The honest platform fact first:** Android does not let an ordinary app capture the call's own audio stream (`VOICE_CALL` is privileged; his primary phone is a Google Pixel 9), so the phone records **through its microphone with the call on speaker** and uploads that, and the far end is heard through the speaker - quieter and noisier than a system recorder would give. That is said on the card, in the docs and in the note itself, and importing a file from the phone's own call recorder is a later addition that is **not built**. This pull request is the **PC half**, one shipped module (`backend/jarvis_call_notes.py`) with five routes installed by its own `install()` through `plugins/ready/call-notes` - no patch: `POST /api/call/recording/start|chunk|finish`, `GET /api/call/recording` (+`?session=`) and the PC-only `POST /api/call/recording/delete`, 16 kHz mono s16le PCM, chunks in order from `seq` 1 at most 512 KiB each, a `receipt` that is the frozen contract's one-line STRING plus the structured `recording`, `finish` requiring `consent_notice: "on"` and starting the transcription on a daemon thread so the request never waits for the model. It reuses the existing local reader (`jarvis_media_read.read_media`, sherpa-onnx, English only, in 9-minute parts because its own ceiling is 10 minutes), the owner's enrolled voice print and the real speaker model (`jarvis_voice.find_profile` + `EcapaEmbedder`/`StrongEmbedder` (whichever the print was made with) + `cosine`, then clustering at 0.55 up to six, numbered in first-speech order; with no model or no trained print **every line says "Speaker"** and the note records why - never a guessed name), and the notes editor's own create path (`jarvis_notes_edit.handle_create`, so the ONE `edit_vault_note` card, File Guardian copy and undo receipt are unchanged - a call can therefore raise TWO cards, the start and the note). The note is a NEW `Calls/YYYY-MM-DD HHMM - Call.md` with `date`, `started_at`, `duration`, `source` ("phone call, speaker recording"), `speakers`, `audio`, `session`, `consent` ("Recorded locally; tell the other person") and `[HH:MM:SS] You: ...` lines in the time of day they were said; if the vault is missing or invalid the transcript is still written as `transcript.md` beside the audio and that path is returned with a plain sentence, so a recording is never lost. **It is off by default** (`[call_recording] enabled = false`, a hand edit - no in-app switch, the same shape `github_search` uses), and starting is ONE `record_call` approval card at tier `ask` because it captures *other people's* speech. The eight whole messages ("record call", "record this call", "record the call", "start recording the call", "start call recording", "stop recording", "stop the call recording", "stop call recording") are answered by `jarvis_quick.py` whole-message only, and the answer carries the new additive `X-Jarvis-Route` field `call_record: {"action": "arm"|"stop"}` that the Android app acts on; with the feature off the reply says so and the field is absent. Registered in the repo's own machinery: `features/features.json` (+ the two app copies and the regenerated catalogue), `contract/feature-controls.json` (one Command-Only row, 103/43/2/16/12), `jarvis_asks_first.py`'s page, `jarvis_card_words.py`, `jarvis_reach.py`, the framework's `[autonomy.tiers]` and `[call_recording]`, `_where.py` and `apply-patches.ps1`'s SHIPPED lists, and `plugins/registry.json` (all regenerated by their own tools). **Proved by** `backend/test_call_notes.py` - 211 checks: byte-exact chunk assembly behind a canonical WAV header, out-of-order/oversized/consent refusals, fake transcriber segments into the note body, fake embedders for the owner match, the clusters and both degrade cases, the note name and frontmatter, the vault-missing fallback, the phrase parser and whole-message rule, the directive, the feature-off refusal, the PC-only read route and the install wrapper. **Recorded, not hidden:** the gate's `_RISK` table now HAS a row for `record_call` (`("yes", "local", ...)`, added 2026-11-05 by this fix), so its card no longer prints the generic "unclassified action ... able to leave this PC" warning whose second half was wrong for this action; the phone's recorder is its own pull request against that contract and neither lane drove a real call on the Pixel 9, so the speaker path and its words are NOT-TESTABLE until the owner's field test; the delete route is PC-only and behind its own `delete_call_recording` card, and recordings are kept until the owner deletes them (no timer; the 400-recording cap refuses rather than deletes - `docs/CALL-RECORDING.md` section 7); a repeated chunk `seq` is now accepted idempotently (200, `already: true`) instead of 409, so a crash between the PC's 200 and the phone's own bookkeeping can no longer brick a recording; and **no real phone recording, transcription, speaker model, vault write or approval card was driven** - those rows are NOT-TESTABLE, never passed.
- **The phone can record a call when you say "record call", and your PC turns it into a dated note (2026-11-04).** Say "record call" to Jarvis (or press Arm in Settings, Voice, Call recording) and the next call on this phone is recorded: a notification stays up for the whole call with the clock, Stop and the reminder "Recording - tell the other person", and the audio goes to your own PC as it is made. The PC turns it into words, dates it, works out who was speaking and writes one note in Obsidian named with the date and time. The honest limit is in the notification and in the card: Android does not let a normal app record the call's own audio, so this records the phone's MICROPHONE with the call on speaker - both voices through the air - and if the phone refuses to switch the call to speaker the notification says "Turn the call on speaker so Jarvis can hear both sides" instead of claiming both sides were caught. A dropped connection loses nothing: every piece is written to the phone's own storage first, and a failed send is retried with the same number. A crash between the PC's own 200 and the phone's bookkeeping used to make that retry ask for a number the PC already had, which answered 409 for ever (2026-11-05's privacy audit, D3); the phone now reads the number the PC says it wants (`expected`), records every piece below it as sent and sends the real next one, so the recording recovers instead of being stuck. A recording the PC has not taken is kept and offered again - and, when the owner no longer wants it sent (a denied card, a PC that refuses it), the same card offers Delete behind a confirmation that says it is deleted from this phone only and cannot be undone (D7). While it is armed or recording, Jarvis Live, "hey Jarvis" and the talk button keep their microphones closed (they are paused, not stopped, and come back when you disarm), and nothing on the phone turns speech into words or writes to the vault. **NOT tested on a real call from this session** - the owner's own Pixel 9 is the field test, after this and the PC half land.

- **A GitHub watcher has to earn the right to interrupt: `observe` mode, ONE message per pull request, and no approval card lost across a restart (2026-11-04).** A background watcher that speaks about every check is a watcher the owner mutes, so the four mechanisms the owner adopted from the `dsh-superagent` spec (Part II patterns 1, 2, 3 and 5B) are now built natively. **Pattern 1:** `WATCH_MODES = ("off", "observe", "active")`, and a new proactive rule defaults to `observe` - it runs the whole pipeline (poll, batch, gate) and writes one structured decision row instead of interrupting, served by the new `GET /api/watch/decisions?limit=50` with a CLOSED reason code (`ci_all_required_green`, `ci_required_failed`, `ci_still_running_debounced`, `duplicate_sha_state`, `observe_shadow_logged`, `filtered_bot_actor`, ...) and `preview_text`, the exact one-line message that would have been shown. **Pattern 2:** a pull request is one thread, `pr:<number>:<head_sha[:9]>`, because its seven required checks (`rust`, `frontend`, `backend`, `backend-windows`, `credential-manager`, `powershell-5`, `phone-unit-tests`) finish minutes apart: any required failure speaks ONCE immediately, all seven green AND mergeable speaks ONCE, and while any required check is still running with none failed it says nothing (`ci_still_running_debounced`). `audit` and `python-advisories` are informational - red on `main` while merges land - and are dropped by name before any count, so they can never trigger a notification. Idempotent receipts in `watch-receipts.json`, keyed `(pr_number, head_sha, terminal_verdict)`, mean twenty polls of one commit alert once, while a re-run that changes the verdict is a second, genuinely new sentence. **Pattern 3:** the gate is `backend/jarvis_watch_policy.py`, which imports nothing from Jarvis and nothing that can reach a disk, a network or a model - so "a filtered event never reaches the costly stage" is structural, not promised - and `assess()` runs only for a failed REQUIRED check, reading the failing run's log through the same `gh` path the poll uses. No model is called: the summarizer seam exists and nothing passes one. **Pattern 5B:** `backend/jarvis_outbox.py` writes every parked approval card and every job-completion notice to `outbox.json` with a deterministic `(kind, key)` BEFORE it is published (temp file, flush, rename), and `jarvis_jobs._init()` re-announces whatever is still owed, once per process - which closes the restart card loss, where the job row survived but the event that told the apps about it did not. A card is settled by being ANSWERED, not by being announced, so an unanswered card survives a restart; rehydration approves nothing. The limit is stated rather than hidden: this is at-least-once, so a crash between the send and the settle repeats one notice, never loses one. Nothing is always-on - the watcher is a job body (`watch_pr_checks`) that runs only when a job names a pull request, asks `github_read` before it reads GitHub, and starts no thread or timer - and nothing here pushes, merges, labels or comments. `backend/test_watch_ci.py` (139 checks) and `backend/test_outbox.py` (63) are plain Python with a fake clock and a fake `gh` runner, and they prove observe-vs-active (observe calls the notifier ZERO times), the quiet period, fail fast, the all-green settle, informational checks ignored, duplicate-receipt silence, `gate` never calling `assess` for a filtered event, and a crash between the write and the send being delivered exactly once afterwards. Both new modules are shipped whole (twin files in `jarvis-backend/`), the route comes from the drop-in folder `plugins/ready/watch-decisions/` rather than a patch, and `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §186 and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §14 document it.

The version gap is now `DEF-036` in both register files: the About card's number is the STAMPED build version (`update.rs:244-246`), the only literal `0.2.0` inside the running program is the startup log line (`lib.rs:1855-1857`, `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` from `Cargo.toml:3`), and the live backend folder has no `VERSION` file, so `/api/self/version` answers `"unknown"` (`backend/jarvis_self_portrait.py:621-638`) and the two-halves handshake can never call the pair in sync.
