Two of the three asks were already true before this change and are now held by a test: the phone's mic press has run no owner check since 2026-11-02 (`jarvis_speech._is_quick_message`, `_QuickMessage`), and "hi Jarvis" on the phone has always been checked. The gap was the third: `jarvis_live.Live.trust_decision()` demanded a full sentence and then ran the strict check on the FIRST clip of every Live session (the 2026-11-01 "verified once per session" rule), so starting Live from an unlocked phone still asked. There is now ONE decision - `backend/jarvis_live.py`'s `voice_check_needed(trigger, device, locked, setting_on)` - with one docstring stating the seven steps in order and exactly four cases: (a) the mic press never checks; (b) "hi Jarvis" while the phone is LOCKED checks, and it is the only check left (an UNLOCKED phone's "hi Jarvis" is meant to skip too, but the wake route cannot carry the lock state until the patch wave, so that clip is still checked today - MORE than the rule asks, never less: DEF-033); (c) Live started from an UNLOCKED phone does not check; (d) ONE setting, `voice_check_locked`, ON by default, and its two directions run opposite to "a check": ON is the EXEMPTION the owner asked for, so turning it ON is the looser direction and raises ONE `change_own_config` approval card, while turning it OFF is at once because it withdraws the exemption and gives the OLD, FULL checks back - the phone's "I am unlocked" is then ignored, and OFF is never "no checks". The phone sends its own screen-lock state as one new field on the EXISTING `POST /api/voice/live` start body (`"locked": true|false`, `jarvis-client`'s `VoiceCheckRule.lockedField`), and nothing else: no new route, no new permission, no new tier. **Fail closed, and the old behaviour is the fallback:** `locked` is believed only when the phone really said true or false; a missing value (every app older than this change sends none) reads as "did not say" and keeps the check, and a session on the DESKTOP keeps the 2026-11-01 rule unchanged because a PC has no locked phone. A phone Live session started from an unlocked phone runs no speaker model at all, and because its "trusted" verdict carries no strictness, nothing that needs a real check is read aloud on it - the session earned no privilege, it simply was not asked to prove itself. The one setting is read and written through the SAME existing Live route (`{"do":"voice_check"}`, with no `enabled` meaning read), so no route was added; its file (`<config>/live/voice-check.json`) holds one boolean and a damaged file reads as ON, never off. **The desktop has no switch for it yet and that is reported, not hidden:** the phone's Settings, Voice card carries the toggle ("Only check my voice on a locked phone"), the spoken phrases work on both apps ("turn off only checking my voice on a locked phone"), and `contract/feature-controls.json` records the missing desktop row as a gap (`planned`, owner `setup-ui`). Proved by two new suites: `backend/test_voice_check_rule.py` - 61 checks, 0 failed - holds the four cases row for row, the fail-closed rows, the card semantics (ON is 202 while one card waits, a denied card changes nothing, OFF withdraws a waiting card), and drives the real `jarvis_speech.hear()` with `jarvis_voice.verify` counted to prove a phone mic press never reaches the speaker model, and `jarvis-client`'s `VoiceCheckRuleTest` holds the phone's copy of the same table plus the start body's exact bytes and the corrected Live-screen sentence. `backend/test_live.py` stays green (414 passed, 0 failed) with its "Live writes no file" pin NARROWED and proved harder rather than dropped: the one save function is cut out of the source before the search, and the file it writes is read back and must hold one boolean and nothing else. The shared `live-cases.json` fixtures are untouched, because the setting deliberately adds no `status` field - a status key would have rewritten both apps' fixture for one boolean.
- **The tray offers "Update Jarvis to <version>" only while an update exists, and pressing it installs that version (2026-11-03).** The owner asked for a right-click row that "appears if there is an update to jarvis". It used to sit in the "More…" submenu permanently, reading "Jarvis Desktop 0.2.0" and disabled when there was nothing newer; now `tray.rs`'s `update_row` is the whole presence rule (no update means the row is *absent*, not greyed out) and `on_update_status` adds or removes the row from the menu, because Tauri 2.12's `MenuItem` has no `set_visible`. The label names the version the check found (`Update Jarvis to 0.2.411`) or falls back to `Update Jarvis`. Pressing it runs the same `update::install_update` the Settings Install button runs - never a second updater and never anything automatic - after turning the row into "Updating Jarvis to <version>…" so a second press cannot start a second download, with a toast carrying the "Jarvis closes while this installs" sentence the Settings card shows. On Windows a successful install ends the process and the next launch starts with no row; a failure re-reads the real state and rebuilds the row from it. Availability is the existing check's own answer (`update::available_version`, read from `UpdateState`), not a second network path. No App-lock gate is added: `lock::may_open` gates *opening a covered window* and its unlock path opens one, while the update commands themselves never ask App lock - the same rule the tray's Quit, Stop everything and backend rows already follow.
- **Storage self-scan and safe temporary-file cleanup (2026-11-03).** Jarvis can now take a bounded inventory of this PC - per-disk space and the folders it actually uses (its own program folder, the repository, `~/.openjarvis`, Ollama's models and `%TEMP%`) - and name every temporary-file candidate with exact bytes and times: Python `__pycache__`/`.pyc`, its own `_jarvis-logs`, old `_jarvis-deploy-backup-*` folders and `.before-`/`.backup-`/`.old-` copies, and its own prefixed `%TEMP%` files. A cleanup is a dry-run plan built only from that explicit allowlist, and it runs only after ONE approval card naming every path: cache is deleted, logs and old snapshots are moved to `_jarvis-quarantine-<yyyy-mm-dd>` and never deleted, `~/.openjarvis` (memory, history, receipts) is refused, and a plan is single-use and stops at the first item that changed. Standard library only; no network, no elevation.
- **Jarvis can free the graphics cards in hours the owner sets, and wake on the next question (2026-11-03).** The owner asked "jarvis should have the ability to offload the gpus during standby hours: can i set standby hours for you?" and chose "Unload the GPUs in my hours". The keys were already in his `[power]` section and **read by nothing** - the file annotated `schedule_mode` and `idle_mode` `# not read`, and it was right: `jarvis_power.current()` returned a hard-coded `"quiet"` inside the window and never called `should_standby()` at all, so a window he set could never be anything but Quiet and freed nothing. Now `current()` returns `schedule_mode` inside the window and `idle_mode` when the idle timer runs out, still computed from the clock on every call with no background thread flipping a variable and no second copy of the mode anywhere; a mode the owner chose always wins, and a `manual` flag stops the window overruling his own tap until the clock's answer next changes (which his settings file already promised at line 1492). A new `enforce()` makes the clock's answer real: it calls `jarvis_power_switch.set_mode("standby", why="the standby hours", force=True)` - the ONE function here that unloads, the same call a tap on Standby makes - so every model on every card is freed through the existing path and the answer says which, and at the window's end it wakes only a standby its own rules made, warm-up included. `force` is what stops the feature shipping broken: inside the window `current()` already READS standby while the stored mode is still `active`, so without it `set_mode` answers "Already standby." and frees nothing. **Nothing is unloaded while something is using it** - a multi-step task, a turn being answered (`jarvis_events.activity()` at `thinking`/`speaking`/`working`), a Live conversation, or a waiting approval card each hold it off with a plain reason in `status()["last_hold"]`, and the same guard sits in `set_mode` before the card and again after it, so a tap on Standby gets the same 409. The setting is four rows in `jarvis_limits.LIMITS` - "Keep Jarvis quiet during my hours", "Unload the graphics cards during my hours", "My hours start", "My hours end" - so both apps draw it from the one table with **no client change** (kinds `bool`/`time`, `app` `"both"`, `pc_only` False, the unload row a switch over the word `standby`/`quiet`), defaulting to today's behaviour (off, quiet, 23:00-07:00) so a PC that never touches it behaves exactly as before and starts no ticker; all four carry `always_asks` and go to the `change_own_config` card in either direction, and a value set to what it already is raises none. Tests: `backend/test_standby_hours.py` (152 checks - the whole decision table including a midnight-crossing window, the unload driven against a FAKE `jarvis_models` and a fake Ollama so no real model can be freed, a refusing unload that must not raise, all four in-flight holds, the `force` bug, and the rows' defaults/words/card), plus the four existing suites it touches (`test_power_switch.py` 77, `test_standby_schedule.py` 70, `test_limits.py` 353, `test_limits_settings_route.py` 43) and the three base/twin checkers. **Not measured on a real card:** no window was run against the owner's Ollama here, and the first-question delay after standby is the existing standby path's measured 5-15 s, not a new measurement.
- **Nine more settings families leave an undo receipt when you change them by asking (2026-11-03).** Changing your wake word, which browser Jarvis uses, an anti-slop scope, the speaking speed, either captcha hand-off choice, "ask me first" for one action, how much of an approval card is shown, or offering a reading tool to the model now writes the same ONE receipt every other cardless setting change does - so "undo" in that chat puts the value back through that setting's own setter, and a card or a PC-only refusal still stops it. The Anti-Slop filter's own switch, mode and scopes already record their own receipt, and "undo" in the chat now finds that exact one - the id the filter returns, never "whatever row is newest", so it can never put back another chat's or another screen's change. A change that only waits on a card writes no receipt, a sentence that changes nothing ("turn on the wake word" while it is already on) writes none either - before that guard its undo quietly switched the microphone off - and when the current value genuinely cannot be read the change is made without a receipt rather than with a guessed "before".
- **Self portrait, named places, one-card conversation clear, and asking by chat (2026-11-03).** Jarvis can now say what it is made of: `GET /api/self` reports 190 places imported from the two registries that already hold them (59 Settings sections from `jarvis_settings_registry.SECTIONS` and 131 menus from `jarvis_menus.MENUS`, never a hand-written list), 46 settings with their live values where one can be read (35 switches, 10 choices, 1 number), what asks first (135 rows), 175 abilities, the drop-in plugins, the three stores with how each is cleared, and the installer's recorded identity - fixed registry data and live state only, never a token, key, secret, memory or chat word, owner path or model sentence, and an unreadable value says "unknown" never "off". `GET /api/self/version` gives the Update button the version STRING at `version.app_version` plus `version.deploy` (the installer's recorded sha256 for the live gate/hud/skills modules and the resealed commit), so both halves can be compared honestly; `POST /api/self/refresh` re-reads the portrait now and answers one plain sentence with what moved, no card and no restart. "Open a place" keeps the existing per-answer `X-Jarvis-Route` field (no new event kind): `resolve_place()` resolves the registries' own aliases - including a settings sub-row opening its parent card - and refuses rather than jumping anywhere dead. Conversation ids already existed (both clients send one per request and `jarvis_chat_log` keeps one row per id), so `GET /api/conversations` and `GET /api/conversations/<id>` are thin aliases onto the one History store, and by chat `self_portrait`, `conversation_find` (titles and dates only, never the words - the 2026-09-28 search decision), `conversation_open` (one kept chat's turns, local model only) and `refresh_abilities` are read-only with no card. Clearing is two-phase and per item: ONE `conversation_clear` card at tier `ask` names the exact chat by title and message count, says it cannot be undone, that the facts Jarvis learned are KEPT and that copies in older backups age out, and deletes nothing until a person approves; the model is deliberately NOT given a clear tool (Gemini ruling 1: an LLM must never have an autonomous way to wipe the transcript) - clearing is the route, an app UI action or the fast path only; there is no bulk form, no cardless form, and no memory-clear route added (memory keeps its own Forget and Forget a time frame flows). Also fixed: the ONE number setting (the Jarvis Live quiet timeout) is reachable by the `change_setting` tool, not only by speech; the dead duplicate `TOOL_GROUPS` definition is gone; and a cached unlocked portrait could have handed App lock's withheld counts to a locked request - only the unlocked portrait is cached now. The storage self-scan's routes and tool group are wired defensively (loaded only when `jarvis_storage_health.py` is on the PC; absent today, so no storage route is served and the four shipped tool groups are exactly as before).
- **Scheduled tasks can run any job in the owner's own words, and never as two cards (2026-11-03).** A reminder's `run-task` action may now carry `job` - a phrase in the owner's words, up to 240 characters - instead of only the closed `briefing`/`backup` names (which are unchanged). The phrase is resolved through the same `jarvis_quick.match` path chat uses when it is saved (an unresolvable phrase, or one asking for a shell/command/script, is refused in one plain sentence) and again at fire time (a phrase that no longer resolves raises no card and runs nothing). A phrase that resolves to an intent raising its OWN approval card (`forget_range`, `update_start`, a carded setting change, a repeating briefing, "read this link", …) is refused when the reminder is saved, in one honest sentence saying it needs the owner's approval each time, naming what the phrase matched and saying it was not saved - so one scheduled task can never put a second card on screen; a stored row that resolves to one later is refused at fire time too (no card, nothing runs, `needs_approval` in the audit, and the row says why). Every intent the resolver can return is classified, and an unclassified one is refused conservatively. At fire time a cardless job raises exactly ONE `schedule_action` card, tier ask, naming the action in plain words and saying nothing happens before a yes; denial/timeout runs nothing. Approved, it runs through `jarvis_quick.run` - the same executor chat uses - so the module adds no shell, no command line and no second interpreter. The owner's words never reach the audit log or the card's `detail`. Both apps' Reminders screens still send only the closed name; that one-sided gap is recorded in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 as a follow-up.
- **Reminders can be routines: up to 12 parts, each with its own time and its own buttons (2026-11-03).** "Remind me at 8 to start the laundry, then at 8:30 move it to the dryer, then at 9 fold it" sets one reminder with timed parts; "morning routine at 7: 1. meds 2. keys 3. badge" sets a checklist whose parts come up one after another. Each part is one notification, each part has its own Done / record / snooze buttons and its own destination (history, today's Obsidian note, a goal, a habit), and an existing reminder's question or buttons can now be edited in place instead of deleting it and retyping it. Creating a routine in chat needs no card and leaves one Undo receipt, so Undo outlives the 120-second "cancel that" window; only a part that runs a task raises the usual schedule card. Honest limits: the PC is still the clock, so a part that goes off while the phone is away is not pushed later; a part more than 12 hours missed is skipped and counted rather than notified; the Windows toast names the part in words but carries no per-part buttons; and the phone answers parts and never creates or edits a routine, because a part's destination can be a folder on this PC.
- **The Coding preset's window grows to 32,768 tokens, with its 323.5 MiB spill measured and capped (2026-11-03).** The pooled both-card lane now asks for 32,768 tokens instead of 16,384 - the largest rung measured to load on this PC - at 16,513.7 MiB with 323.5 MiB in system RAM and speed inside the model's own noise (80.36 vs 79.88 tok/s median on three short prompts; the whole ladder from 16,384 to 32,768 was measured through the same shipped path, and only 16,384 loads with zero spill). `jarvis_big_coder.load_coder` gains a narrow `allow_spill` argument that only this lane passes, capped at 352 MiB - the measurement plus about 9% - so the default and every other caller still refuse ANY spill, the big-coder mode's 28,672-token zero-spill load is unchanged, and a load above the cap is still refused with both the actual spill and the allowance named. A 15-minute real coding test runs after deployment; the measurement configured the window, it did not fill it.
- **The phone can open any place Jarvis names, and clearing a conversation now asks first (2026-11-03).** Two closes for the same gap: "open X" answered by the PC used to know only the Settings registry's section ids, so "open Live", "open history", "open memory" or "open my goals" landed at the top of Settings, and a conversation's Delete went through without the PC's own approval card. Now `OpenPlace` (the same closed table `OpenPlaceTest` holds to the real registry) also resolves whole screens, the Brain's plates, the shared menu ids from `backend/jarvis_menus.py`, and says so in one plain sentence for the places this build has no screen for yet (Habits, Mood, Plugins) - through the existing `X-Jarvis-Route` field and the existing one-time request, with no new event kind, no Navigation Compose, no deep link and no new `Screen` entry. Conversation Delete is two-phase and per item: One request names exactly one conversation id, the PC raises ONE card naming that conversation and saying it cannot be undone and that the facts it taught are kept, and nothing is deleted until the owner answers it - the phone keeps the row and says "waiting for your approval" rather than reporting a delete that has not happened. There is no bulk clear and no cardless path.
- **"Personalize Jarvis": the setup questionnaire becomes a 25-question quiz in 7 sections (2026-11-03).** The same Settings card, stepped one question at a time, with a "show only new/unanswered" filter and a retake that no longer wipes the answers you skipped. One quiet toast and a HUD line until it is done, both dismissible; nothing applies without the existing card, and the phone stays read-only.
- **The Brain's Memory tab now opens on the cards waiting for you (2026-11-03).** The owner reported that when he clicked the HUD's "N memory cards waiting for you" notice, the pending cards he came to decide were "towards the bottom" of the list, not at the top. "Waiting for you" was the tenth card on the Memory tab - behind Learning, "Bring in old chats", Topics, "Saved automatically", "Always keep in mind", "Between us", the person dossier and "What Jarvis knows about you" - so it is now the FIRST card on that tab, above the Learning card and every saved list, with its own `<h2>Waiting for you</h2>` and its `#memory-proposals` list kept exactly as they were. The view is also scrolled back to that queue whenever the Memory tab is shown, so a window left halfway down its saved facts cannot hide the cards again; the scroll moves the page only and never takes focus, so the rail's own tab keeps it and a screen reader does not hear the heading twice. What does not change: one card is still one decision (Keep / Discard, "Both are true", "Stop using this fact", exactly as before), no route or queue rule is touched, the HUD still decides nothing, and no Rust or backend file changed. The notification path was measured rather than assumed: the HUD's notice and its Memory-tab list both invite the owner to "Review in the Brain", which calls the existing `open_fix_place {place:"brain"}`, and the Brain's own landing view already IS Memory (`brain.js`, `landing`), so putting the queue first is what makes that click land on it. `node tests/memory.mjs` pins the new place in the page, the queue above the saved list, and the first waiting row on screen in a fresh window.
- **Facts now save around a bad turn, a busy sensitive check gets one patient retry, and the reworded switch rechecks the cards it waited on (2026-11-03).** Three repairs in `jarvis_auto_learn.py`, from the memory review's measurements on the owner's PC (five passes, zero facts saved, six carded). ONE bad turn no longer cards the whole learning pass: each fact is saved from the clean turns that hold its words (`_attributed`), with Gemini's two hardenings - the words must fit one clean turn or two consecutive clean turns, never stitched across a turn that read outside text, and a pass with any tool turn or re-sent words may not use "Save facts even when Jarvis had to reword them" to skip the grounding check. A sensitive-topic check that could not RUN is asked once more after a 1.5 s pause with a 30 s deadline before the fact is carded; a clean second answer saves, a second failure is still a card and still counted as the fault it is. And turning the reworded switch on rechecks the pending cards whose only reason was "not in your own words" (`recheck_pending_proposals`, also on every later pass): they save with `meta.reworded`, at most five per call. The other two old card reasons need the pass's turns, which were never stored, so those cards stay for the owner's yes - said plainly. `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §19, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `backend/README.md` say the same; `backend/test_auto_learn.py` carries Gemini's three named test pins plus the recheck and the injectable pause.
- **Jarvis can read your GitHub, and take three small actions on it - each behind its own card, and it can never merge, push or close (2026-11-03).** The owner's decision was "Read + actions": six tools in `backend/jarvis_github.py`, and one module that talks to `api.github.com` and nothing else. Three read: `github_list` (your repositories, a repo's open pull requests, its open issues, its recent workflow runs - a closed set of four names, never an address the model wrote), `github_read_file` (one file, at an optional branch) and `github_ci_status` (the newest run for a branch or a pull request). Three act, one card each: `github_comment`, `github_open_issue` and `github_rerun_workflow`. All six ask a person every time - the reads included, because a read still sends the GitHub token saved on this PC out to a server - and they are in `NEEDS_A_PERSON` as well as at tier `ask`, so loosening the setting cannot make one run with nobody asked. They are deliberately NOT the existing `github_read` action, which is the scheduled look a "tell me when" GitHub watch makes and must stay `auto`; their own action is `github_inspect`. There is no merge, push, commit, delete or close ANYWHERE: no planner, no endpoint and no tool, and the words say why. The token is never printed, a redirect is refused rather than followed, every answer is bounded, and every failure is a sentence with no HTTP code in it. `backend/github-tools.patch` gives the gate its four actions, since `jarvis_gate.py` is not shipped whole. All six ship SWITCHED OFF, like `github_search`; add the names to `[tools].enabled` and say "connect GitHub". Proved by `backend/test_github_tools.py` (184 checks, no network, no real token: a socket opened anywhere in it fails the run).
- **The focus-presets feature row now says what the Coding preset's heavy lane really does, and stops saying it refuses until a lane that already landed (2026-11-03).** The `focus-presets` row of `features/features.json` still claimed "The Coding preset's heavy mode refuses until its both-card lane support lands". That stopped being true when #1106 ("the Coding preset runs on one pooled both-card lane", merged 2026-11-03) landed the pooled lane and `decisions.d/2026-11-02-coding-preset-pooled-both-card-lane.md` recorded it: the Coding preset's own row is `lane="pooled"`, `heavy_mode=True`, `context=16384`, and `backend/jarvis_model_lanes.py`'s `start_pooled_lane` really starts it - raising the one `switch_model` card before it pauses the other two models, and changing nothing if the card is declined. The row now says exactly that, scopes the old declined-card sentence to the other eight presets (the heavy path is the exception, which `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 145.1 already said), and says the pooled lane runs at the 32,768-token window that #1129 landed (merged as 9cf55df68 on 2026-11-03, after this row was first written), measured on this PC on 2026-11-03 at 323.5 MiB spilled into system RAM with a 352 MiB cap, while 16,384 stays the largest rung with no spill. Its id, group, title, what, where, asks, surface, aliases, covers, gate and the approved label counts are untouched. Every copy moved in the same touch: the three byte-identical `features.json` copies, and the two generated catalogues (`backend/jarvis_feature_catalogue.py` and its `jarvis-backend/` twin) written by `tools/gen_feature_guide_catalogue.py`, never hand-typed. Checks: `check_feature_list` 13 passed / 0 failed (175 rows), `backend/test_feature_list.py` 61/0, `backend/test_feature_guide.py` 2279/0, `check_feature_controls` clean (175/175; labels 12/102/16/2/43), `gen_feature_guide_catalogue --check`, `gen_feature_directory --check` for both the desktop and the phone, `check_parity`, `check_stale_twins`, `test_base_matches_repo` 136/0 and `test_base_regeneration` 39/0. Not done, said plainly: the live backend, desktop build, phone and model were not touched, and one adjacent sentence was left alone because it is not this row - `tools/check_feature_list.py`'s `TEACHING_GAP` reason for `focus-presets` still says its one action is disabled until the lane/apply patch, which is now stale for the same reason and is a separate fix.
- **A bare pasted link is read behind one card that names its address, four natural sentences now answer from the PC instead of the local model, and "yes"/"no" are ordinary words again unless a card is really waiting (2026-11-03).** Three measured fast-path gaps closed in `jarvis_quick.py` (and its `jarvis-backend` twin). (1) D1: a whole message of "yes", "Yes", "yes please" or "no" returned the canned "Approvals are decided on the card itself..." sentence UNCONDITIONALLY, so ordinary conversation was answered with a non-answer while no card existed at all; the matcher now asks this PC's own approvals table (`jarvis_gate.pending()`, through the module's one lazy gate import) and returns that intent ONLY while a card is waiting, and otherwise leaves "yes" to the model like any other sentence - it still cannot approve anything, and a gate that is missing or unreadable counts as "nothing waiting". (2) Q7, the owner's own words: "list my plugins" / "show my plugins" now reach the plug-in list (they matched nothing and the model has no plug-in tool); "which apps on my phone may you open" / "which apps can you open on my phone" / "what can you open on my phone" list the real `[phone_apps]` allow-list read-only through `jarvis_phone_apps.view()` - no card, no write, no package id printed, and the honest empty sentence when the table ships empty (before, the first fell to the model and the last got the generic feature-capability sentence that names no app); "which model is answering me" answers from the same records as "which model are you using"; and "where do I change <setting>, and what is it set to" reaches the SAME `setting_explain` the plain question does, whose words already print the real Settings place AND the current value (before, the compound sentence matched nothing and the model invented a `configuration.yaml` place). (3) Q2: a message that is ONLY an http(s) link, or a link plus a question about it ("https://... what is this about?"), now reaches the read-a-link path with the same ONE card per URL - the card is the reader's own, nothing is fetched before a yes, a decline fetches nothing, and a statement ("here is a link ...") or a browser command ("open <url> in my browser") keeps its own path. The answer's FIRST line now carries the canonical address the card showed (`Read from https://... - "<title>". It says: "..."`), so both apps make it tappable with no rendering change, and the page's words are kept IN MEMORY for that conversation for 900 seconds (one page per chat, at most eight chats, never on a private turn) so a follow-up - "what does it say about the limescale filter?" - is answered from words already on this PC with NO second card and NO second fetch, quoting around what it finds or saying plainly that the kept characters do not mention it. NOT in this change: the "Where this came from" source row (it needs `read_web_page` added to `jarvis_sources.KNOWN_TOOLS` and a seam in `jarvis_hud.py`, both outside this file - the turn is still marked `read=["read_web_page"]`), and the nine cardless receipt families (they need value readers that do not exist in `jarvis_settings_registry.py`). `backend/test_open_chat.py`, `test_read_link.py`, `test_plugins_honesty.py`, `test_preset_answers.py`, `test_setting_explain.py` and `test_phone_app_allowlist.py` prove each sentence, the no-card-waiting case, one card and one fetch per URL, the address on the first line, the zero-card follow-up and the 15-minute expiry.
- **Every setting now explains itself with its current value and the exact phrase that changes it, a change that loosens nothing leaves an undo receipt, Jarvis Live speaks one calm line while a card waits, and "read this link" reads one link behind one card - and the page-reader tool is deliberately NOT made switchable (2026-11-03).** Before this slice the explain door (`jarvis_settings_registry.find_explain_setting` / `explain_setting_words`) answered where a switch or a named choice lives and gave one example phrase, but never its current value, and the one number setting, the sun-and-moon switch, every animal switch, the per-device auto quality and the weather source could not be named at all. Now the explain door has the five missing kinds (`number`, `animal`, `device`, `sky` and `weather`), every value it prints is read through ONE entry point (`current_value` - a switch's own registered reader, `ChoiceSetting.now`, `NumberSetting.now`, `jarvis_animal.values()`, `jarvis_sky.view()`), and the answer prints `Right now: <the value>` beside the real Settings place and a phrase the real matcher accepts: a switch says *"turn on web search" or "turn off web search"*, a choice says *"set the personality to advocate"*, the number says *"set the jarvis live timeout to 3 minutes"* with its real range, and the sun-and-moon, animal and weather options say the same shape and that they are cosmetic, so no card is needed (the weather source's own line still says Open-Meteo asks on a card first, because it sends your rough position to the internet). When a reader cannot answer, the line is exactly *"I could not read its current value on this PC, so I will not guess."* - never a default dressed up as the value, and never the word None. `jarvis_feature_guide.state` / `how_to` answer a named choice as well as a switch, and the chat door now PRODUCES those two intents for a choice (it was bool-only), so "is the personality on?" is answered on the PC with the row's own value instead of reaching the model, and the things that cannot be changed by asking (`theme`, `hud layout` and every `NOT_BY_ASKING` row) still say so and name the row to open, while Auto adjust - which IS reachable by "turn on auto adjust" - gets its own honest answer instead of a false refusal: where it lives, the one fixed line saying its value is kept by the app that draws the face rather than guessed, and the phrase that really works. A change that loosens nothing is still immediate and now leaves ONE receipt in `jarvis_receipts` (tool name `change_setting`) - a switch, a named choice, the Live timeout, every animal switch, the sun-and-moon switch and the weather source (its two cardless directions, off and Home Assistant) - and the snapshot holds the VALUE each setter takes (a named choice's display word is resolved back through that row's own `options()`, `small_approvals` stores its bool, and the weather source stores its id, never the label); a change waiting on a card writes none, because nothing has happened yet, and so does a row whose value cannot be read or has no value to go back to (a face with none chosen, a focus preset with none applied). In the same chat, "undo" takes back the newest cardless settings change once, through that setting's own setter - so a reversal that loosens something raises that setting's own card - and a second "undo" says the setting is already back, a reversal that did not happen says which failure it was - the setter's own card when a card really was raised, otherwise the setter's own refusal words, never an invented card - keeps this chat's pointer so the next "undo" tries again, and a reminder or timer recorded before it still wins. The sentence the registry has always printed, "say undo in the same chat if you change your mind", is now true for a change that really happened. In Jarvis Live a carded change gets ONE calm spoken line instead of the setter's card id and list - *"A card is waiting for <the setting>, so approve it on your phone or PC and it changes."* - and the existing pause shows while the card is in the queue; nothing is approved by voice, and every read-only answer, an explain included, is still word for word the same in both doors, which `backend/test_live_parity.py` keeps pinned. "Read this link" and "read this YouTube video and tell me about it" now work in either app's chat: the sentence names one http(s) link and a read verb (a negated or past-tense statement - "don't read https://x", "i already read https://x yesterday" - raises no card, and "read this link" with no address answers "Say the address to read, starting with http:// or https://."), the YouTube caption reader is asked first and any other address goes to the page reader, and each link raises exactly ONE card under that reader's own action (`youtube_captions_read` or `read_web_page`), with only the first address in one message used. A "tell me when this page changes" watch still reaches the watcher, a declined or timed-out card fetches nothing and says so, captions are the only thing fetched from a video (never its sound or the video itself), the terms caveat on the YouTube card is `jarvis_youtube`'s own sentence, one page is read and a link on it is never followed, and after a link is read `change_setting` refuses in that same turn (`SETTINGS_AFTER_OUTSIDE`) because outside text shaped it. The page-reading TOOL itself is deliberately NOT made switchable - `read_web_page` stays in `jarvis_asks_first.TIER_C`, out of `TOOLS_SWITCHABLE`, still in `HARD_LIMITS` and `MUST_ASK`, so no app may turn it on and the settings file's `[tools].enabled` line is still the only way, by hand on the PC (`decisions.d/2026-11-03-page-reader-stays-unswitchable.md`). The chat path reads a page without it, by calling the page reader's own prepare/run behind the same `ask` card. `backend/test_setting_explain.py` proves every row's value or the fixed sentence, every printed phrase through the real matcher, and that explaining calls no setter at all; `backend/test_read_link.py` proves one card per link, the card's words byte for byte the reader's own, a declined card fetching nothing, no captions said plainly, and the watch still winning. No route, no model tool, no gate action and no tier changed for any of this.

- **Jarvis can explain which accounts are connected, what it may do with each, what can be changed, and how to disconnect or connect one (2026-11-03).** One read-only `GET /api/accounts` answers the owner's own question - "what accounts are actively connected to Jarvis, what permissions and abilities does it have for them, what's changeable, how do I disconnect, how do I connect a new one" - for twelve families: the private iCal link, CalDAV sign-in, Google Calendar, GitHub, email, Home Assistant, the search keys, the cloud-AI keys, the blind credential vault, the notes folder, and two honest non-entries (Notion is an export, not a sign-in; Spotify/Drive/Dropbox are not connectable and Jarvis says so rather than pretending). Search is approved for this conversation." - because the grant tool was never offered. It was a Settings, Tools, "Safety and sharing" switch that was off, so the model had no tool to call and no card could exist. Every job row now carries an immutable `created_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, the PC's local day), written once when the item is created and never rewritten - not at midnight, not by an edit, not by the mode switch - and an existing `schedule.db` is migrated once, from each row's own `created` stamp, or today for a legacy row with no usable one. Full daily rollover is the default: today's list is every open item, each older one tagged by the PC itself (1 day "from yesterday", 2-6 days "from <Weekday> (<N>d ago)", 7+ "from <MMM D>"), so a 3-day-old item never says "from yesterday"; "Day by day" instead keeps each item on the day it was written, under that day's heading, and switching between the two is lossless by construction (the same rows, the same `created_date`, only drawn differently). "Make a note: X" is answered by the PC's fast path with no model (`backend/jarvis_quick.py`'s `_run_note_make`), and while its card is up the WHOLE reply is the note-capture route's own 202 sentence, in practice the literal "Waiting for your approval." The line is matched on its question as well as its exact words, so two notes asked one after another in the same chat cannot swap their endings, and the settle also rewrites what the model is re-sent with the next question - never what is read aloud, which still goes through the private-answer gate. Additive on the wire: an answer that never left a note waiting carries no `note_job`, and an app that does not know the key (the desktop) shows the waiting line exactly as before - its own chat still says it, written down in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 rather than left quiet. Measured on `origin/main` with a throwaway JVM probe before any change: the Settings box answered `[]` for **"presets"**, **"preset"**, **"focus"**, **"focus presets"** and **"hardware"** - every one of the five words he might type - while the app's own "Find anything" box already answered `settings.focus-presets -> BRAIN/hardware` for four of them. Answering is a log line, cardless like ticking a to-do; the PC draws the question on its "Just went off" row and the phone on its notification, with an answer from the phone refused while it is locked. Jarvis Live, "Hey Jarvis" and the desktop's talk button still check every clip.

Both were false: Coding is `qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-ud-q3-k-xl`, heavy mode across both cards, applied only after ONE approval card. "Are you using both cards" reads the real lane state and says yes, not right now, or "I cannot read that"; an unknown preset name lists the real ones instead of inventing a model. No model call, no card, no cloud.
- **Plugins by chat: Jarvis lists its drop-in plugins and turns ONE on or off, one card per change (2026-11-02).** The owner decided: "Jarvis may list plugins and turn them on/off by chat, one card per change." Two existing facts made this a small door rather than a new system: `jarvis_plugins.py` already discovers every feature folder in `jarvis_plugins\` beside `jarvis_hud.py`, already switches one off with a `disabled` marker in that folder (or `"enabled": false` in its plugin.json), and already names every load, skip and failure in `status()`. Two model tools in `backend/jarvis_agent.py` now reach that from either app's chat: `plugin_list` names every plugin, whether it is on, and why it is off - a `disabled` marker, a hand-edited `plugin.json`, a load that failed (with the loader's own reason), a broken manifest, a folder added after Jarvis started, or a plugin whose folder has gone since (still running until the next restart) - and a missing plugin folder says so instead of showing an empty list. `plugin_switch` turns ONE named plugin on or off. **ON raises ONE approval card under the EXISTING `modify_own_code` action** (a plugin is program code that runs inside Jarvis at start-up, and the gate already ships that action at "ask"); **OFF is immediate and cardless**, the project's own on/off rule, because stopping only narrows what runs. Nothing here approves anything, and the tool is in `NEEDS_A_PERSON` as the belt: a loosened tier cannot switch a plugin on with nobody asked. **What a toggle means is said plainly, never pretended:** the loader runs once at HUD start-up, so neither direction is live in the running process, and every answer says the change lands the next time Jarvis starts and that Jarvis cannot restart itself - nothing restarts the backend. **No second mechanism and no delete:** OFF creates the loader's own `disabled` marker (`O_CREAT|O_EXCL`), ON removes that same marker and only after the folder and its `plugin.json` are still there; no folder is created, moved, renamed or deleted, `plugin.json` is never rewritten, and a plugin switched off in its own manifest is reported and refused as a hand edit. **No bulk, and no new route:** the schema takes one plugin name and an `on`/`off` action with no array, so a call naming two plugins is refused before anything is prepared; there is no `GET`/`POST` for any of this, no Rust command and no app screen, so `tools/check_parity.py` is unchanged and clean, no gate action, tier line, risk row or card wording is invented, and the card is the existing `modify_own_code` row already on the "What asks first" page. Both tools ship ON in `[tools].enabled` (a feature reachable only by hand-editing that same list would not be reachable by chat), are listed in `jarvis_reach.TOOL_NAMES`, sit in the `settings` short-list group, and carry tool-diet hints; `tools/tool_eval/jarvis_tools.json`, `reach-cases.json` and `private-aloud-cases.json` were regenerated by their own generators. The feature is on both apps' Features pages (`plugin-switch`), and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 records why neither app has a screen for it. `backend/test_plugin_switch.py` proves the list, the states, the read-only snapshot, the immediate OFF, the one card and the denied/timed-out/loosened refusals, the unknown-name refusal, no bulk, no delete, and a manifest-off plugin left unrewritten; the record is `docs/DECISIONS.md` 2026-11-02 and `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §181.
- **"Hey Jarvis" works in the picture-in-picture window (2026-11-02).** While Jarvis is in its small window on top of another app, saying "hey Jarvis" records ONE sentence and answers it as one ordinary turn: no Live session is started or needed, nothing brings the app back to full screen, and the answer is spoken through the existing voice path. - **Resetting the phone app can no longer read as "it forgot my voice": the PC keeps and reports the owner's saved voice, a damaged voice store is refused instead of silently reset to the defaults, and a re-paired phone reads the stored choice straight away (2026-11-02).** The owner's report: *"when I reset the jarvis Android app it changes the voice to the default. it doesn't seem to remember what I changed it to. fix it"*. Measured end to end: the phone's one app-level reset is Settings, Devices, **"Unpair & clear the token"** (`Devices.UNPAIR_BUTTON` -> `JarvisRuntime.unpairAndClearToken()` -> `POST /api/devices/remove` -> `jarvis_devices.remove()`), and that route writes the device registry only - it never touches `voices/state.json`, so the reset itself cannot change the voice (his own PC's audit log has no `devices.removed` since 2026-10-10, while the voice was overwritten with the pack default `af_heart` on 10-31, 11-01 and 11-02 by `POST /api/voice/voices/speaker`). What made that look like a reset, and made it stick, is now fixed: `GET /api/voice/voices` reported the voice that **speaks** as `speaker.choice`, so whenever the saved name was not the speaking one (a pack without it, a blend still being checked, a refused voice, a fresh install) both apps marked the pack default as the selection and there was nothing that said what the owner had actually chosen - the answer now also carries `speaker.saved`, the owner's own choice, null when he never made one. And a write to a `voices/state.json` that exists but cannot be read is now **refused with a 500 and the file left untouched**, instead of merging the change onto a full set of defaults and rewriting the owner's whole voice (speaker, speed, face voice, every animal) from one changed key - the same rule `jarvis_manner` already follows (data-integrity audit F3). The phone asks for the PC's voice the moment a pair connects (`refreshCustomVoices()` beside the post-pair appearance read), so a reset or reinstalled app shows the stored choice instead of staying on "Asking your PC…" until the Voices screen is opened, and its reset prompt now says the PC's settings - the voice Jarvis speaks in included - are kept. The phone's own JVM suite is green from `jarvis-client`: `gradlew.bat testDebugUnitTest --offline` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 3,097 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped, including the new `DevicesTest` check that the reset prompt says the PC's voice choice is kept. The cause is not the panel's height (the split gives the chat its own room and keeps its 132dp floor, unchanged) and not the state surviving the toggle (`peekChat` is `rememberSaveable`, `HomeScreen.kt:1302`): full screen composes **no conversation list at all**, so the list is laid out for the first *time* the moment the chat opens, and a `LazyColumn` laid out for the first time starts at its first row — the Home cards, then the collapsed "Earlier in this chat", then the question. Honest limits: no phone was driven from this lane — the APK that reaches the owner is CI's, so "the panel looks right on the real screen" is NOT-TESTED here; the panel is still only about 200dp tall in the owner's split, so a long answer is still read by scrolling inside it, which this change does not alter.
- **The apps Jarvis may open on your phone are now managed by approval card: add one, remove one, in chat or in Settings (2026-11-02).** The owner asked in these words: "any apps that i ask if to open or do something with. i would need to approve a card with the apps i would like it to manipulate first and i can remove or add any android app to that list any time with an approval card... or by going to the settings and changing it there too." PR #1067 gave Jarvis the ability to open a listed app on the phone, but the list that permits it (`[phone_apps]` in `jarvis-framework.toml`) ships EMPTY and could only be filled by hand-editing that file, so the feature could not be used at all without a text editor. It now has a management: a new `phone_apps` model tool (`list` / `add` / `remove`) in chat and in Live on both apps, and two routes for the settings screens - `GET /api/phone/apps` (read-only, the allowed apps by the names the owner wrote, and whether Jarvis can also search in each one) and `POST /api/phone/apps` (ONE app, and it raises ONE approval card first). **Every add and every removal is one card that names BOTH the friendly name and the exact package id** - `Let Jarvis open "YouTube Music" (com.google.android.apps.youtube.music) on your phone?` - and nothing is written until a person approves it; a denied card, a timed-out card, and a call refused before a card exists all leave the settings file byte-for-byte unchanged. **There is no bulk path**: one call carries one app, the tool's schema has no array for apps, and a list where a string belongs is refused in the owner's words before any card. The one line is written through the same config layer the other settings use (`jarvis_phone_apps.write` follows `jarvis_limits.py`/`jarvis_notify_prefs.py`: the owner's own text changed by exactly one line, the whole file re-parsed and compared, an atomic `os.replace`, then `reload_framework()` so the next message sees it - no bare `open(path, "w")` anywhere), and each applied change writes one local audit line, `phone_apps.added` or `phone_apps.removed`, naming the app and the package. The gate mapping needed no new action and no new patch: the tool is put to the gate under the existing `change_setting` key, which the published gate base already maps to `change_own_config` at its existing `ask` tier - the same action the other settings changes use - and `backend/test_phone_app_allowlist.py` proves that mapping is load-bearing (the tool's own name is not a gate key, so without it the gate would answer `unclassified_tool`); pre-fix the suite fails because the tool does not exist. `phone_apps` ships ON in `[tools].enabled`, because a tool that is itself the only way to fill a list that ships empty cannot be gated behind a hand edit of the same file; what it can reach is that ONE table, and `control_phone` - the tool that actually opens apps - is still opt-in, still `ask`, still one card printing every literal adb command. The chat/Live tool and the PC Settings write route are ONE permission model, not two. Honest limit, said plainly: the phone's Settings is a READ-ONLY list plus "ask Jarvis to add an app", not an editor - typing a friendly name AND a package id is deep config editing, which the standing rule keeps off the phone, and the phone is the one device that cannot look a package up; the owner's "or by going to the settings and changing it there too" is answered by the PC's Settings and by the same card from the phone's chat (record: `docs/DECISIONS.md` 2026-11-02, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8, `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §176). The desktop Settings section and the phone's read-only screen are the remaining half of this slice and are named in the PR body rather than claimed here.

A fact it saves is `source="auto"` with `meta.reworded`, listed in "Saved automatically" in both apps with the mark "Jarvis's own words", forgotten with one tap, and capped at five per learning pass. **The three repairs, no policy change:** (a) "remember that …", "remember this: …", "please remember: …" and "remember, …" are now the same one-line automatic shape as the literal "Remember:" - the intake queues them and the automatic check accepts them; (b) length alone no longer makes a typed turn "pasted text" (the research measured 601 characters carding an ordinary typed fact) - any other outside-text sign still does, and where this PC did not see the typing length still counts; (c) a sensitive-topic check that could not RUN ("no local model", "took too long", "did not answer", "could not be read") now says so on the card and is counted in `stats()` (`sensitive_unchecked`, `last_sensitive_error`), so a dead learning lane reads as a fault instead of the owner's facts looking suspicious. **The safe default is unchanged** - everything above is off or exactly as before, and the bulk Discard (C3) is deliberately NOT built: the research's order is repairs, measure, switch, discard. - **The phone's "One moment." clip can no longer be played in the voice the owner replaced (2026-11-02).** The owner's report: *"in jarvis live on my android phone, the 'one moment' will be in the default male voice while the rest of the response from jarvis is in the female voice i choice"*. The cause, from the shipped code: the Live turn path (`VoiceSession.deliverLiveClip` - the only path a Live question takes, called from `LiveService.kt`) never re-read `flow` or the clip; only push-to-talk and the wake word did, in `deliver()` - so Live kept whatever clip a screen's last status read had fetched, however long ago; `toolStarted()` then played those bytes without comparing their key with `flow.moment.key`; and `refreshMoment()` kept the old bytes on any failed, empty or 503 fetch, so even a refresh could leave the old voice playable under the new key. The PC cannot hand out the old voice for a new key: `jarvis_voice_flow.moment()` only returns a clip whose key matches `moment_key()` (a hash of speaking voice, speed, face voice and engine) at the moment it is asked, which is why the answers themselves were female. The fix is phone-only: a `MomentClip` holder that hands out bytes only for the key in use now, clears them before asking for a new key's clip (so a 503 is silence, not yesterday's voice), re-reads `flow` at the start of every spoken turn including Live's, and retries one clip fetch once (700 ms) when a turn begins before the PC has made the clip. No new route, no new permission, no speech-to-text; the phone's "Say 'One moment' if I'm kept waiting" switch and the once-per-question rule are unchanged. Tests: 7 new JVM checks in `MomentClipTest` (old-key bytes never play, a new key means a fetch, a 503 leaves silence, overtaken bytes are dropped, once per question, `ready:false` is still fetched at turn start, and the shipped wiring), and the whole phone suite is green (3,117 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped). Honest limits: no phone audio was heard from here, and the phone keeps no log of when its in-memory clip was fetched, so the exact fetch that supplied the male bytes is inferred from the code, not proved.

The 90-second silent window that used to be `jarvis_live.QUIET_S` is now `[live].quiet_s`, bound 30 seconds to 10 minutes with a 30-second step for the two apps' controls. Say "how long before Jarvis Live turns off when it hears nothing" and Jarvis answers with the value and the range; say "make Jarvis Live wait three minutes" (or "set the jarvis live timeout to five minutes") and it changes, then answers "Okay - Jarvis Live will now wait 3 minutes before turning off when it hears nothing. It can be anything from 30 seconds to 10 minutes". A length outside the range is refused in words that name the range, and nothing is written. It is in Settings on the PC ("Limits and frequency") and the phone (Limits) too, from the same one row, so both apps show the same label and range. No approval card in either direction: Live is already running and its microphone already open, and the sentence only decides when an idle session ends - it can never start Live, read, send or store anything. - **Live hears you through a car's Bluetooth again (2026-11-02).** Jarvis Live now records through a car's (or headset's) hands-free microphone properly. A car's Bluetooth microphone only exists while the phone is in a call, so Live asks Android for the call configuration - the voice-communication recorder source, communication audio mode, and the car as the communication device - and puts the phone's audio mode and device back when it stops. Before this, Live made the car the communication device and recorded on the normal path, so the car showed a call and the microphone recorded silence (the owner's report, 2026-11-02: "it acts like it is in a call but jarvis cannot hear me"). With Bluetooth that has no microphone (media only) the Live screen now says so, and if Android refuses the car Live falls back to the phone's own microphone instead of silence. The route is decided by a pure function with JVM tests for no Bluetooth, A2DP only, hands-free Bluetooth, a wired headset, a device unplugged mid-session and restoration after stop. Only the owner's own car can prove it works there.

A skill that ships a `scripts/` folder says so on its row and on its card, in the owner's words: "Imported SKILL.md instructions (N file(s) in scripts/ are kept inert and never run automatically)." - **An approval card can be answered from its Android notification, with Approve, Deny and Review in Jarvis (2026-11-02).** The owner asked: *"make sure i can approve jarvis cards through an android notification with a deny or approve button or tap too see more button if the summary that's short enough to fit into an android notification isn't long enough."* Notification cards already existed with Deny; this adds Approve under Gemini's binding five-point envelope. Deny still works locked, because refusing is safe. Every approve action is built with `setAuthenticationRequired(true)`, so Android itself will not deliver it until the device is unlocked. Only a small read-only card (the owner's 2026-11-01 exemption) may send its decision straight from the tap: it goes through EventService, which waits for a live link, re-reads the card, and re-checks that it is still small and still private before using the same `JarvisRuntime.decide` the app uses. A card whose notification text is over 240 characters replaces Approve with Review in Jarvis, so a clipped filename or command is never approved sight-unseen; PC-only cards and multi-plan proposals get Review for the same reason. The lock screen gets `VISIBILITY_PRIVATE` with the public version **"Jarvis: 1 approval waiting"** and no card words. A redacted notification - App lock on (the default), hidden memory lists, or a phone with no secure lock - offers **Review in Jarvis and Deny, and no Approve**, because approving words the notification did not show is the blind approval the 240-character rule also forbids; turning App lock off is the owner's existing Security choice, not something this feature changes. A card that leaves `/api/pending` has its notification cancelled by the existing sync, now with its rule in the tested policy. No backend change, no new route, no second permission path, and `notice.approve_ok` is still ignored. Desk check: `jarvis-client` JVM suite **3,223 tests, 0 failed, BUILD SUCCESSFUL**, with 19 of them new in `ApprovalNotificationPolicyTest`; the one source pin this change altered was updated to the new envelope. NOT-TESTABLE without the phone: the shade drawing two buttons, the lock-screen refusal, the real prompt, and a direct approve reaching the PC after a process kill.

Gemini's ruling 1 removes the list and the hardcoded upper bound: the check now reads every `## N.` heading from 129 up, in document order, and fails on a duplicate number, on a number that does not strictly increase, and on more than three numbers missing between two sections — three may be missing because an in-flight sibling PR reserved that number and has not merged yet, and four is no longer one waiting sibling. The file keeps a fixture case for each part (a duplicate fails and names the number, out-of-order fails, three missing passes, four fails, and the order of the sections below 129 is not this rule's business), so the rule is proved to BITE and not only to pass; it is also run against the real document with `## 176.` appended, which the old contiguous rule failed and the new one accepts. Honest limit: the old list also caught a stale-branch merge that silently deleted sections 135 and 136, and with the list gone a middle gap of up to three — and a dropped tail — now passes. That is the trade the ruling makes deliberately, and the file says so where the rule lives instead of leaving it implied. At the desk: `python -B backend/test_pictures.py` 266 passed, 0 failed; `backend/test_base_matches_repo.py` 135 passed, 0 failed; `backend/test_base_regeneration.py` 39 passed, 0 failed; `tools/check_stale_twins.py` exits 0; `tools/check_no_source_pins.py` exits 0 (no new pins — this is a test file, and it has no `jarvis-backend` twin).
- **A small read-only approval is approved by its card alone - no fingerprint, no Windows Hello (2026-11-01).** The owner asked: *"for small approvals like asking jarvis to search the web (for things like weather or the news or anything small) i would like to only have to approve the card, not necessarily use my fingerprint on top of approving the card. make this setting adjustable in settings or through chatting to jarvis."* The reason it asked was the approval-check rule itself, not the owner's setting: `SecurityRules.riskyByToday` (and the PC's `jarvis_owner_check.is_risky`) calls anything `outbound` risky, and a web search is outbound, so pressing Approve on it asked for the phone's fingerprint or the PC's Windows Hello on top of the card's own yes. There is now a third answer to "which approvals ask" - **`small`**, next to `risky` (today's rule) and `every` - and it is the default. A card is small only when BOTH hold: its action is on an explicit read-only list (a web search, a public query, the news, the one page you named, public GitHub data, the model catalogue, and the calendar / mail / notes / home reads - `jarvis_owner_check.SMALL_ACTIONS`, mirrored in `SecurityRules.SMALL_ACTIONS`), and the gate's own risk row for it says it changes nothing (`reversible` "yes"), has classified it, and nothing rushed it. Everything else - unclassified, irreversible, rushed, or anything that writes, spends, sends, deletes or changes an account, a credential, a device, the network, an app or a permission - is not small and still asks. The backend answers it once, in `is_small`, and applies the same answer to both prompts: no Windows Hello for such a card approved on this PC, and a phone's approval of it needs no device signature (a signature can only be made after a fingerprint). The phone's Security screen draws all three choices, the desktop Settings note says what the rule is, and the PC's own answer is changeable by voice or chat through the existing `change_setting` tool and the new `small_approvals` setting ("ask me for my fingerprint on everything again" / "leave the small approvals alone") - the same function the approval itself reads, so the two prompts can never disagree. Nothing is auto-approved: the card is still raised and still needs its own yes, denying still asks nothing, and the rule is held to the PC's own answers by `contract/risky-approval-cases.json` (`tools/gen_risky_approval_cases.py`, now carrying `small` per row), with `SmallApprovalContractTest` on the phone and new checks in `backend/test_owner_check.py` and `backend/test_settings_registry.py`.
- **Jarvis can open one of your own apps on your phone, and start a media search in it (2026-11-01).** The owner asked in these words: "id like jarvis live to be able to open certain apps on my android phone if i ask it (during a live session on my android phone) and to be able to perform certain actions like if i aaid 'hey jarvis open yourube music and play the weekend'". The `control_phone` tool's list of actions stopped at tap, swipe, key, text and screenshot, so the one thing the module underneath had known how to do since 5A could not be asked for at all; it now also offers `open_app` (Android's own launcher: `adb shell monkey -p <package> -c android.intent.category.LAUNCHER 1`), `play` (`am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d <the app's own search address> -p <package>`, so "play The Weeknd" opens YouTube Music on `https://music.youtube.com/search?q=The%20Weeknd`) and the read-only `list_apps`. The owner's permission is a new `[phone_apps]` table in `jarvis-framework.toml`, one line per app - the name you would say out loud, and the package behind it - and it ships EMPTY, so a fresh install can open nothing; anything not on that list is refused in plain words before any card exists, and the refusal names the apps that are allowed. The words of a search are percent-encoded (`;`, `&`, quotes and `$(...)` arrive as `%3B`, `%26`, `%22`, `%24%28...`) and the finished address is checked against a strict pattern, so nothing the owner says can become a second command on the phone's own shell. A list-only call and a refusal raise **no** approval card (there is nothing to approve); a real plan still goes to the same `jarvis_android_control_run` action at the same `ask` tier, with every literal command printed on the card, and the tool is still opt-in - `control_phone` is not in the shipped `[tools].enabled`. Two gaps found on the way and fixed in the same change: `device` is now optional and resolved from `adb devices` (exactly one connected phone, or a plain refusal - before this the tool was unusable by voice, because "open YouTube Music" carries no serial and the model was never told one), and `am start`/`monkey` report a launch they could not make on stdout while still exiting 0, so `run()` now reads that instead of reporting `done` for an app that never opened. A third was worse and closer to the point: `run()` refused every step that sends input while the Jarvis app is in front - which is exactly where it is during a Live session on the phone - so `open_app` and `play` are now `PACKAGE_PINNED_ACTIONS` and skip that guard, because both name the package in the command itself and a `com.jarvis.` package is refused before a command exists, so neither can tap inside Jarvis (a `tap` is still refused there). Honest limits: `play` opens the app on a search for those words - whether the music starts without one tap is the app's business, and both the tool text and the card say so; only YouTube Music has a known search address today, so any other app can be opened and not searched, and Jarvis says exactly that rather than pretending; opening a media app takes it to the front, so a Live session on that phone is backgrounded by the thing it asked for; and the exact intent behaviour on the owner's own phone is verified separately on the real device, not in this repository.
- **One moment, off by asking (2026-11-01).** "Say \"One moment\" if I'm kept waiting" is now a real switch Jarvis can change by talking: type or say "stop saying one moment" in Jarvis Live (or "turn off the one moment message"; the model's own wording reaches the same setter) and the PC saves that answer, so the desktop bar and the phone both stay quiet - both apps already gate the clip on `flow.moment.enabled`, which now reflects it.
