The PC's `[voice] one_moment_enabled` line stays the hard, hand-edited switch and still wins. It was the last "One moment." row in `NOT_BY_ASKING`, refused in words because each app held its own value; the audit that came with this change is in `backend/README.md` (22 of the 34 Settings rows adjustable by asking, 9 refused by name, 2 reached by another grammar, 1 not a preference).
- **Jarvis Live can now reach the same tools a typed chat turn can (2026-11-01).** A Live turn already went through the same `/api/chat` route, the same agent, the same approval cards and the same tool gate as a typed one, but it was shown a narrower tool list: `[live] tool_limit` cut the offer to 6 tools, and the cut also applied to the top-K diet's full-list fallback. Measured on `1861485da`, for "book a table for two at the italian place" a typed turn was shown all 32 tools and a Live turn 6 - 26 hidden, including `notes_search`, `append_obsidian_daily`, `set_timer`, `set_reminder`, `todo_add`, `send_email`, `change_setting` and `connect_account`; a many-match question showed 12 typed and 6 spoken, a multi-step question 9 and 6. The model was never told a hidden tool's name or its arguments, so a spoken request would not reach it in practice - the gate would still accept a call to any allowed tool, but most of what Jarvis can do was out of Live's reach - the owner's request of 2026-11-01 was that Live "reasonably do anything that jarvis can do through chat". Now a Live turn is shown exactly what a typed turn is shown for the same words: `jarvis_live.LIVE_TOOL_FLOOR` is typed chat's own diet size (8), `[live] tool_limit` can only raise it and never lower it, the full-list fallback is never trimmed, and the carried prefix-cache list uses the same cap. What stays Live-only is the speed half - the `[live]` model, its lane and the 16K window - and the deliberate rules are untouched: cards are the same gate cards, decided by tapping only, Live still pauses while a card waits, and the phone still does no speech-to-text. The switched-off persistent-stream path also marks its loopback message `provenance: "voice"` beside `live: true`, the shape both apps already send; without it the server did not treat that turn as Live at all. Proved by the new `backend/test_live_parity.py` (40 checks: tool-list equality for six kinds of question, the floor, the carried list, a whole Live turn raising the same card and running nothing first, the prompt's only difference, the server's marks, the fast path's identical PC-state answer, and the deliberate rules), plus updated assertions in `backend/test_live.py` and `backend/test_agent.py` that had pinned the old cap. Honest limit: no real model, phone or Live session was driven; the proof is headless with a fake model and a stub tool.
- **Jarvis Live: verify your voice once per session, and say the answer instead of pointing at the screen (2026-11-01, the owner's two reports).** (1) "Once I actively verify my voice in a single Jarvis Live session, Jarvis shouldn't need to re-verify my voice." It did: after ONE successful full-sentence check, `jarvis_live` still counted a **120-second window or 16 short clips**, and when that ran out the next short clip was answered with "Say a full sentence so I can re-check your voice." - the owner verifying again, in the same session, two minutes after he had already done it. The window is gone: one successful check verifies the whole session, so nothing asks again for as long as it lasts. `[live] trust_window_s` and `[live] trust_max_short_clips` are no longer read (an installed file still carrying them changes nothing), and the status payload keeps both keys with `window_s` = the session length and `max_short_clips` = 0. The strict check itself still runs **silently** on a >= 2.0 s clip, and that is on purpose: it is what refuses a voice that is not the owner's, and its verdict is what a private answer needs before it may be read aloud - the owner hears nothing about it. A failed or erroring check, a re-enrolled voice print, a new session or the other device all still leave the session unverified. (2) "It will say 'it's on your screen' when it'd clearly capable of reading the info out loud." The cause was not only wording: a 1.5-2.0 s clip running on the session's verification carried an empty `strictness`, so `_really_checked` was false and the reply said `memory_aloud: false` even though the session's own check had just proved the voice - so an answer that used what Jarvis remembers (read aloud by default, the owner's choice of 2026-09-24) was kept on screen and the app said "It's on your screen." The strictness the session's real check earned now travels with those clips, so the flags answer exactly as they did for the clip that passed; every setting that withholds an answer still withholds it (a sensitive saved fact, a private answer, the screen rule), and the apps' own read-aloud rules were not touched. The one Live instruction to the model (`jarvis_live.MODEL_NOTE`) also now says it: when it already has the answer in hand - a tool result, a page it read, a quick fact - it says it, and a screen line is for what it truly cannot say, such as a table of numbers, a picture or a long list. Tests: `backend/test_live.py` gained `t_one_verification_covers_the_whole_session` (one check, then a second turn with no speaker model and no ask; twenty short clips and fifteen minutes later still trusted; a new session asks again; a failed check, a voice-check error and a re-enrolled print each void it) and `t_session_verification_keeps_the_read_aloud_flags` (a memory answer is read aloud on the very next turn; a private answer and a sensitive fact still follow their own settings; a screen answer still stays on screen), and both were shown to fail without the change. The shared contract table was regenerated with `tools/gen_live_cases.py` (both app copies; `trust_window_s` 120 -> 7200, the two new honest keys) and the whole live fleet is green (1676 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed). No new route, no new setting, no new disk file: the verification lives in memory for the life of the session.
- **Jarvis Live speaks an answer from its own feature list, and the phone's Live screen no longer promises every sentence is checked (2026-11-01).** Two gaps found by the review lane, both checked against the source before anything changed. (1) **`feature_guide` was missing from the read-aloud list.** That read-only tool answers "what is the prompt coach?", "where do I switch it on?" and "is it on now?" from Jarvis's own shipped feature list (`jarvis_agent.FEATURE_GUIDE_TOOL`; no card, and it is in `jarvis_agent._NOT_READING` because it reads no outside text). It was absent from `READ_ALOUD_TOOLS` in `jarvis-desktop/src/private-speech.js`, the phone's `PrivateAloud.kt` and `tools/gen_private_aloud_cases.py`, so a spoken question the model answered with the guide had its answer treated as private and kept on screen with "It's on your screen." - against the owner's 2026-11-01 decision that Live speaks an answer it can say. The name is now on the list in all three places, the backend's served copy and the base twin follow the desktop file byte for byte, and the shared `private-aloud-cases.json` was regenerated rather than hand-edited (103 cases; both copies match). `backend/test_private_aloud.py` now pins the name and its read-only shape (118 checks, 0 failed), and the desktop `tests/private-speech.mjs` is green (28 checks, 0 failed, exit 0). The gap was real, not assumed: the same node check run against `origin/main`'s module reported that a `feature_guide` answer stays on screen, and reports it read aloud after the change, while `email_check` and `memory_search` stay private. `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 16's prose list was corrected too (it also still omitted `read_camera` and `read_web_page`). (2) **The phone's Live start screen said every sentence is checked.** `LiveScreen.kt` read "Every sentence is checked for your voice on your PC before any words are made of it." #1069 made that false: `jarvis_live.trust_decision()` checks a clip of 2.0 s or more (`TRUST_SPOT_S`), but once a session is verified a 1.5-2.0 s clip runs on the session's trust with no speaker model (`TRUST_STEADY_S`, the `"trusted"` action). The sentence is now "Every full sentence is checked for your voice on your PC; once this session is verified, a short reply is trusted without a check." - same one small plate and layout, no test or screenshot pin held the old words, and the phone's JVM tests are green (3,096 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped, exit 0).
- **The agent and runtime-identity test suites no longer read the owner's live settings (2026-11-01).** `backend/test_agent.py` and `backend/test_runtime_identity.py` pin the exact bytes of a prompt, and two of the lines in that prompt come from this PC's saved state: a chosen Cloud preset adds "The Cloud preset is set to DeepSeek (api.deepseek.com, model deepseek-flash); ..." to every local request (through `jarvis_presets`, reading `cloud-choice.json`), and the data-sandbox switch in `sandbox.json` makes `run_data_script` be offered even when a test passes `enabled_tools={"calculator"}`. So the same suite was green in CI, which has no owner config, and failed at the owner's desk: measured on 2026-11-01 at `c1b5c5236`, `python -B backend/test_agent.py` was 304 passed and 11 failed with the live folder and 311 passed and 4 failed with an empty one, and `python -B backend/test_runtime_identity.py` was 12 passed and 1 failed live against 13 passed and 0 failed empty. Each suite now makes its own empty temporary config folder and points `OPENJARVIS_CONFIG_DIR` at it before any product module is imported, restoring the old value on exit - the pattern `test_schedule.py` and `test_manner.py` already use - so a run is the same whether or not a Cloud preset is chosen, a key is saved, or the sandbox is on; pointed at a folder holding exactly the owner's `cloud-choice.json` and `sandbox.json`, both suites now report exactly what they report on the live folder (311/4 and 13/0). No assertion was weakened and nothing was skipped, and the 4 remaining `test_agent` failures are not config state at all: the owner's installed `jarvis_gate.py` has no `_TOOL_ACTIONS` entry for `send_file_to_phone`, `protect_from_jarvis`, `connect_account` or `rea_investigate`, no patch in this repository adds one, and CI never sees it because `jarvis_gate` is not importable in a clone (there the run is 279 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0). Those four are left exactly as they were, so the gap is still visible rather than hidden by this change.
- **Four tools the model can pick - send a file to the phone, protect something from Jarvis, connect an account, investigate a program with REA - reached the approval gate with no action of their own, so the card they raised was never their card (2026-11-01).** `jarvis_agent.py` offers `send_file_to_phone`, `protect_from_jarvis`, `connect_account` and `rea_investigate`, and none of them had a line in `jarvis_gate._TOOL_ACTIONS`; no patch in `backend/` named any of the four either, so no run of `apply-patches.ps1` could ever have added them. `action_for_tool()` therefore answered `unclassified_tool` for every one - fail-safe, because that name takes `unknown_action_tier` ("ask", so nothing ran unattended), and wrong in two ways you could see: the card showed a generic worst case instead of the tool's own words, and "What can Jarvis reach" listed all four as unclassified, which reads as "cannot be undone and can leave this PC". Each is now mapped onto an action that already existed and already owned its tier and card wording - `send_file_to_phone` itself, `protect_item`, `change_own_config`, `run_shell_on_host` - so no new action, tier or card wording was invented, and nothing about how often you are asked changes. The CI blind spot is closed too: the check written for exactly this needs `import jarvis_gate`, which no plain clone can do, so it printed `skip` in CI and could only ever fail at the desk. A new suite rebuilds the table an install really gets from the published base plus every patch's added lines, and fails if any tool the model can be offered resolves to no real gate action. Against a copy of the installed backend, `backend/test_agent.py` went from 311 passed / 4 failed to 315 passed / 0 failed.
- **The three gaps the 2026-11-01 field test found are fixed (2026-11-01).** Typing "was this answer right?" into the desktop HUD or the phone now opens that answer's own menu (Right / Wrong, read aloud, copy, pin) instead of sending the words to the model - the app answers it locally, so no chat turn, no history entry and no request leaves the machine; with no finished answer on screen it says so in its own words and still sends nothing. The phone's answer menu also gains the desktop HUD's own read-only line with the answer's date and time ("Sat 31 Oct, 21:10"), hidden when the moment is not known. And "where am I talking from?" is now answered deterministically from the header both apps already send: "You are talking to me from the desktop program on your PC." / "You are talking to me from the Jarvis app on your Android phone." - never a guess at a physical location, and one honest sentence when a request carries no label at all. Honest limits: the desktop's main chat window keeps its always-visible Right/Wrong row (a different design, no caret menu), so nothing there needed routing; the phone's open chat still shows no per-answer clock outside the menu, and its History list keeps its own relative ages (unchanged); the new "where am I talking from" lane answers whole-sentence surface questions only - a near miss ("where am I", "which app can open my notes") keeps its old path, which for a location question is still the model; and every row was proved locally and in CI, then driven on the live PC and phone in the field test whose verdict is recorded with the deploy.
- **"You have full approval to search the web for this conversation": one card, once, and search only.** Say that sentence in a chat and Jarvis raises ONE approval card; approve it and web searches in that chat stop asking for the rest of the conversation - everything else still asks every time. The grant covers `search_the_web` and nothing else: booking a flight, sending an email or a file, spending money, deleting, running a command, changing a setting and working a browser each raise their own card with the grant live, because the only code that reads a grant is the web-search path. It is ended instantly by saying stop ("stop searching without asking", "you don't have approval", "revoke that") with no card at all, by the chat ending, by an 8-hour cap, or by a restart - it is never a setting, and nothing about it is written to disk. Lockdown outranks it. Every search it covers is written in the approval log with the grant's id (`gate.grant_made`, `gate.granted`, `gate.grant_ended`), and the conversation id never is. The model can ask for the grant but can never decide it: a denied, timed-out or unanswered card grants nothing, and the tool is one a person must answer even if the tier is loosened. Both tools are switched on in Settings, Tools, "Safety and sharing" (`approve_web_search_for_conversation`, `stop_web_search_approval`); neither is a fresh-install default. Delivered as `backend/web-search-grant.patch` (three additive hunks in `jarvis_gate.py`: the two `_RISK` rows, the word `grant` in `_SAFE_KEYS`, and the three audit writers) plus the shipped `jarvis_agent.py`, with the two tier lines in both settings copies and `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 175.
- **The desktop HUD's calendar no longer reads an event an hour out on a daylight-saving day, and the README's stale deployment lines are true again (2026-11-01).** The HUD calendar built each event's moment as local midnight plus the clock time in absolute milliseconds; a daylight-saving day is 23 or 25 local hours long, so on a change day every event moved an hour - on 2026-11-01 an event at 12:14 was computed as 11:14 and read "past" five minutes after it started (the same arithmetic read it an hour late on the spring-forward day). It is now built from the date's own local components, so the clock time the owner reads is the time the event happens on every day; the past/now/upcoming rules are unchanged, the all-day and midnight-crossing cases are covered, and five new fixed-date cases in `jarvis-desktop/tests/hud-calendar.mjs` catch the whole family all year instead of only on the day the suite happens to run on a Pacific PC (CI runs in UTC, which has no daylight saving, so the old arithmetic could never fail there). The phone's calendar never had this bug: it keeps dates and times as local date strings and has no past/now/upcoming arithmetic at all. Also in this change: the README's "in the next update" section now says what is actually on the PC (the notes/HUD wave was merged and installed on 2026-11-01), the Obsidian plugin line says 0.1.3 installed and connected in both the test vault and the live vault (token in Obsidian's SecretStorage), and the page names no pull-request number. Honest limits: the calendar fix is proved by the page's own helpers under Node (plus the full HUD harness), not yet by watching the installed window cross a daylight-saving day; the plugin is still not driven on real notes.
- **An approved card is no longer forgotten when the app's stream dies while it waits (2026-11-01).** The owner's report - approve the card, hear "Approved. Carrying on.", and get an answer that clearly never used the thing that was approved - was measured on his own run at 15:44-15:47 that day. That sentence is the app's own fixed line for a real yes (`jarvis_card_words.VOICE`, `CARD_VOICE` in the HUD page), never the model's, so it proves only that the gate recorded the tap. What happened next is the bug: `jarvis_gate.decide()` consumed the tap and NULLed the card's prompt and detail, the turn then found `out.gone` (the phone had closed its stream while the card waited) and unwound through `ClientGone` without running the approved tool, and the app re-sent the same conversation 91 ms later with nothing on the PC remembering the yes - so the new turn made one model round, ran no tool and answered in 17 tokens. `jarvis_agent.py` now keeps that one approved step for that one conversation, in memory only, and runs it once at the start of the next turn for the same conversation through the same `prepare()`/`gate`/`execute()` contract, putting its result in the transcript the model answers from. **The yes is re-made at replay time, never treated as a standing permission:** `owed_may_run()` checks the gate's CURRENT decision before anything is appended - a Stop everything pressed after the approval (the stop-all generation recorded at the tap), a crisis turn in that same conversation after it, the tool no longer in the turn's allowed or offered set, or its action now at tier "never" all DROP the step (`agent.owed_dropped`, with the reason recorded) and the answer says so in code's own words; none of them raises a second card, and nothing the gate would now refuse is run. A picture-lane turn and a turn whose model cannot use tools run no tool, so they leave the step owed rather than spending it, and a replay that raises after its tool-call message was appended puts a result beside it, never a tool call with no answer. It is keyed by the card's own id, so a client that re-sends twice runs it once; it is dropped after ten minutes, never crosses into another conversation, never survives a restart, and is never written for a denied, timed-out, expired or never-answered card (`owed_record()` asks `_a_person_said_yes()` for itself rather than trusting a caller). The gate contract is unchanged - one card per action, nothing runs before its yes - and the carried step raises no second card because it already has one; a carried step that fails says so in code's own words and never claims it ran. Both the record and the replay are in the audit log as `agent.owed` / `agent.owed_ran` (names and ids only, never the card's words or the question). `jarvis_agent.py` is a module this repository ships whole (it is in `$SHIPPED` and no patch targets it), so the change is delivered as the whole file in `backend/` and `jarvis-backend/`, not as a new patch. Proved headless by `backend/test_approval_continuity.py` - 109 checks, 0 failed - which now also drives the reported seam END TO END (turn 1: the model asks for a `web_search`, its card is approved while the app's stream is dead, the search does not run; turn 2: the app re-sends the same conversation, the search really runs exactly once and its result is in the FIRST round of the answering turn; turn 3: a second re-sent turn runs nothing) and the replay-time policy drops, including a Stop everything pressed WHILE the card waited (the dead stream must not become a way round the product's own "a stop wins over the approval" rule, so the record carries the turn's own earlier stop mark) and a crisis turn ordered by a counter rather than a millisecond clock (time.monotonic() on Windows put the approval and the following crisis turn in the same tick). With only the new `owed_may_run()` disabled in the same tree the suite is red - 92 passed, 0 skipped, 17 failed (16 of them the new policy checks; the seventeenth is the base-copy check, red until the twin is taken) - and the suites that already guard this path are all 0 failed: `test_agent.py` 279 passed and 1 skipped, `test_chat_stream.py` 68 passed and 1 skipped under a clean config (the two failures on this PC without one are the owner's own sandbox switch and reproduce on unmodified `HEAD`), `test_approval_contract.py` 67 passed, `test_web_search.py` 415 passed, `test_asks_first.py` 226 passed.

Phone: Mind -> the notes plate"*, `protected-items` step 2 said *"PC: Settings -> Protected from Jarvis"*, and `file-from-pc` step 2 said *"Phone: Settings -> File from your PC"* — none of `PC: Brain`, `PC: Settings` or `Phone: Settings` is a name either app draws, so the checker (correctly) refused them. Each line now uses the names the apps really have: **"The PC's Brain → Memory → Notes; the phone's Brain → What Jarvis knows about you → Notes"**, **"The PC's Settings → Protected from Jarvis"** and **"The phone's Settings → File from your PC"**; the notes lesson's body also names the phone's Brain screen instead of the internal "Mind" nickname. The three lessons' `version` goes **1 → 2** so the corrected steps are re-offered, which is the tutorials' own rule for changed steps; `backend/jarvis_tutorials.py` and `jarvis-backend/jarvis_tutorials.py` carry the same bytes. `tools/check_tutorial_places.py` now reads 261 `where` lines, 143 breadcrumbs and 323 names, all real; no code, route, setting or live change, and no new document.
- **In-app tool switches, tiered (2026-10-31).** The owner can now offer the safe Tier A and Tier B tools to the AI model from Settings, What asks first - 21 one-tool switches grouped as `Notes and reading`, `Timers, lists and plans`, `Connected accounts & home` and `Safety and sharing`, plus the vault organizer's own switch row - each ON with ONE PC-only card plus Windows Hello, OFF instantly from either app, and read-only on the phone. - **The Settings page draws the tiered tool switches (2026-10-31).** "Let the AI use this" now lists all 21 Tier A and Tier B tools in four groups - Notes and reading, Timers lists and plans, Connected accounts & home, Safety and sharing - one switch per row, plus the vault organizer's own switch row (its own PC-only card + Windows Hello) and a plain note naming every raw/unlisted tool that stays a settings-file choice. - **Jarvis knows whether it is talking to the phone or the desktop program, and
  tailors its answers by default:** both clients now send one plain
  `X-Jarvis-Surface` header (`phone` from the Android app, `desktop` from the
  desktop program) beside the unchanged `X-Jarvis-Client: hud`. The PC reads it

  brain" from the phone names the phone's Brain, a PC-only feature asked from
  the phone says where the PC door is, and a phone-only feature asked from the
  desktop says it is on the phone only. No setting, no opt-in and no first-run
  step; a request with no header is `unknown` and behaves exactly as before. The

  `backend/test_surface.py`, `SurfaceHeaderTest.kt` and the Rust

- **Keyboard shortcuts are real, and Jarvis now says so (2026-10-31).** Asked "what keyboard shortcuts do you have?", Jarvis answered "I don't have any keyboard shortcuts myself… that's up to your OS settings" - false, because the desktop ships 11 bindable global hotkeys (Alt+Space for the Jarvis bar, Alt+Shift+N for a quick note, Alt+Shift+X to stop everything and more, all changeable in Settings, Shortcuts) and the notes editor has its own formatting keys (Ctrl+B and the rest). The chat now answers every shortcut question from that measured list, says where each key works, tells the phone the keys are on the PC, refuses a shortcut that does not exist and names the nearest real one, and leaves Windows' and other programs' shortcuts to the model. The system prompt carries one honest line so general chat stops denying them, and the Keyboard shortcuts and quick-note catalogue rows now carry the true list and limits.
- **Send one file from the PC to the phone:** ask Jarvis in chat to find a file
  in the folders it may look in and send it to the Jarvis phone app. ONE
  approval card shows the exact filename, folder and byte size; after the yes
  the phone fetches it by an opaque id - never a path - within ten minutes and
  once only, at most 10 MiB (bigger files are refused in words). The phone's own
  half is built: Settings -> "File from your PC" lists the approved files in the
  PC's words and can **View** one (handed to Android's viewer through the app's

  MediaStore); a small "File from your PC" block appears inside Coming up on
  Brain so a waiting file is noticed, and while "Hide memory lists and chat
  history" is on no filename is fetched or drawn. The phone never approves a
  file and no route here ever carries a path (Gemini Q7; docs/JARVIS-API.md
  section 172).
- **The chat can send one file to the phone (2026-10-31).** "send me the file X", "send X to my phone", "send the file X to my phone", "find the file X and send it to my phone" and "send me X from my Downloads/Documents/Desktop" are answered by a deterministic fast path that calls `jarvis_send_file.prepare()` itself - the same allow-list search, the same one-card rule and the same plain refusals - and raises the module's own card under its own `send_file_to_phone` action. No new route, tool or permission, the fast path approves nothing, and the answer is the card's own sentence plus "Nothing is sent until you approve the card." A no match, several matches, a protected/outside file or a file over 10 MiB returns the module's own sentence with no card; "send an email", "send me a message" and "send my regards" stay the model's.
- **Jarvis now knows which app it is on, and its own live runtime (2026-10-31).** The model's system prompt gains exactly two dynamic lines (no static prose): `Runtime: Jarvis on <surface> (local model: ..., preset: ..., cloud escalation: <provider or off>, vault: <configured or off>, phone: <connected or off>).` and the Rule "Never invent features, shortcuts, or settings; if unsure, point to 'Everything Jarvis can do' in the Brain." The two lines are added only when the request knows its surface, so an older client, a script or a pre-#1046 test keeps exactly its old prompt bytes. No secret, path or static feature list is added.

- **The vault organizer now has a real chat door, and a stale card can no longer block a new one (2026-10-31).** The organizer field test found two gaps. First, a turn-on card that timed out or whose window was dismissed could leave the in-memory marker saying a card was waiting while `/api/pending` showed none, so a later "turn on the vault organizer" answered "one card is already waiting" and never raised another; the switch's status and turn-on now reconcile that marker against the gate's own waiting cards (matched by the action and the card's setting), and the gate's own expiry bounds it, so a fresh turn-on raises a fresh card. Second, chat could only say the organizer was off/on: with it ON, "organize my notes" / "plan my vault" / "tidy my vault" runs the READ-ONLY plan and shows the module's own scheme words and counts, says nothing has changed yet, and names the one-card, never-deletes apply; "apply the plan" / "organize my vault now" / "tidy it for real" raises the writer's ONE approval card through its own `POST /api/vault/organize` path, returns the module's words unchanged, and a denial writes nothing. A pick-a-set ask ("organize just my Welcome note", "organize these notes: Welcome, Alpha", "reorganize a specific set of notes: ...") now gets a READ-ONLY scoped plan for exactly those notes - tags only, no moves, no Map-of-Content or Vault Home, no other note read for content, and while the hidden lists are on the words are counts only; "apply the plan" raises the writer's ONE card for the whole selected batch, never deletes, and one Undo restores exactly that batch. Empty, unknown, outside or hidden selections are refused in the module's own words and change nothing, and the default stays the whole vault. The tests are hermetic (temp vault, fake gate) and cover raise-stale-status-fresh-card, the read-only plan, the selection/refusal matrix, deny/apply, scoped Undo, the hidden-lists counts-only words, and the whole-vault regression. No new tool, no model call; not deployed.
- **Jarvis becomes a first-class guest inside Obsidian: a new first-party plugin in `obsidian-plugin/` (ribbon, commands, right-side panel, selection actions) that asks the local Jarvis and drives note edits only through Jarvis's own one-card routes (2026-10-31).** `jarvis-notes-bridge` 0.1.1 (desktop only, min Obsidian 1.13.0) talks to `http://127.0.0.1:4719` with `X-Jarvis-Client: hud` and `X-Jarvis-Surface: desktop` through Obsidian's `requestUrl`, and never writes the vault itself: there is no `Vault.modify`, no `editor.replaceSelection`, no `/api/approve`, no `/api/deny`, no `obsidian://` write action in the bundle, and the token is read at request time from Obsidian SecretStorage (with a plainly warned plain-text fallback) and is never logged or put in a URL. Wave 1 (read-only plus capture) works on the shipped backend: ask about the note or the selection (`POST /api/chat`), capture to today's daily note (`POST /api/notes/capture`), and a right-side panel showing the note's headings, links, backlinks, unresolved links and frontmatter keys from Obsidian's own cache, bounded. Wave 2 (structured edits) drives the routes built on PR #1049 with the same one-card flow - insert one line under a chosen heading, bold/italic the selection, replace the selection, turn its line into a checklist item, tag the note, and create one note from a vault/Jarvis template - each showing the PC's own card sentence and polling `GET /api/notes/change` until the card is answered outside the plugin; until the notes-editor backend deploy reaches the live PC those buttons answer honestly that this backend does not have the route yet. Ships with node tests for URL/header building, answer parsing, error mapping and template labels, a `BUILD-VERIFICATION.txt` (typecheck, esbuild bundle, `node --check`, JSON checks, safety greps, a test-vault copy dry run and the zip's SHA-256), and README/INSTALL/SECURITY documents; the shipped tree is unchanged apart from this new folder and this one bullet. Honest limits: the plugin has NEVER been loaded by Obsidian - Obsidian is installed on this PC, but this work never opened it, never installed the plugin and never touched a vault - and no live card flow has been driven; every one of those checks is UNTESTED, not passed.
- **Obsidian plugin packaging follows the binary rule: source, `manifest.json` and a committed `main.js`, with a build-drift check and no packaged zips in the tree (2026-10-31).** The committed `main.js` stays exactly where it is, on purpose, so the owner can copy `obsidian-plugin/` into a test vault without installing Node or running a build. `npm run check:build-drift` (a new script running `node tests/check-build-drift.mjs`) rebuilds the bundle with `node esbuild.config.mjs` and fails if `obsidian-plugin/main.js` changes at all - the zero-drift proof that the committed file is exactly the build of `src/` - and the exact step a CI lane could add to the informational `audit` job (`cd obsidian-plugin`, `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund`, `npm run check:build-drift`; Node 20 is enough and it takes seconds) is written in the README, although this change edits no workflow file. No packaged binaries are tracked: `*.zip` and `dist/` are in `obsidian-plugin/.gitignore`, packages are built into a scratch/release folder and never committed, and their sizes and SHA-256 values are recorded in `BUILD-VERIFICATION.txt` (0.1.3's exact size and SHA-256 are recorded there after the package is built; 0.1.2: 86,666 bytes, SHA-256 `7FA8BE04ADF83ED3BA50826C32D95F249B7164743D349D85F08479A5CB1EE5E6`; 0.1.1 kept for history: 80,765 bytes, SHA-256 `52504033CD3D6529129C868623109D013D17FABE40F2CB104F0AD03685146AB1`). The node tests now include a fake-Jarvis integration suite that stands up a real local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` and drives the plugin's own request builders and answer interpreters through the wave-2 routes - read then insert (waiting to saved), format saved, replace conflict, customize unchanged, tag saved, create waiting to saved, capture waiting to filed, chat answer, templates, wrong token 401, pre-deploy templates 404, query and path encoding, invalid-JSON handling - plus the first-run checklist (no token gives the Settings sentence, the default backend is loopback, and requests carry the `hud`/`desktop` headers). The first-run checklist is now a tested state list: `firstRunChecklist` in `src/protocol.ts` feeds the panel's numbered **First run** block, which stays until the connection is `connected` and otherwise names the ONE next action, with tests for no token, checking, unreachable, token refused, routes not deployed and an unexpected HTTP answer. The suite also covers the remaining honesty shapes rather than only the happy paths: a card that arrives with no change id (the plugin says it cannot follow it instead of pretending it can), unknown write/capture state words (never reported as saved or filed), denied/failed/conflict status polls, a vanished job id, 400/403/409/413/429/500/503 errors, malformed read/chat/template answers, and a server closed while a card was waiting. Two honesty bugs were found by the new tests and fixed rather than blessed: a capture-status 404 for an unknown job id used to claim "not_filed" although the PC merely has no record of that job (it is now an error with the route's own sentence), and a 403 used to be blamed on the token although on this backend 403 is the protected-note refusal (only 401 is the token refusal now). A new `tests/accessibility.test.mjs` (20 tests) and `src/a11y.ts` pin what the panel asks a screen reader for: an accessible name on every control the plugin creates itself, live regions plus `aria-busy` on the ask answer, write result, Test connection result and dialog answers, a named group for the selection buttons, the reason a disabled button is disabled, and a live-region status bar; the replace dialog's selected words are read-only rather than disabled so a keyboard user can still focus and read them. An independent read-only accessibility audit then drove a second pass in the same change: errors are announced as `role="alert"`, every action gives focus back after it disables its own button, the panel refuses to rebuild while a field in it has focus, the selection buttons are no longer disabled from a stale one-time selection read (the handlers refuse and say why in the live result line), unavailable insert/create actions explain themselves, the template preview is a live region a keyboard can scroll, a cut list says how many items are hidden, a clipped replace preview says so, and a command-palette failure is explained in the panel's live line instead of only in a toast. Honest limits: the plugin has still never been loaded by Obsidian, so no keyboard and no screen reader has been used against it, and these tests check the attributes and source pins, not what Obsidian's webview renders; the wave-2 routes await the #1049 deploy to the live backend; and the integration suite drives a stand-in server, not the real backend.
- **The Obsidian plugin can now hand back a read-only `obsidian://open` link to the note you are reading (2026-10-31).** A tenth command, **Copy an Obsidian link to this note (read-only)**, puts an `obsidian://open?vault=<vault name>&file=<vault-relative path>` link on the clipboard (a `#Heading` can follow the file to jump to a section), so a person or a Jarvis answer can send the owner straight back to that exact note. The plugin builds **only the `open` action**: it never builds Obsidian's `new`/`daily`/`unique` actions or the `prepend`/`append` they take, because those write a note immediately and would bypass the one-card model, the File Guardian copy and Undo - and a unit test plus a source-text safety test now pin that (the URI builder is pure and tested for vault/path/heading encoding, and no URI write action may appear in `src/`). Version `0.1.2`; the wave-1/wave-2 behaviour, safety model, routes and UNTESTED list are unchanged. Honest limits: still never loaded by Obsidian (the app is installed on this PC but this work never opened it), the clipboard write and the copied link opening a real note are UNTESTED, and the desktop/chat direction of "Jarvis sends you back to a note" belongs to those lanes - this plugin only creates the link.
- **Flexibility with your Obsidian notes, first slice (2026-10-31).** Chat and the notes editor can now create ONE note, add words to the end of ANY note, and add or remove ONE tag - each with one approval card, a File Guardian copy first, an undo receipt, and the sha256 the change started from so nothing is overwritten. Rename, move, delete and several notes at once stay refused (wave 2).
- **Surgical edits for your Obsidian notes, wave 2 (2026-10-31).** Chat can now add a line under ONE exact heading, add a line before/after ONE literal anchor, bold/italic a span, and replace ONE exact occurrence - each with an exact-match rule (zero or several matches refuse with the count), ONE card showing the before/after, a File Guardian copy, one Undo, and no deletions.
- **Renaming and moving Obsidian notes, keeping their links working (wave 4, 2026-10-31).** Say "rename my Welcome note to Home" or "move my Welcome note into Projects" and Jarvis plans the path change plus every link that named the note - `[[old]]`, aliases, sections, embeds and relative Markdown links - shows the old path, the new path and "2 links in 1 note" (or says there are no links), names up to the first three affected note files when lists are visible, and raises ONE ordinary approval card. Code fences and inline code are never touched; a missing folder is refused unless you explicitly say "create the folder"; two notes with the same title are refused with the count. After approval the File Guardian copies the note and every note whose links change, only those link bytes are rewritten, and the note is moved atomically; ONE Undo puts every byte and path back. Deleting notes, moving outside the vault, renaming folders and renaming onto an existing name stay unbuilt and are said so plainly.
- **Rename and move a note from the desktop Notes plate:** the editor's chrome now has **Rename…** and **Move…** beside Save, calling the same wave-4 routes the chat uses - `POST /api/notes/rename` with exactly `{"path", "title"}` and `POST /api/notes/move` with exactly `{"path", "folder", "create_folder"}` - and following the job with `GET /api/notes/change?id=`. Rename is pre-filled with the current title and disabled when the note has no path. Move offers every folder the editor's own note list proves exists (plus the top level) and a new-folder field whose **"Create it if it does not exist"** checkbox is the only way `create_folder` can become true. The PC's ONE ordinary approval card decides; the plate only asks and follows, shows the module's own waiting/denied/failed/saved words (including "You can undo it."), and opens the note at its new path after a saved change. No second write path, no autosave, no approval from the window, and no rename/move of folders.
- **Read and search your Obsidian notes from chat:** ask "what does my <title> note say?" (or "read my note <title>", "what is in my ... note?") and Jarvis reads that note from the vault and quotes it - bounded to the first 4,000 characters, then says how many more there are - naming the note only when the memory lists are not hidden. "Find my notes about <x>" / "which notes mention <x>" matches titles first and then bounded content, answers with the count and up to five titles (never bodies), and says where the real vault search lives when nothing matches. "Open my <title> note" names the note and opens the existing Brain window where the Notes plate is. "Read my notes" is refused with "I can read one note at a time; tell me which one." All of it is deterministic (no model), read-only (no card, no route, no tool), uses the same vault resolution, protection and hidden-folder rules as the notes editor (`.obsidian` and paths outside the vault are never read, notes over 2 MiB are refused), and while "Hide memory lists and chat history" or App lock is on it shows no note title and no note word. Proved by `backend/test_notes_read_search.py` on a throwaway vault.
- **The owner has one plain-language how-to for Obsidian notes (2026-10-31).** The new [docs/NOTES-HOW-TO.md](../docs/NOTES-HOW-TO.md) is written for a beginner, not a developer: the exact sentences to say in chat and what each says back (read/search/open, create, append, insert under a heading or beside an exact line, bold/italic/strike/code, replace, line shapes and tick/untick, heading rename and new sections, front-matter properties, wikilinks, tags), the desktop editor's toolbar buttons and Ctrl shortcuts, the four built-in templates (workout log, meeting notes, daily journal, project note) plus saving a note as a template and the vault Templates folder, the vault organizer (whole-vault plan and apply, and the pick-a-set scoped plan), a worked example end to end ("make a workout log and log today's session"), a troubleshooting table of the refusals in the app's own words, and "coming next" (rename/move with link preservation). It states honestly that the customization wave is in PR #1049 and not yet driven live; the wording is taken from the module's own card/answer strings and its tests, not invented. `docs/README.md` gains the link and its document count moves 409 -> 410 by hand (the size figure is deliberately not regenerated, per the standing rule).
- **You can now read and edit every note in your Obsidian vault from both apps (2026-10-31).** The Brain gets a Notes plate on the PC and on the phone: search the vault, open a note, edit it, and Save — which raises exactly one approval card on the PC (the app never approves anything itself). Before anything is written the old bytes are copied through the File Guardian, so a bad save is recoverable; a save whose edit started from an older version is refused with `conflict` and the current version instead of overwriting; and the edits stay inside the configured vault (absolute paths, `..`, links, junctions, hidden folders and non-`.md`/`.txt` files are refused before any card; 2 MiB per note). The phone shows the PC's own plain sentence when a note was denied, conflicted or lost, and the whole plate sits behind the phone's existing lists' Show gate with no new bypass. **Honest limits:** no creating, deleting or renaming notes in this slice; search matches note titles and paths, not full text; and it is implemented and proved locally but **not deployed to the live PC yet** — the four `/api/notes/*` routes need their own deploy pass before the live apps show it.
- **The desktop Notes editor has a real formatting toolbar, shortcuts and templates (2026-10-31).** Opening a note now shows, above the box: bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, quote, bullet list, numbered list, checklist, H2/H3 headings, horizontal rule, wikilink and tag buttons, an Insert date/time button, a code-fence wrapper, and a template picker. Every button edits only the words in the box with the exact Markdown it advertises in its tooltip, and the same actions have keyboard shortcuts inside the box only (Ctrl+B/I/K/E, Ctrl+Shift+X/Q/7/8/9, Ctrl+2/3) - no app-wide shortcut changes. The template menu lists the four built-ins (Workout log, Meeting notes, Daily journal, Project note) and any `.md` files in the vault's Templates folder, read through the editor's existing read-only `notes_read` command; choosing one inserts its text at the caret and creates or overwrites nothing. A word/character counter now also shows the selection count. Save remains the ONLY write: the toolbar and templates never call the PC's save route, and every save still raises its one approval card. The built-in template text is local to the desktop until the backend's own templates land; the vault-folder list is always read from the live vault.
- **Customizing your Obsidian notes, wave 3 (2026-10-31).** Chat can now format a span in strike or inline code, turn a line into a bullet, number, checklist item, quote or heading (and back/untick it), rename a heading, add a new section, set or remove one frontmatter property, add one wikilink, and create/save/list plain-Markdown templates (workout log, meeting notes, daily journal, project note) - every edit exactly one match, ONE card showing the before/after, a File Guardian copy, one Undo, and no deletions.
- **The tutorials now teach the new notes abilities (2026-10-31).** The notes editor lesson (version 3) explains the PC's formatting toolbar, its shortcuts and word/character count, and the Insert template menu (built-ins plus any `.md` in the vault's Templates folder). A new "Customize a note" lesson walks through creating a note, adding words at the end, adding under a heading or before/after a line, making a phrase bold or italic, ticking a checklist item, setting one property, adding a link to another note, and using/saving templates. A new "Rename or move a note" lesson teaches the one-card old-path/new-path/counts/first-filenames preview, rename, move into a folder (with the explicit create-folder step) and the one batch Undo. The feature row "Create and customize your notes" now names all three lessons, the catalogue is **61 lessons** (all claimed by a feature row), and every `where` line names a real place in the two apps.
- **A brand-new note is created card-free, and "where is my vault / where did that note go?" now answers from the real path (2026-10-31).** The owner's decision: "jarvis should be able to make a new note into my notes without needing an approval card" - and live, asking "can you write a note?" made Jarvis deny it could write without approval. Creating a brand-new note is additive and can never destroy content, so `POST /api/notes/create` and the chat shapes now write it with **NO card**: the vault-path/collision/protected checks run first, the undo receipt is recorded before the file exists (one Undo removes exactly the new file), the write is `O_EXCL` and read back, and the answer is the module's own "Created ... You can undo it." It is card-free ONLY for a direct owner write (provenance typed/voice and `X-Jarvis-Client: hud`): after outside text, a background job or another client keeps its ONE card, the payload is capped at 64 KB, a same-name collision is a 409 case-insensitively on Windows, and the vault/protected/hidden/symlink/`..` refusals are unchanged; every change to an EXISTING note keeps its ONE approval card, deleting a note is still not built, and hidden lists create the note but echo no title. Chat adds "write a note for me about ...", "write me a note with ...", "can you write a note?" (yes + how, writes nothing), "make a new note called X with ...", "create a note called X and put ... in it", keeping "note this:" on the daily note. The same field test's next wrong answer is fixed deterministically: "what folder is it in?", "where did that note go?", "which folder are my notes in?", "where is my vault?" and "where do you save my notes?" read the configured vault and an in-process last-filed record and say the vault location and the exact file last written; no last note still gets the vault location, hidden lists get the location only, and none of them offers to search the PC or claims no access. Tests: the wave-1 notes suite updated for the card-free create (bytes, no card, undo removes exactly the file, collision writes nothing, capability question creates nothing, hidden mode, existing edits still carded) plus the new chat-shape and location checks; API docs, feature row, tutorials and the generated feature catalogue updated, ONE decision fragment, ONE changelog bullet.
- **Chat can make a note and ask the vault organizer, and it no longer promises Obsidian things Jarvis cannot do (2026-10-31).** The live HUD field test asked "make a note: ...", "organize my notes", "organize my Obsidian vault with tags and Maps of Content", "create a new note called Shopping", "rename my note Welcome to Home" and "customize my Obsidian theme": every answer was a promise and nothing happened (the note tools are off in `[tools].enabled` and the fast path had no note grammar; the vault organizer is built but had no chat door; create/rename/delete and Obsidian theme/CSS/templates were invented). The fast path now has a deterministic note writer for the owner's shapes ("make a note: X", "make a note X", "note that X", "jot down X", "add a note: X", "add to my daily note: X", "add to today's note: X") that calls the EXISTING `jarvis_note_capture` capture path for Obsidian - so the File Guardian copy before the append, the undo receipt and the `append_obsidian_daily` tier are all preserved, its own "Filed in Obsidian, <file>." sentence is the answer, and after outside text it asks under the agent's `write_notes_after_outside_text` action. "organize my notes / my vault / tidy my vault" answers from the organizer's real state: when off it quotes its own "off by default, turning it on is one approval card" sentence and says the plan is a dry run that changes nothing; when on it shows the module's own read-only plan (scheme words and counts) plus the writer's one-card / never-deletes rule; "turn on the vault organizer" raises that existing `change_own_config` card and nothing is switched on until the owner approves. Create/rename/delete a note get the notes editor's own plain refusal, and Obsidian theme/CSS/templates/customisation get the honest "not one of my features" answer. A question that asks chat to read or find a note ("what does my Welcome note say?", "find my notes about vault") no longer gets a model's "I have located your notes" claim: it says chat does not read note text today, points at the Notes plate in the Brain window where any note can be searched, read and saved with one card, and names no note title (hidden lists respected). No new tool, no new route, no model call; not deployed.
- **Jarvis knows the AI model it is running, the presets, the measured local models, and can switch them with the existing card:** asked "what ai model do you have?" it now answers from the PC's own state - e.g. "You are running qwen3.5:9b on this PC, under the \"General\" preset" - instead of denying it while the HUD telemetry says the same thing; "which model answered that?", "what local models are installed?", "what presets do you have?", "what does the coding preset change?", "which model would the general preset load?", "how fast is qwen3.5:9b?", "what are the pros and cons of ...", "when was ... released?" and "which model should I use for <task>?" all have deterministic answers with no model involved. Speeds are the real measured figures with units, context, VRAM and whether they were measured on this PC ("44.9 tokens a second at 196,608 tokens ... measured on this PC"); a model with no benchmark says "No benchmark is recorded on this PC" and where to measure it; release dates say "not recorded" rather than invented, because no official release metadata is in this tree. "switch to the coding preset" and "switch to qwen3.5:4b" raise the SAME existing cards (jarvis_presets.apply_from_body and jarvis_models.switch_to) and answer "the approval card is up ... nothing switches until you answer it" - they never approve, never claim a switch before the card, and a refusal is reported as no change. Advice questions ("which model is best for coding", "use the dark theme") stay advice/chat, not switches. The model's system prompt now carries one honest line naming the running model and preset so general chat stops denying it; the feature-guide catalogue rows are left for their own regeneration slice (the source rows already describe the model and preset doors).
- **The Studio stage panels are opaque now, so nothing shows through the Telemetry panel (2026-10-31).** The owner's screenshot: with the Telemetry stage tab active, the words of the main-screen cards (Today, Coming up, Right now, Settings) read through the panel - "words on top of words". Cause: the dark theme's window surfaces are translucent by design (`theme.css`: `--bg-window: rgba(4,7,12,.86)`, `--surface-1: rgba(10,17,25,.9)`), the HUD aliases them to `--void`/`--plate`, and the split-stage right rail - the one panel that draws Telemetry, Approvals, Reminders and Memory - painted itself from those aliases plus one gradient, so it was ~10-14% transparent over whatever the stage had behind it. Fix: the panel now puts the theme's opaque surface token **`--surface-sunken`** (opaque in all three themes: #04070c dark, rgb(228,233,240) light, rgb(0,0,0) high contrast) under its own gradient, so it keeps the theme's look and is solid; no colour is hard-coded and the Galaxy stage is untouched. Tests: a new browser-free pin (`tests/hud-stage-opaque.mjs`) checks the rule, the opaque token in every theme and the three-copy rule, and the Playwright HUD suite now asserts the Telemetry panel's computed background is an opaque rgb and keeps its gradient. Nothing about the panels' content, the routes or the tab behaviour changed.
- **The HUD's own chat now opens the place it says it is opening:** typing "open settings" in the big HUD window says "Opening Jarvis settings on this PC." and now really opens Settings (on the named section for "open settings, web search"); "open the second brain" / "open brain" / "open memory" / "open the memory map" open the Brain window instead of being answered as a program called "brain", "open history" / "open earlier chats" open it on History, "open tutorials" / "open the FAQ" on Tutorials, and "open my notes" / "open notes" / "open documents" open the Brain and say where the notes are inside it. Real programs ("open Notion", "open Chrome") work from the HUD too, now through the same shared opener the Jarvis bar uses. No new route, field, command or permission: the backend resolves the words to places the apps already open, the HUD walks through the same `open_fix_place` its settings gear already calls, and a section that does not exist is answered honestly ("open settings, sound") without claiming an opening (2026-10-31).
- **The HUD's Memory tab now lists the pending memory cards** (`/api/memory/pending?retire_cards=1&sleep_offer=1`, the same read the phone's Learning plate uses): each row shows its own words and kind (new fact / correction / retire / sleep offer), **Review in the Brain** opens the Brain through the existing `open_fix_place` navigation (Memory is its Memory tab), and **Dismiss** is the banner's own local removal shared through one function - no memory decision, approval or send leaves the HUD, and while App lock / hidden memory lists are on the list draws the owner-independent sentence and no titles. The floating banner keeps its place on every other tab and collapses while the Memory tab is showing; the list refreshes on the banner's beat and when the tab is entered. `hud_proxy.rs`'s read whitelist allows exactly those two query forms and refuses every other one.
- **A History row now opens that chat in the main HUD and you can continue it; each answer's caret menu shows when it was produced (2026-10-31).** Live, the HUD's History sidebar said "This window cannot open a chat on its own - open the Brain's History tab" because the sidebar only used the host it was mounted with; it now re-reads the page's own host before refusing, so a row click reads the EXISTING `/api/history/conversation?id=` route, draws the turns into the main HUD chat, and makes the chat's own id the conversation (`S.conversationId`, the same id the next turn sends as `conversation_id`) - the session really continues that conversation. Non-continuable records (someone else's conversation) stay read-only with a new id and their honest note; archived chats still say Unarchive there, and if an ARCHIVED chat is loaded and then continued the page reopens it first (existing archive route, archived:false) so the new turn is never hidden in the Archive filter; the sad fallback survives only for a window with no page host at all. The row's caret actions remain the real `/api/history/pin|tag|archive|delete` routes. The answer caret menu also gained a first, read-only line with the answer's DATE AND TIME in local time ("Sat 31 Oct, 21:10"): kept-chat turns use the PC's own turn `at` (now carried on the bubble as `data-at`), while a live answer - whose route has no per-turn timestamp - uses the moment that turn arrived, never the moment the menu was opened; it is a `role="presentation"` line, not an action, and arrow keys skip it. Tests: a new browser-free pin (`tests/hud-history-open.mjs`, 7/7) holds the existing route, the host's id/continue wiring, the read-only record, the guarded fallback and the three-copy rules; `tests/hud-answer-menu.mjs` (11/11) now also pins the timestamp line's shape, its real source and its exclusion from the action list.
- **"Edit HUD" is simplified into tabs, and the cards' control rows are no longer all open at once (2026-10-31).** The owner: "the edit hud needs to be way more simplified with the options under menu tabs instead of everything all at once." Each card's own controls stay clickable on the canvas while editing (CI's layout and field tests drive them there); picking a card's body moves that SAME toolbar into the bar's editor, so the full row is not what greets you on entry and every control is reachable either way. - **The desktop HUD's per-answer "Was this answer right?" row is now a caret menu (2026-10-31).** The owner asked for the always-visible Right/Wrong line under every Jarvis answer to be gone, replaced by a small caret menu beside the answer: "was the answer right?", "read out loud", and the other real options. Each finished answer now has one quiet caret ("Answer options"); opening it shows **Right** and **Wrong** (the same feedback path as before - the shell's `mark_answer` command with the same `{turnId, mark}` body, so the recorded learning signal is unchanged; pressing the chosen mark again takes it back, and a PC without the route removes the menu quietly), **Read out loud** (clicks the page's own per-answer speaker, so the voice, its rate, its pitch, the local-voices-only rule and the read-aloud privacy gate are all the existing ones - the item appears only when that real speaker exists), and **Copy answer** (the answer's own words to the clipboard, with "Copied." in place). - **DEF-020: the updater no longer installs the signed release over uncommitted work - on either side of the release (fixed in code, machine-proven).** The route decision asked only about commits: a folder standing on the release's own commit answered "same" even with uncommitted work on top of it, so `update-jarvis.ps1` installed the signed release over that work and silently replaced it. The same shape existed one branch over: a folder BEHIND the release was installed over without looking at its working tree. `Get-LocalVsRelease` now asks `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no` once, before the identity questions, and uses it wherever the signed release could be installed over uncommitted work: standing ON the release's commit with a tracked change (staged or not, or a deletion) answers **"dirty"**, and standing BEHIND the release with uncommitted work answers the new sixth answer **"release-ahead-dirty"** - both build the folder instead, and the caller says why in each shape ("this folder is behind the released code, but it has uncommitted changes - installing the release would replace those changes. Building this folder instead, so they are kept"). A CLEAN folder at the commit still installs the signed release, and a CLEAN folder behind it still installs it too - the ordinary update path is unchanged; a genuinely newer local build is still never downgraded. Untracked files are deliberately ignored on purpose (build output and scratch, and a build does not ship them), and a failing `git status` counts as dirty rather than assuming the tree is clean. Pinned in `scripts/test-update-jarvis.ps1` (21 -> 35 checks): throwaway repos at the release commit and behind it, each with a tracked change, with only a staged change, with an untracked file alone, and clean, must answer the right one of "dirty"/"release-ahead-dirty"/"same"/"release-ahead"; plus source pins that the caller branches on both new answers and says why. Measured with the same harness: against the pre-fix updater 31 passed / 4 failed for the behind half (the dirty-behind cases come back "release-ahead", exit 1); against this branch 35 passed / 0 failed, exit 0, in both pwsh 7.6.9 and Windows PowerShell 5.1.
