App lock is unchanged and its "hide the card's words" rule is now a pure function (`ApprovalWidgetRules.cardTitle`/`cardDetail`) instead of logic inside the composable. `WidgetStatesTest` adds 13 JVM tests: every approvals/board/link combination lands in exactly one terminal state, a genuinely blocked wait still returns inside its budget, the timeout/error sentences, App lock hiding the card even when it has words, a real `/api/pending` row still decoding and reaching the card, and no widget XML naming Glance's spinner. **Not proven here:** the widgets on a phone - no APK built from this branch was installed, so the field-test step is the CI-built APK, add the five widgets, and expect terminal states.
- **a reminder can open a page or a file, or raise one card to run a task (2026-10-27).** A reminder may now carry ONE action: show a note, open a web page or a file on this PC, or put the morning briefing together. A page or a file is only a notice with an Open button - nothing opens until it is pressed, and pressing it is the approval (a 15-minute card would expire before "when I get to it"). The button sends the reminder's id only; the PC reads the target back from its own answer and checks it again at the tap (https only, a folder Jarvis may look in, and an extension allow-list that refuses `.lnk`, `.exe`, scripts and `.html`). A task is acting, so it raises exactly ONE `schedule_action` card at fire time and runs nothing if that card is denied, expires or is refused; its detail carries ids and the task name only, so no address, path or note reaches the audit log or the phone. Confirming the design's second target was wrong: a backup is locked with a fresh recovery code that nothing would be left to show, so `backup` is refused when the reminder is saved, with that reason. Creating one is the desktop HUD's; the phone shows a note and the card, and creates nothing (ARCHITECTURE §8).
- **Two phone fixes: a withheld read-aloud now says so, a read stops when the phone leaves your hands, and Home's three doors outlive the face (2026-10-27).** Three corrections to this morning's typed "Read aloud" and one to Home's doors, all phone-side, no new route and no new control. A missing or unreadable `X-Jarvis-Route` header means the privacy gate and the injected-fact counts are unknown, and unknown is never spoken: the wiring asked a reader that could never answer "unknown", so the fail-closed branch was dead code and such an answer could be read aloud - `routeOrNull` is that reader now. A read stops the moment the app leaves the screen (the phone locking, HOME, another app) and the live lock is asked again before every sentence, because the "locked" fact was a snapshot taken when the answer arrived. A withheld read is no longer silence: the one fixed sentence "It's on your screen." is shown where the Read aloud control would have been, and nothing beyond it - a locked phone or a stale link shows nothing. And "The Galaxy →", "Presets →" and "Model →" used to live inside the face's caption strip, so they vanished with Face size Hidden (the owner's own setting, which meant the Model door he asked for was not on his phone at all) and while the keyboard was up; the row is one composable drawn under the lane pill and above the conversation, the caption gate is gone, and a source pin fails if it returns.
- **The phone reads a typed answer aloud, in Jarvis's voice, beside Copy (2026-10-27).** The desktop HUD already read typed answers aloud (the owner's decision of 2026-10-16), so the phone's silence was a parity gap: a finished typed answer now has one Read aloud control beside Copy and Share, which asks the PC's existing `/api/voice/say` for the answer in Jarvis's chosen voice (one request per sentence, eight at most) and plays it through the phone's one speaker - no new route and nothing sent beyond the answer text the PC already produced. The control only appears when the answer on screen is the one the phone holds and the same never-speak rules as the voice path allow it, all failing closed: an answer that used saved or sensitive facts, a private gate, a screen or camera read, a tool that ran, a stream that could not say, a stale link or a locked phone keeps the words on screen with one fixed sentence; turning the link down and the App lock holding never start a clip. The decision and the sentence cap are proved off-device, the wiring by source pins, and the on-phone look remains a field-test row, not a pass.
- **The phone's model name opens the model list, and the PC's cloud setting is shown read-only (2026-10-27).** Two small phone-side halves of the owner's Presets asks, with no new route and no write: the lane pill under the face ("Local · <model>" / "Cloud · <model>") is now a button that opens the Brain's existing Model plate, and because this PC's status names no lane or model (so the pill is not drawn at all there), Home also gains a one-tap "Model →" door beside "Presets →" that always exists - both call the same action the plain-word model errors already use, navigation only, so switching or installing a model keeps its approval card. And the new additive cloud block on the presets answer is read as one line ("The cloud may answer hard questions through <provider> - set on your PC", or that escalation is off) with no switch, no provider write and nothing shown by an older PC. The "Answered by a cloud model, not on your PC." sentence and the pill's Cloud/Local words are pinned by tests now, and a source pin fails if any phone file ever gains a cloud-escalation write. The per-question "Try the cloud model" offer is unchanged, and the on-phone look is a field-test row, not a pass.
- **A card stays readable even when one of its fields arrives null (2026-10-27).** The phone now settles every declared field of a waiting card's `risk`, `notice`, `raised`, `options` and `replaces` before decoding it, because a single explicit null inside any of them would otherwise throw the whole row out of the queue exactly as `replaces_kind` did. Unreadable values settle toward caution, never convenience: an unreadable `replaces` keeps the two-press ask, an unknown reversibility/reach is read as the worse one, an unreadable weight makes the card heavy (slower Approve), Deny stays allowed, Approve never switches on by itself, and a raise that was sent still refuses every quick gesture. A null-bomb test pins a row where every one of those fields is null and asserts it is read with those values; no server change, no new route, no write.
- **Every approval card waiting on the PC is readable on the phone again (2026-10-27).** The PC sends `replaces_kind: null` on any card that replaces nothing (`jarvis_gate.pending()` sets it from `replaces_words_for(...)`, which returns nothing for an ordinary card), and the phone declared that field non-nullable while its JSON reader does not coerce nulls - so the explicit null made the whole row fail to decode and the phone showed only "N waiting approval could not be read on this phone" with an empty queue, for every ordinary card (picture mode's card was the one seen on 2026-10-27). The three replaces fields are now normalised before decoding, so ordinary cards read exactly as the HUD shows them; no server wire change, no new route, no write. A pin test decodes a real gate-shaped row with those nulls; the phone's own look at a real card remains a field-test row, not a pass.
- **A Live button in the HUD's left column, and read-aloud speakers on answers that are opt-in (the owner's asks, 2026-10-27).** The big "Jarvis" window's rail carries ONE **Live** button in its own `.rail-toolbar` - the rail block no shell hides - and it is the floating bar's control rather than a second idea of Live: the same `live_start` (`by: "button"` plus a fresh chat id) and `live_stop`, the same "Jarvis Live" name and on/off sentences, the same `aria-pressed`, and the same state read (`live_status` on opening, then the shell's `live-status` event through `live-rules.js`'s `onHere`), so a session running on the phone does not paint this window as on. It needed one new grant and no new command or route: a `hud-live` set holding `live_status`/`live_start`/`live_stop` and deliberately not `live_act`/`live_mute`/`live_hold`, with every refusal still Rust's (stale link, App lock, no microphone) and no approval card. Separately, Settings -> "The big HUD window" gained **"Read-aloud buttons on answers"**, OFF by default and stored on this computer like the switch beside it (no backend, no card): with it on, each finished answer gets a small speaker that reads THAT answer through the page's existing `voice.speak`, the same object and OS voice the window already uses - and speaks nothing by itself, while with it off nothing changes at all. An answer that has to stay on screen gets **no speaker**, judged by `private-speech.js`'s `mayReadAloud` on that answer's own route (the same call the automatic read-aloud makes, failing closed if the rule cannot be loaded), with the shell's `speechSynthesis` wrapper still refusing it as a second gate; the owner's own messages and the canned hello never get one. `tests/hud-live-read-aloud.mjs` (13 checks) drives all of it, including the private answer that must stay silent.
- **The HUD's menu is called Presets, and now lists the PC's own presets and personalities (the owner's asks, 2026-10-27: "you didnt put presets, you put hud layouts", "i also want the presets to include all the ideal local ai presets that are made (like coder, or general, etc) along with the different personalities of jarvis that i can select").** Above the saved HUD layouts, the one menu now draws the five local-AI focus presets from `GET /api/presets` and the nine personalities plus "My personalities" from `GET /api/manner`, with only the PC's own `chosen_preset`/`personality` marking what is current. Applying a model preset starts its lane and raises the PC's ONE existing `switch_model` approval card, and nothing is marked chosen until a refetch of the contract names it; switching personality is immediate, asks for no card (wording only, as the backend itself says) and shows Jarvis's own switch line. The settings gear beside the button now wears the page's own rail-button class and a line-drawn 24-unit gear instead of the bar's filled one, so the two controls are the same box and the same icon style ("the spacing of the two new buttons is uneven", "i want the settings to be in a similar style of icon to the others"). The menu's saved-layout actions are unchanged, it is still ONE menu, and the HUD page still holds no token: the shell adds it through `get_focus_presets`/`apply_focus_preset` and the new narrow `hud_personalities`/`hud_switch_personality` commands, while a plain browser uses the routes with `X-Jarvis-Client: hud`.
- **A lane you pick by hand now runs the same privacy gates as an automatic turn (2026-10-27, F-01).** `POST /api/chat` with `"auto": false` and a `"lane"` skipped every routing gate: any client with the pairing token could send `{"lane": "<cloud lane>", "auto": false}` and have the turn answered on a cloud model with private memory text, a tainted conversation, a picture or the owner's screen attached, because the manual path built its own decision and ran no gate at all. Both paths now go through the ONE `jarvis_router.choose()` call, the pick stands in for the owner's own yes for that one question, and a pick the router would not have escalated is answered on the local model with the router's own `gate` and a plain `reason` in `X-Jarvis-Route` ("you chose <lane>, but this turn stays local: ..."). A pick of the local model is unchanged, no wire field was added, no app changed, and a PC with no `jarvis_router.py` fails closed. `backend/f01-manual-lane-gate.patch`, proved by `backend/test_hud_manual_lane_gate.py`.
- **The Studio HUD's lane dropdown is a "Current Models" button now, opening a read-only panel of what Jarvis is using and has loaded (the owner's ask, 2026-10-26: "under the button on the jarvis hud that says auto, theres several options including bulk, critic, escalate, can you just get rid of this button and replace it with a button that says \"Current Models\" and clicking it will show what models are being used and or loaded on jarvis?").** In the Studio (split-stage) header the `<select id="lane-compact">` is gone; a `#current-models` button in the same slot, with the same plate/border/mono tokens and the same Studio-only visibility, opens a panel wearing the Presets menu's own popover classes. It shows the PC's own `GET /api/models` `current` and `previous` (plus `/api/status`'s `default_model` only when it differs), its `offload.models` with `size_mb`/`vram_mb`/`on_gpu_percent` - or the owner's exact sentence "The PC did not say any model is in memory right now." when the PC says nothing - and `GET /api/presets`'s `chosen_preset`/`chosen_model`. Its fourth section routes the NEXT message: the buttons are built from the page's own `#lanes .lane` buttons and click them, so every lane the old dropdown listed (auto, the model, and the cloud lanes) is still there, still one list, and the mark is the page's own. Nothing is switched, installed or approved: `/api/models` joins `hud_proxy.rs`'s fixed read list while `/api/models/switch`, `/install`, `/rollback` and `?recommend=1` stay refused, there is no new command, no card and no new route, and a read that fails says the PC did not answer and changes nothing. A Refresh button re-reads all three.
- **A rushed approval card can no longer be swipe-approved because its reason was cut short (2026-10-27).** `jarvis_gate.check()` stored the rush latch's chip as `json.dumps(raised)[:1000]`, and that chip is a couple of kilobytes once `json.dumps` escapes non-English text: the real bounds are `quote[:80]`, `context[:200]` and `source[:120]` (`jarvis_content_risk.py:319`, `:217-219`), and every non-ASCII character becomes six characters of `\uXXXX`. A chip cut at 1,000 is no longer JSON, so `pending()`'s `json.loads` threw and its `except` served `raised: null` - and BOTH apps read that as "not raised" (the phone's `swipeable = risk.swipeOk && raised == null`, the desktop's `if (approval.raised) return false`), so the one card the latch had raised arrived looking ordinary with its swipe back on. `jarvis-backend/jarvis_gate.py:1803` now stores the chip whole (the column is `TEXT` and `chip_from()` already bounds every value, so there is nothing to trim); the separate 4,000-character `detail` cut is deliberately untouched, because that is a different fault (a cut-off request the phone has no guard against) and changing it here would alter a second behaviour. The published base's three companions are kept in step with it, because the repository's own suites reverse the patch stack out of that file: `backend/gate-touches.patch` (its added side now carries the same line, so it still reverses out and re-applies - `test_gate_touches`, `test_approval_guards`), the deploy block `tools/hud-deltas/gate-digest-insert-new.txt` (must be the base's own text, byte for byte - `test_reconcile_live_backend`), and `backend/patch-history/gate-touches/` with the previous patch text. Measured through the real `check()` with a real `jarvis_content_risk` latch: a 2,068-character chip was stored as 1,000 characters, `JSONDecodeError: Invalid \uXXXX escape`, `raised: None`, `risk.swipe_ok: True`, card swipeable; after the change the same card stores 2,106 characters, parses, and is not swipeable. Proved by `backend/test_gate_rush_chip.py` (19 checks, 12 of which fail on the old line), including a control that an unraised card of the same action keeps its swipe, and a check that `detail` is still cut at 4,000. **Honest limits:** `jarvis-backend/jarvis_gate.py` has no twin in `backend/`, so the two-file rule does not apply to it; `jarvis-backend/` is the published base and a running PC is not updated by committing this, so this fixes the repository's gate copy and does NOT claim the owner's live backend is already fixed - that needs a `tools/reconcile_live_backend.py` delta of this region (the existing digest deltas are already applied there and are skipped) or a base re-take, measured separately. Nothing on the phone was touched, and the phone's rule is applied here as `ApiModels.kt` declares it, not compiled.
- **The Galaxy has five more looks and an easy switch for them, and the HUD's left column now follows the words above it (2026-10-27, the owner's own ask).** `galaxy-presets.js` builds the five rich looks the blueprint listed first - **Planetary orbit** (one sun, homothetic ellipses around it, spaced by arc length so no two names crowd), **Neural arbor** (a crown of rows widening upward with faint dendrites down), **Nebula** (one golden-angle cloud: the only look with no rings, rows or lines), **DNA helix** (double helices side by side, two strands and a rung per row) and **Radar dome** (names on arcs over a ground row) - so nothing anywhere says "not built yet" any more, and keys 1-5 that used to announce a plan now draw a picture. The HUD's own Galaxy (the `#brain` view with the Memory / Neural / Unified lenses) gets ONE plain **Look** list beside those lenses, filled from that module's own list of looks: choosing one lays the same names out in that look, remembers it on this device under `jarvis.galaxy.preset`, brings it back on the next load, and an unknown or corrupt stored value is the constellation rather than a broken canvas. The page imports the module dynamically (the same way it already loads the speech rule), so the vendored page stays byte-identical in all three copies. And the Studio dock's icons were in a different order from the inspector's words - the owner: *"reminder is out of place for example"* - so the dock now reads Galaxy, Approvals, Reminders, Memory, Telemetry like the words do, with every id and data attribute unchanged.
- **Cloud in the Presets menu, and one switch that lets Jarvis escalate without asking first (2026-10-27).** The Cloud row now sits beside General/Coding/Agentic+Vision/Fast and opens the six connected API services; picking one is ONE `change_own_config` card, nothing is marked chosen until the PC's own `cloud-choice.json` says so, and a cloud apply **starts no lane and switches no model**. `GET /api/presets` gains two additive keys and nothing moved (`version` stays 1): `cloud_preset` - a sixth row in a preset's own shape, deliberately not in `presets[]`, so both apps' five-row list is unchanged - and `cloud {provider, providers[], escalate{on, why}}`, where a provider row carries whether a key is **saved** (presence only, never a key or a fragment) and the one honest connect action, the command line to run on the PC. `POST /api/work/apply` gains one optional `provider` field, read only for the cloud preset; `POST /api/work/cloud-escalate {"on": true|false}` is new - ON is ONE card and nothing is written before it, OFF is instant. The **"no standing grant" rule is changed by the owner** and recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md`: the standing yes is read from THIS PC's `escalate-cloud.json` by `jarvis_router.choose()` and from nowhere else, so no client flag can forge it, while the HUD page's `cloud_yes` counts only while that file still says on. Asking in the message ("escalate this", "send this to the cloud") is a yes for that turn only, evaluated after every privacy gate. Every gate still runs first and still only pushes a turn back to local. `X-Jarvis-Route` gains `auto` (`true` when nobody clicked); on such a turn a cloud reply with no usable answer is **not** shown as its working-out - the PC answers it instead under one honest line (`jarvis_chatbot_api.CloudAnswer`, `jarvis_agent.answer_here`), and the 2026-10-14 rule is untouched for a turn the owner clicked for. The three lane names become **one**: `jarvis-critic` and `jarvis-bulk` are gone from `CLOUD_LANES`, `jarvis_auto_router` and `jarvis_projects`, `degrade_chain` is `["jarvis-escalate"]`, and `_lane_names()` no longer reads `litellm-proxy.yaml` - a dead config for a proxy that was never installed - but asks the chosen provider instead, so no provider chosen is gate `unavailable` rather than three names that do not exist. `cloud-escalate.patch` is new in the stack (three hunks, no install block) and `backend/_stack.py`'s ratchet records it honestly (58 → 60). The phone reads all of it and writes none of it; `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §8 says why. Tests: `backend/test_presets_cloud.py` (46), `backend/test_cloud_escalate_setting.py` (72), plus the 15 suites the lane removal touched.
- **CI now parses every Python file, stops counting two non-tests as frontend suites, has one shard-count definition, and cannot report a suite that skipped every check as a pass (2026-10-27).** The 2026-10-27 test audit found 14 backend suites (364 checks) that no CI job ran and that no job even parsed; the required `backend` job now compiles every `.py` file under `backend/`, `jarvis-backend/` and `tools/` in memory (a few seconds, no `__pycache__`) and fails on the first syntax error, before the ~35-minute sweep - not `compileall` or `py_compile`, because both write bytecode even under `-B` (measured: 1,090 `.pyc` files in a copy). `poll-hygiene-measure.mjs` and `make-before-overlay.mjs` say in their own headers that they are not tests (one prints JSON, the other copies `src/` to `src-old/`), so the frontend loop no longer runs them, and the selected count is 225 real suites out of 229 top-level `.mjs` files. The frontend shard count has ONE definition - the `matrix.shard` list - with `SHARDS` and the job name reading `strategy.job-total`, so a `SHARDS`/matrix mismatch can no longer drop a shard's worth of suites silently. `backend/run_suites.py` reports a suite that exits 0 having skipped every check as `NO-CHECKS`, a new state that is neither a pass nor a skip, and fails the sweep unless the suite is on the new `ZERO_CHECK_ALLOWED` list (three suites needing an optional package: playwright, cryptography, Pillow). The same 2026-10-27 probe moved four of the 14 audit suites into the required backend job - `test_bitemporal.py`, `test_extraction_wiring.py`, `test_gate_push.py`, `test_import_history.py`, 61 checks that now run - and kept the other ten skipped by name with the owner files each needs. Proven by `backend/test_suite_report.py` (74 checks), `backend/test_suite_state.py` and the repo's checkers. **The rule's first CI run paid for itself immediately (run 40468616102):** the required `backend` job went red on exactly the two suites that were proving nothing on every push. `test_decks.py` printed one skip and ran NO check because `py-fsrs` was never installed by either backend job - 349 checks sat unrun on every push while the job reported green; `fsrs==6.3.2` (the version `requirements.lock` pins for Python 3.12) is now installed by BOTH the Ubuntu and the Windows backend jobs, so its 351 checks (2 skipped only where `time.tzset` does not exist) really run. `test_tool_calling_wiring.py` lifts `do_POST`'s text out of `jarvis_hud.py` in all six checks, and that file is the owner's patched entry point that no checkout holds, so no CI runner can run it at all: it is now in `run_suites.py`'s `NEEDS_OWNER` list (skipped by name, saying which file it waits for) and out of the Windows job's suite list, where six skips and exit 0 would have read as a pass - the owner's PC remains the only machine it runs on, for real. **Honest limit:** the Windows job still trusts exit codes alone, so a later suite that skips every check there would still read as a pass; widening the rule to that job is named as remaining work, not claimed here. The amended branch's own green CI run is what has not been seen yet - the next run is what shows the fix.
- **A setting can be changed by asking for it on or off, and the answer is a read-back (2026-10-27).** "Make the prompt coach off", "set web search to off", "I want the prompt coach off" and "the prompt coach should be off" matched nothing in the chat grammar, so they reached the model, which has no settings tool - while "turn on/off <name>" already worked. 27 of the 31 on/off switches now take the plainest phrasings too, through the SAME setter their Settings switch, the HUD route and the "turn on/off" phrase already call, so the card, the tier, the PC-only refusal and the wording are unchanged. A sentence naming a switch with no state ("change the prompt coach") gets ONE question back and changes nothing; a switch outside the list keeps the guide's own explanation word for word; a password, key, token, deep config or an irreversible ask is refused in one plain sentence. When the writer applies at once, the value is RE-READ and the reply names the old and the new value; when a card is up it says a card is up and never claims the change; a value that cannot be read is never written at all. `backend/test_ask_to_change.py` proves it, including a real end-to-end run against a throwaway config folder.
- **A blocked click no longer freezes the browser for eight seconds and then reports the wrong reason (2026-10-27).** When Jarvis clicked a link that leaves the allowed sites, the navigation fence answered it with an empty `204` - a navigation Playwright never sees finish - so `locator.click()` sat out its whole 8-second timeout and raised `TimeoutError`; `run()` then reported "step 1 failed: TimeoutError: Locator.click: Timeout 8000ms exceeded" and listed the step it actually attempted among the steps that "did not run". The click now passes `no_wait_after=True`, so a blocked click returns immediately and `run()` gives the fence's own sentence ("the page tried to go to ..., outside the allowed sites - Jarvis blocked it before it loaded"); the fence itself is unchanged and the tab still never leaves the allowed site. Measured headless on Windows 11 with Playwright 1.64.1 / Chromium 156.0.8078.4: `backend/test_browser_control_live.py` 66 passed, 0 failed (was 63 passed, 3 failed). Two test-side corrections came with it: the live suite's record-shape assertion still expected the nine keys of 2026-09-23 and now includes the `box` added on 2026-10-15, and `backend/test_browser_control.py` - which CI does run, unlike the live suite, which self-skips without Playwright - now pins that exact key set so the next `box`-style addition cannot re-break the live suite invisibly.
- **The Jarvis bar reads like the HUD: flat plates, line glyphs, one Incognito chip, and fewer buttons (the owner's decisions, 2026-10-27).** The second row is no longer 999px pills: the mode chips, the lane badge and the preset chip are 3px plates with mono 10px uppercase 0.14em labels, every chip glyph is a fine stroke on the bar's 16-unit grid tuned to render the HUD's 1.05px line weight (1.2 at 14px, 1.05 at 16px), and a pressed mode is the HUD's ice text plus an ice-edged border instead of the old glow or Live's red. "Auto" is renamed "Hey Jarvis" (the wake-word listener, id unchanged), "Private" becomes "Incognito", and the milder "Temp" chip leaves the DOM so Private chat and Temp collapse into that ONE Incognito chip with the strict zero-write behaviour `private_chat` already enforces; the server capability, the `private` flag and the Tauri commands are untouched. The "?" primer door and its panel, the pin button and the Esc key badge also leave the bar (Esc still hides it, the close's tooltip still names it, and the settings gear and close are what remain), and the help words the panel carried still live in Settings' Brain tab, "Tutorials and the FAQ". The window still pins itself while a card is up; it is just no longer something the owner toggles from the bar.
- **A read-aloud now stops when the next question is asked, and turning the phone sideways no longer cuts it off (2026-10-27).** Four wiring fixes behind the phone's read-aloud: a new typed question - from Home's box or the Live screen's - stops a read that was still playing and clears its offer, instead of letting the old answer finish while the control said "Stop" for the answer before this one; a question that starts by voice (the talk button, "hey Jarvis" heard, or Train my voice) stops a read before the microphone opens, because the recorder has no echo canceller and the clip would be recorded into the question; and a rotation no longer stops a read that is still on screen, since a configuration change is not leaving the app - that is the Lead's 2026-10-27 ruling, pinned at the guard's source line because a JVM test cannot simulate a configuration change. The question-start stops are guarded on `readingAloud`, so a typed question sent over a *spoken* answer never cuts the voice's own speech. Still open and named: turning Jarvis Live on does not stop a read, and whether Live's own echo-cancelled listener would remove it is not measured. Four new tests in `ReadAloudWiringTest`; the whole phone suite is 2,706 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped.
- **Jarvis can talk about an update in chat, and start one only through ONE approval card (2026-10-26).** "Is there an update?" and "what changed in the update?" are answered without the model from the same public release manifest the app's updater reads, using the version the desktop shell reports in the chat body; a release's changes come from the changelog, now published into `latest.json`'s notes by the release workflow, and an empty or one-release-only list says so rather than inventing changes. "Update Jarvis" raises ONE card (action `desktop_update`, tier ask, PC-only with Windows Hello) that names both halves, the version, the restart and the pace; only the owner's Approve makes the shell run the same `update_both` the Settings button runs - backend first, then the signed desktop release, then a restart - so no page, timer, page script or chat message can install anything, and the HUD gained no update command. The phone is one-sided on purpose: its reply points at Platform checks, its own update card, and the PC-only card refuses a phone approve with nothing changed. Proven by `backend/test_update_chat.py`, `jarvis-desktop/tests/update-chat.mjs`, `jarvis-desktop/tests/release-notes.mjs` and the existing Rust suite; a real signed install is the owner's field test, not a pass.
- **The owner-secret hand-off can raise its card on the live backend (2026-10-26).** The backend's HTTP request threads never initialised Windows COM, so `POST /api/secret-handoff/create` refused every card with "the host could not verify a password-masked control" even when a password box really had focus; every thread that calls UI Automation now initialises COM once before its first call, and a refused create names a safe reason code (`E_*`) instead of a bare exception type.
- **The desktop's watchdog now waits up to about three and a half minutes before calling the backend hung, and its "stop after 3 restarts" cap works again (2026-10-26).** It used to allow 45 seconds (3 failed checks, 15 seconds apart) and then restart the backend, and on 2026-10-26 that cut off a real answer: "tell me about the Galaxy" ran 37-38 seconds and was restarted mid-turn. Now 10 checks have to fail in a row, and one probe gets 5 seconds instead of 1.5 because a cold first probe costs about 3.0 seconds while `hello()` builds the voice sessions. The wait is not simply 10 x 15 s: a backend that is listening but silent makes each failed check wait out the whole probe, so the honest worst case is 10 x (15 s + 5 s) = 200 seconds - which is what the app's own settings screen and `docs/INSTALL.md` now say, instead of the "two and a half minutes" they said before. The restart window is 15 minutes, not 10, for the same reason: three slow hangs are noticed about 200 seconds apart, so a 10-minute window could never hold all three - the fourth attempt would arrive after the first had aged out, the cap would never trip, and the app would restart a wedged backend every three and a half minutes for ever without ever telling the owner. The 15-second check interval and the Windows service are unchanged. Two Rust tests pin the arithmetic and the window-versus-cycle relationship, so raising the patience again cannot silently break the cap.

The card shows the target separately from the agent's cleaned, explicitly-untrusted note, and voids with zero characters typed on any target/kind/control/password-mask change, an expired card, an empty or whitespace-only value, or an unproven caller. A typing failure is reported in the module's own fixed words, so the injected error cannot echo the value. `backend/test_secret_handoff.py`: 93 checks, 0 skipped, 0 failed, no GUI and no network. Nothing imports the module yet - the wiring into `jarvis_ui_control.py` / `jarvis_browser_control.py`, the host-only route and the HUD card are the next slice; `docs/DESIGN-SECRET-HANDOFF.md` records both halves and the honest limits that Python cannot wipe memory, that the snapshot is caller-supplied until the wiring measures it, and that the taint is in-memory only.

- **A Windows Hello prompt now closes when its card stops waiting, can never be given more than 180 s, and only an action with written words can prompt (2026-10-26).** The measured defect (`.dsh-scratch/WINDOWS-HELLO-2026-10-26/FINDINGS.md`) was that `POST /api/approve` read the card's remaining seconds BEFORE waiting for the one-prompt-at-a-time lock and never read them again, so a queued card kept its original 900 s even with 2 s left; and nothing watched the card while the dialog was up, so a card that was denied, withdrawn or expired under an open prompt left the dialog on screen for the rest of that number. Now the card is read again after the lock - a card that has run out by then is a 409 with no prompt - and the prompt gets `min(the seconds left now, 180 s)`. While the prompt is up a watcher polls the card four times a second and tells the child to close when it stops waiting, so the dialog goes within about a quarter of a second instead of being waited out; a queue that cannot be read is not treated as a card that went away. The watcher can only close its OWN prompt: the prompt is tagged when it is raised and the cancel is matched by that tag, because a queue read can outlive the watcher's two-second stop and the next card's prompt could otherwise be the one on screen. The wait for the lock is bounded too (`_PROMPT_WAIT_MAX` = 210 s, covering the worst legitimate hold of about 194 s: 180 of prompt, ten for the child's answer, two for the cancel and two for the watcher's stop) and refuses with 409 rather than waiting for ever. The long-lived `--hello` child no longer reads an empty stdin line as `{}` (which gave a cardless prompt the 900 s default) and clamps any timeout it is given to `_PROMPT_MAX` itself. Separately, an action with no written title in `jarvis_card_words` is refused with 403 `owner_check: "unlabelled"` before any prompt is shown - checked again on the post-lock live row, and stamped for that live action - because the title could only quote the action's name back at the owner; `unclassified_tool`, `send_email` and every other action with a phrase still prompt. A clean backend shutdown now cancels a live prompt (an `atexit` hook writes "cancel" to the child's stdin, and the child's own watcher calls the Windows cancel), instead of leaving the dialog to its own deadline. **Deploying it means copying BOTH `jarvis_owner_check.py` and `jarvis_card_words.py` into the live backend in one go, then restarting the backend:** `has_written_title` lives in the words module, and a one-module copy makes every risky approval on this PC refuse with 403 `unlabelled` before any prompt - silently, and it looks like the new guard working. `scripts/apply-patches.ps1` copies every shipped module in one run, so use it rather than a hand copy. Proven with fake verifiers and a fake child process only - no real dialog was raised: `backend/test_owner_check.py` 214 passed, 1 skipped; `backend/test_card_words.py` 168 passed. Honest limits: the prompt is still a detached child process and is still not parented to the app's window (the next fix, needing a real-prompt half-day test), so a hard kill of the backend - the desktop's job object, Task Manager - runs no Python, cannot run the cancel or the watcher, and the dialog then ends only at its deadline; a queue read that keeps failing also leaves the dialog to its deadline (nothing is approved either way); the desktop's own prompt (`op.get()` with no timeout) is unchanged; and the off-Windows test that used to call the real verifier on Windows now skips before that call, so the suite can no longer raise a real prompt on the owner's PC.

The backend now sends it once: a drawn picture says it in `words`, a failed draw says it in `error`, and `card` keeps only the machine-readable times and has no `words` key; the desktop panel's `words || card.words` guard is unchanged for a PC that has not taken this update. The desktop, the phone and the Rust boundary all show the owner the sentence exactly once, with no Kotlin change, and the new tests count the sentence in the whole answer (a phrase, not the word "words") on a drawn picture, a failed draw and a chat that did not come back - so a second copy in any field fails them.
- **A slow picture draw no longer looks like a failure on either app (2026-10-25).** One drawing on the PC can legitimately take up to **1,680 s** in the worst case - the five ceilings are `unload_lane(timeout=120)` 120 s, `DRAW_WAIT_S = 600` 600 s, the `POST /free` call's own `FREE_WAIT_S` 180 s, the `/system_stats` poll's second `FREE_WAIT_S` 180 s and `warm_lane(timeout=600)` 600 s, and 120 + 600 + 180 + 180 + 600 = 1,680 s (`backend/jarvis_picture_card.py:526` and `:564-565`; `backend/jarvis_pictures.py:197` and `:208`) - but both apps gave the one long silent request only 1,200 s, so a legitimate slow draw plus the chat warm-back could outlast the app and the owner saw a false failure. The desktop's `PICTURE_TIMEOUT` and the phone's `CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_S` are now **1,740 s**, a minute over that sum, and the "about 20 minutes" wording where it described the client wait is now "about 29 minutes". `FREE_WAIT_S` is counted twice because `free_models()` calls `/free` with `timeout=FREE_WAIT_S` and *then* sets `deadline = time.time() + FREE_WAIT_S` for its `/system_stats` poll: the earlier draft of this change counted that step once, said four ceilings and 1,500 s, and was 180 s short. The relationship is pinned on all four sides so the two cannot drift apart again: a Rust unit test asserts the budget exceeds the 1,680 s sum and names each of the five terms, a JVM test asserts the same for the phone, the desktop source-pin suite reads the budget back out of `brain.rs`, and `backend/test_pictures.py` reads the PC's own defaults plus `free_models`' source (to prove the second wait is really there), asserts their sum is 1,680 s, and reads both clients' source to prove each budget is above it. No backend production code changed - the PC's own timeouts were correct and only the clients were too eager. The phone change is CI-verified only: there is no Android build, emulator or phone here.
- **The phone's microphone works again, and Home is one shared More menu lighter (2026-10-25, Android only).** A tap on the talk button now starts a recording that outlives the tap - a second tap sends, a sustained hold still sends on release, sliding away still cancels - because the gesture was keyed on the very capture state it changed, so every press began and instantly cancelled itself; Full screen's microphone is drawn only when the PC offers push-to-talk. Home's redundant "Open the Brain →" caption is gone; Find moved from the status line into Help (hidden on an unpaired phone, because Find is not reachable there); and the chat bar keeps only the typing box, Send and the microphone: Photo, Think, Coach this, the temporary-chat toggle, Earlier chats, Notifications, Quick note and Jarvis Presets now live in one More menu, shared by the chat bar and the full-screen face bar, each row shown only when this PC offers it. Android-only on purpose - the desktop has no equivalent of this phone Home screen - and proved by source pins plus a pure JVM test, not by a run: this container has no local Gradle, so CI's frontend job is the compiler.
- **You can now make a personality by talking to Jarvis (2026-10-25).** Settings -> "How Jarvis talks" already let you type a name, one line and one example; what was missing was the conversation. Say **"make me a personality like a grumpy but caring mechanic"** (typed or spoken, desktop or phone) and the PC answers in chat: it asks the LOCAL model once to draft a name, how it should sound, one example exchange and which of the nine built-in presets it starts from, then shows the whole draft and says `"save it"` keeps it. If you did not say what it should be like, Jarvis asks for one line and treats your next message in that conversation as the description (remembered in memory only - nothing is written to disk, and a new conversation never inherits it). Refine it in your own words - "make it shorter", "call it Old Timer", "base it on the butler" - and say `"save it"`; the row is saved through the SAME `jarvis_manner.save_user_personality()` path the Settings form uses (name 60, line 240, each example half 240, 20 saved at most), so `"switch to <name>"` finds it straight away. `"forget it"` drops a draft; a temporary chat is refused because it remembers nothing. Wording only: no new route, no approval card, no permission change, and the model is only ever the local one - asked on the same lane the chat uses, for the chat's OWN model name (the HUD's own resolver, never a copied base name like qwen3.5:9b), at the chat's own context size, so drafting neither loads a different model nor reloads it at a smaller one - the draft is fields the PC validates, never a finished prompt, so a personality cannot change what Jarvis may do. Two stale defects found on the way are fixed: the quick answer and the settings catalogue both said "the eight personalities" and then listed nine. New `backend/jarvis_personality_creator.py` (shipped whole, called from `jarvis_quick.py`'s `/api/chat` fast path), `backend/test_personality_creator.py` (132 checks), docs in `docs/JARVIS-API.md` section 27.7. Honest limits: no real WebView2 or phone window was driven - the checks run the real chat fast path with the model stubbed - and the Settings "Draft it for me" button is the next slice, not this one.

- **A changed MCP `tools/list` asks the owner again (2026-10-25).** Next to the existing start fingerprint, `jarvis_mcp.py` now remembers a 32-byte SHA-256 of each server's normalized `tools/list` result in `mcp-approved.json`, and a later list whose digest differs raises the same start card again (the server is stopped, the old yes is forgotten, and nothing new is written without a person's yes). Only the 64-character hex digest is stored - never the tools/list text, a tool name, a description or a schema - and tools are put in name order first, so a server that reorders the same list does not ask. A record with no digest or a malformed one is treated as unconfirmed and asks (fails safe), so an approval written before this check asks once and then records its digest. `backend/test_mcp_digest.py` proves the stored shape, the no-card unchanged path, the re-ask and refused-change path, and the missing/malformed digest fallback against the real fake server.

Way A (the recommended one) is the swap; way C never touches the chat; way B is recorded but not wired and says so. `DRAW_WAIT_S = 600` covers the measured 274.4 s draw plus a cold load, and `FREE_WAIT_S = 180` bounds the release wait. **The measured `/free` answer is HTTP 200 with a 0-byte body** - the old client parsed that empty body as JSON, failed in 0.0 s, and warmed the chat back while ~10.9 GB was still being released; the first real draw (2026-10-24) came back 1.36 GB spilled. The wait now accepts the empty answer (`allow_empty=True` on that one call) and polls the card. **Measured on this PC, four real Chroma1-HD draws through this code** (RTX 2060, ComfyUI 0.39.0, 1152x1152 at 26 steps): the 2026-10-24 red panda (2,008,307 bytes, draw 383.6 s, wall 420.8 s, the 1.36 GB spill above); a 2026-10-25 lighthouse (1,409,863 bytes, draw 379.0 s) which found the empty-answer cause; a 2026-10-25 cabin with the wait fixed (2,087,566 bytes, draw 381.0 s, `models_freed: true`, chat back WHOLE - `size_vram == size`, spill 0 - 23.6 s after stepping aside); and the 2026-10-25 phone-path ship where both requests carried `X-Jarvis-Client: phone` (1,721,489 bytes, draw 382.0 s, wall 500.1 s, `models_freed: true`, chat back whole, spill 0). `docs/JARVIS-API.md` §129.4b/§129.8 records the contract and the numbers, `docs/DECISIONS.md` carries the phone decision, and `backend/test_pictures.py` (245 checks) proves the 409, the order (aside before draw, free and warm-back after), the empty-`/free` answer, the release wait, the error-path warm-back, way B's sentence, the phone's first 409 and confirmed success, the one-draw-at-a-time sentence, and the still-PC-only settings route, with the card module stood in for.

- **The phone's Galaxy gets a read-only "at a glance" band (2026-10-24).** Offered three choices, the owner picked the light one: above the existing People and things list, the phone now shows how many names and facts it holds and the eight names that share facts with the most others, as plain labels that never announce as buttons. - **The phone finishes a backup on the PC with one tap (2026-10-24).** The owner upgraded his morning decision from "let the PC finish a backup the phone started" to one tap from the phone: after the code is shown and he ticks "I have written this code down somewhere safe", the phone's finish button makes the PC write the file - no step on the PC. The one-time code the phone holds IS the authorisation for the phone that minted the run; the write still happens on the PC's disk, by the PC's own backend. `POST /api/backup/commit` therefore no longer refuses a caller for not being the PC: a live run minted by `prepare`, its exact code and the 15-minute TTL are what authorise it, and a wrong or missing code (400) or a dead run (409) still writes nothing. This deliberately relaxes the 2026-10-13 rule "a phone may ask, only the PC may write"; the residual risk - the "I saved it" tick is a phone-side promise, so a modified or misused phone could make the PC write a backup whose code nobody kept and push the oldest of the five kept out - is recorded in `docs/DECISIONS.md` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8, with the owner's acceptance. The PC's typed-code block in Settings, Backups stays as the fallback for a run the phone left waiting, on the same route: no new route, and no approval card. The run is claimed under the module's lock before the write, so two presses write ONE file, and the phone's screen now says "Nothing has been written yet" before the press and "Your PC wrote the backup" only after the PC reports a file (the dialog used to claim it the moment it opened). **Hardened the same day on Gemini's ruling:** the finish is BOUND to the phone that minted the run or to the PC - `prepare` records the asking device's existing identity (`handler._jarvis_device`; no new header or token) and another paired device holding the same code is refused 403, writes nothing and does not spend the run, while a run minted with no recorded identity falls back to the code (said plainly in the code and the API doc); and a commit that cannot write now always records `last_attempt.ok: false` - including the 409 when the folder has gone, which used to record nothing - so a failed run is never shown as the previous run's success, while a truncated `.jbak` is never counted as a valid backup. The phone's screen, live run and TalkBack wording are a field-test row, not a pass.

Its prompt asks for plain-English medical and billing words, facts kept apart from guesses, three questions for the care team, and never a diagnosis or advice to stop a medicine. The crisis block still replaces all persona text for all nine. Unproven: the wording on a real device, the blended voice (Hear Sample still plays the base voice), and TalkBack.
- **A pairing card can no longer outlive its session, and a retried approval key keeps the waiter that stores it (2026-10-24, audit B-1/B-2).** Cancelling a pairing, starting a new one or letting the 600 seconds run out now takes the waiting `pair_device` card off `/api/pending` on both apps, so pressing Approve on it later is refused instead of reporting success while minting no key; the approval-key close-out withdraws the gate's real card id, and a retry of the same phone key joins the one card already waiting, so the owner's single Windows Hello yes still stores the key.

While a code is shown, the Jarvis windows stay out of any screen share or recorder.
- **The medical record gets its own encrypted file, a 30-minute local-only latch, a place in your backups and a local MedGemma second reader - and says out loud what it cannot do (2026-10-24).** `backend/jarvis_medical_advocate.py` (shipped whole, no route, no screen) holds four record kinds in `~/.openjarvis/medical/health.db`, its own folder and file rather than another name in `memory.db`; every read and write sets `jarvis_gate.latch_taint(why="health_data")` *before* opening anything and fails closed with `MedicalStoreUnavailable` if it cannot, so a medical read pins the chat to local models for the gate's 30 minutes and no longer. The owner answered the open question the same day - "I wanted it encrypted as well and part of that file" - so every record field (label, dates, value, unit, source, note) is now sealed as one JSON payload per row with AES-256-GCM under a fresh nonce, with the kind and a random row label as associated data, and the 32-byte key lives in Windows Credential Manager under its own entry, `Jarvis Backend/medical key`, made on first use through the same `jarvis_chat_log.CredentialKey` helper chat history and the review decks use; a missing, short, broken or replaced key refuses in plain words before anything is read or written, a file from the earlier unencrypted version is refused rather than read or overwritten, and the tests write a distinctive secret then scan the raw database bytes (and any journal beside it) to prove no record word reaches the disk in plain text. What still sits in plain sight is stated: the file's name and folder, its row numbers, a random per-row label, when each row was made, and the audit rows' action, kind and counts - never a record's words. `health.db` is in `jarvis_backup.SOURCE_DBS` (not `NOT_BACKED_UP`) and travels under `db/medical/health.db`, its own folder, with its key inside the encrypted archive, so a restore on a new PC whose Credential Manager is empty opens the record; a second round-trip proves the harder case - the new PC had already minted its own medical key, the archive's key replaces it and the record still opens, with a stale -wal beside the restored file removed - and the backup suite's pinned counts moved from 17 + 8 to 18 + 7. `erase_all()` deletes only that file's rows (secure delete, a truncated write-ahead log, then a vacuum) and does NOT need the key (a lost or replaced key must never stop the owner wiping the record), a test proves a neighbouring `memory.db` is byte-for-byte untouched, a sealed payload moved between rows is refused rather than decoded, and the store is still NOT covered by a non-expiring latch. The lane client is the one HTTP path already in `jarvis_second_card` (a new `model=`/`keep_alive=` argument, default request byte-identical), probes `127.0.0.1:11435` in 0.20 s, refuses any other host, strips MedGemma's leaked `<unused94> ... <unused95>` thinking markers, and on any failure returns a calm fallback naming the main local model (:11436); its request timeout is 120 s, not the 25 s it first shipped with, because a measured answer took 28.35 s and 25 s cut it off. `validate_bundle()` checks a named subset of FHIR R4 (32 checks: Bundle, required elements and required-bound status values, id/instant shapes, reference syntax and in-bundle resolution, Observation value/unit/range/flag/component contradictions, duplicate rows and a magnitude heuristic, and code SHAPE) plus `summarise()`; it reports `no_errors_found` / `errors_found` / `not_checked` - never "valid" - always lists code meanings under `unverified`, and an optional local model is a second reader with `authority: "none"` whose junky, advice-giving or invented-code answers are dropped and can never change the structural report. `docs/MEDICAL-STORE.md` is the beginner's page (the lane's one-line start command, the honest limits, and the one decision still open); 95 hermetic medical tests and the backup suite's real new-PC round-trip hold all of it, and no federal API, outbound de-identifier, backup toggle, biometric lock screen or phone/desktop surface was built.
- **The phone's persistent Live stream now has its PC half: the transport and one whole turn, switched OFF (2026-10-24, Slice G/G2+G2b of `docs/DESIGN-PHONE-LIVE-STREAM.md`).** The frozen route and switch were already there; this adds the smallest RFC 6455 WebSocket server the design needs (no new dependency - the backend is standard-library only and the lock file cannot be regenerated), with token and origin checked BEFORE the upgrade, 64 ms binary audio frames, a random epoch and a monotonic sequence that refuse replays, and one whole turn: the ring's WAV through the SAME one-shot Live check, the PC's own `/api/chat` over loopback with the message marked live, then `say()`'s PCM back as the design's frames. The speech hand-off is whole-WAV for now (first-fragment streaming is a later phase). **The switch ships OFF and nothing enables it**; the phone half and every real measurement are still to come, so latency, battery and recovery are NOT-MEASURED.
- **The tools Jarvis is built with move to their current releases (2026-10-24).** The GitHub Actions that build and test the project move to their newest major versions (checkout 7, setup-python 7, setup-node 7, setup-java 6, upload-artifact 7, download-artifact 8), and the desktop app's Tauri stack moves to 2.12.5 with its build helper 2.7.4. Nothing you can see changes; this only keeps the build tools current. The upload/download changes are first exercised by the next full release build, not by this pull request's own checks.
- **A claim can no longer read as built when its test skipped the thing (2026-10-24, tools).** `tools/check_claims.py` proved a `test:` row from the exit code alone, and `backend/test_data_backup.py` exits 0 after printing a skip when the guard it would test is absent - so removing the NordLocker guard left claim F11 printed as built/holds. The checker now reads the skip lines a suite prints and withholds proof from any row naming a suite that skipped a check about the code rather than this machine. The environment skips the shipped suites really print (the Windows ACL fixture, a missing `cryptography` package, a module not importable here) stay proven, so the register is still green: 146 claims, 131 built. Its honest limit: a substantive skip in a suite withholds proof from every row naming that suite, and a new environmental skip with a new wording makes its row red until its reason is added to the allow-list - loud, never silent.
- **Past approvals show when they were decided, on both apps (2026-10-24).** The live `/api/pending` history rows carry `created`/`decided` - measured at 13:52 PT as exactly `id,action,tier,state,created,decided,decided_by`, a decided row's `decided` being a number like `1792875072.03678` - while the desktop (`brain.js` `activityWhen`) and the phone (`GateHistory.kt`) both read `decided_at`, which no row carried: a decided card showed the raise time as its decision time, or no time at all. Both readers now take `decided_at` first and fall back to `decided` (and `created_at`, then `created`, for the raise time), which is the whole fix against the measured row - no backend or patch change was needed or made, because the published base is never copied over the live install and both apps are the only readers of those names. `jarvis-desktop/tests/activity-when.mjs` lifts the real reader and pins an old-shape row and a row carrying both names; `PastApprovalsTest.kt` does the same for the Kotlin reader.
- **A slow approval click no longer gives up before the PC does (2026-10-24, desktop).** When a card does not say how long is left, the desktop waited 180 seconds for the answer, but the PC's own Windows Hello prompt is bounded at 900 seconds for the four cards that never expire (pairing a device, a phone's approval key, restoring a backup) - so a slow click was abandoned around 185 seconds while the PC was still waiting. The desktop now waits the PC's own bound plus the few seconds for the answer to come back (905 seconds), and its ceiling matches. Nothing is approved sooner or automatically; a denial is still a denial.
- **Ten small fixes from the phone audit's second pass (2026-10-24).** None changes a word the owner reads of his own, and none touches a setting: a Resume/Retry/Cancel asked for on a stale link is now refused with the existing link sentence instead of being sent; a briefing notification writes its restart point before it rings, so a crash inside two seconds can no longer replay it; the swipe on an approval card now feels the same gates its buttons show, so a heavy card's swipe approves after its two-second gate instead of silently springing back, and a stale-link swipe no longer asks for a fingerprint; the sandbox switch keeps reading while a card waits, so a denied or timed-out card stops reading as "waiting"; "Brief me now" keeps the setups and the senders switch the plate had already read instead of claiming no briefing exists; with the memory lists hidden, Goals no longer shows or speaks the PC's lock/reached/follows lines; a failed gallery read shows the PC's own sentence instead of "run apply-patches.ps1"; a share no longer doubles on a rotation and a sent photo does not come back; the phone's screen-capture guard now outlasts the screen-change fade instead of clearing with it; a limits or attention change and a model switch/install now wait as long as the approval card they raise (up to 20 minutes) instead of reporting "took too long" after 15 seconds; and a face whose shader will not compile costs that face, not the app - the default face is drawn instead of crashing at every launch, and one per-frame brush that was rebuilt 60 times a second is now built once. Runtime behaviour stays NOT-TESTABLE here (no emulator): every desk test is a JUnit or source pin, never a phone pass.
- **The phone stops blaming the pairing key for PC-only cards, and stops a recording it was told to cancel (2026-10-24).** Four small fixes from tonight's full audit, plus one data-rule fix: a card that can only be approved on the PC now says so in its own words instead of "your pairing key was refused" and a trip to the pairing screen, and all eight PC-only actions are known in one place; closing "Add a voice" (or picking a file) now stops a recording already running, instead of letting the take reappear in the next attempt; "Train my voice" and "hey Jarvis" refuse to open a second microphone beside Jarvis Live, so Live's own spoken answer can no longer land in the voice-print clip; a dead microphone now stops Live with the reason instead of spinning at full CPU while holding it open; and Send waits for a photo that is still being prepared, so the photo cannot ride the next question. No route, no new read, no write. Runtime behaviour is NOT-TESTABLE here (no emulator) and stays a field-test row, never a pass.
- **"People and things" past dates no longer mix, and the phone's Galaxy counts each fact once (2026-10-24).** Two bugs from tonight's full audit, both fixed in the phone's read-only code: tapping a different "as of" date now drops the previous date's facts immediately, so the heading and the list always describe the same day - even while the new read is running, and after a read that fails; and the Galaxy band's "N facts" line now counts each saved fact once instead of once per name, which is what its own promise said. No new read, no write, and nothing changes on screen when one fact names two people. Runtime look and TalkBack order remain a field-test row, not a pass.
- **A changelog entry is now one small file per pull request, rolled into the big list when it is safe (2026-10-23).** Every pull request used to append its entry at the top of `CHANGELOG.md` - one shared line, so two pull requests always conflicted and every merge to `main` dirtied the rest; a conflicted pull request gets no CI, and re-clearing one costs a fresh ~71-minute `frontend` run (one night lost six). Now a pull request writes ONE bullet file under `changelog.d/` (`YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`) and never touches `CHANGELOG.md`; on a quiet `main`, `py -3 tools/roll_changelog.py` inserts the bullets newest first under "Not in a numbered version yet" and removes the fragment files, in ONE pull request with nothing else in it. `--check` validates a fragment's name and shape on every PR and never demands that it has already been rolled (that would fail the very pull requests the fragments exist for); `--dry-run` shows the insertion and writes nothing. The roll is deliberate, never automatic, and idempotent. Proven by `backend/test_roll_changelog.py` (20 checks: the good shape, every bad shape named one by one, newest-first insertion, existing entries kept, fragments removed only after the text is read back, a second roll is a no-op, dry-run writes nothing, the real exit codes).
- **Four approval cards now wait for you instead of expiring; every other card keeps its 15 minutes (2026-10-23, rescue #4 narrowed to the owner's ruling Q1).** `rescue/card-expiry-never-expires` (2026-10-13) made **23** gate actions' cards never expire; the owner's ruling refused that scope, so `backend/no-expiry-cards.patch` exempts only the three interactive ceremonies that need you at the PC: **pairing a device** (`pair_device`, `unretire_shared_key`), **registering a phone's approval key** (`register_approval_key`) and **restoring a backup** (`restore_backup`). Every other card - including "forget a time frame" and every switch that loosens a rule (web search, reading tools, notifications, learning, limits, the voice bar) - keeps `#378`'s 15-minute window. There is **no way to ask for no deadline**: the decision is `timeout_for(action)` keyed on the gate's OWN action ids, there is no flow argument, and `None`, `0`, a negative number, a malformed name or an unknown flow name all get the ordinary 900 seconds. `pending()` leaves `expires_in` OFF for those four (never `0`, which both apps read as "expired now"), the start-up sweep no longer ages them out, and a new `jarvis_gate.withdraw()` takes a cancelled or replaced pairing/approval-key card off the list; `jarvis_owner_check.py` asks the gate before treating an absent field as "the shipped timeout", so Windows Hello no longer answers 409 GONE for a card the gate is still waiting on. **Waiting is still not approving:** nothing runs until a person answers, a denial is still a denial, and the re-read after the Windows Hello prompt still refuses a card that is no longer the live one. The two shipped-module halves are carried to `jarvis-backend/` byte-for-byte. **Honest limits:** a restore card whose waiting thread died (an app restart) stays pending until denied or re-raised - the one case where a card is answerable but nothing is listening; that is the cost of "no clock" and it is said in `backend/README.md`. Tests: `backend/test_gate_no_expiry.py` (10 tests, 170 checks: the four required proofs plus approval/denial/withdrawal, the sweep, `expires_in`, and the Windows Hello half); `backend/test_gate_no_expiry.py` applies the patch to the published base with `git apply` and imports the result. Docs: `docs/JARVIS-API.md` (`expires_in`), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §2, `backend/README.md`.
- **DeepSeek's own Search API is a sixth web-search provider, opt-in and key-only, and SearXNG is still the default (2026-10-23).** Jarvis already offered five searches (SearXNG, DuckDuckGo, Exa, Tavily, Brave); this adds `deepseek`, off until the owner chooses it in **Settings, Web search** on the PC (or says "use DeepSeek for web search"). It calls `POST https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/search` with `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and only `{"query", "count": 5, "need_content": false}` - the guide's optional conversation question and address field are deliberately never sent - and turns the answer's `summary` (written for a model) into the 300-character snippet, with `snippet` as the fallback; a null `date` is harmless and other fields are unused. Its **key lives in Windows Credential Manager** as `Jarvis Backend/DeepSeek Search key`, written on the PC only by the desktop's Settings or `py -3 jarvis_search.py key deepseek`, never over HTTP, never logged, sent only to `api.deepseek.com`. The **owner's costs and limits**, from DeepSeek's own guide: **$0.75 per 1,000 successful searches** (failed searches and searches that find nothing are not billed), a **1 to 128 character** query (a longer search is refused in `plan()` before any card or socket), and **100 searches a second** per account. A 401 says the key is wrong or cancelled, 402 says the account is out of balance and where to add credit, 429 says too many searches, and 408/5xx say DeepSeek had a problem and to try again; **no retry is sent automatically**, the same as the other five. Both apps list it last in the PC's order and both carry the same words; the phone still has **no key box**. Setup, "What Jarvis can reach", "tell me when a search shows something new", "which search should I use?" and the feature guide all name it.
